The coefficients of the canonical form are then **exactly the eigenvalues of $A$**, and the transformation is a rotation or reflection (length preserving), which is ideal for geometric questions; the price is solving a characteristic equation.

The **method of completing the square (Lagrange)**: eliminate one variable at a time by forming a perfect square, then treat the remaining variables. If every square coefficient is zero (say $f=2x_1x_2$), first create a square with the invertible substitution $x_1=y_1+y_2$, $x_2=y_1-y_2$. The essential point is that every substitution be invertible: as long as no division by zero occurs and the substitutions are triangular or mutually inverse, the composite change is invertible and the rank is preserved. Canonical forms are not unique, but by the law of inertia the numbers of positive and negative squares (the inertia indices) are uniquely determined.
derivation: 设 $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=\sum_{1\le i\le j\le n}c_{ij}x_ix_j$。令 $a_{ii}=c_{ii}$，并对 $i<j$ 令 $a_{ij}=a_{ji}=\frac12c_{ij}$，则 $f=x^{T}Ax$ 且 $A^{T}=A$。反过来，从任意矩阵 $B$ 出发，$x^{T}Bx$ 是标量，故 $x^{T}Bx=(x^{T}Bx)^{T}=x^{T}B^{T}x$，于是 $x^{T}Bx=x^{T}\frac{B+B^{T}}2x$；所以总可取对称矩阵，且它由 $a_{ij}=\frac12\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}$ 唯一确定。在要求 $A$ 对称的前提下，交叉项系数必须平分，不能整块放在 $a_{ij}$。

作可逆线性变换 $x=Py$（$P$ 可逆），则 $$f=x^{T}Ax=(Py)^{T}A(Py)=y^{T}(P^{T}AP)y.$$ 新矩阵 $P^{T}AP$ 仍对称，因为 $(P^{T}AP)^{T}=P^{T}A^{T}P=P^{T}AP$。又 $\operatorname{rank}(P^{T}AP)=\operatorname{rank}(A)$：左乘或右乘可逆矩阵都不改变秩。故合同变换保持二次型的秩，但一般改变特征值（保持特征值的是相似变换）。例如 $A=\operatorname{diag}(1,4)$、$P=\operatorname{diag}(1,\frac12)$ 时，$P^{T}AP=\operatorname{diag}(1,1)$。

正交变换法：$A$ 实对称，由谱定理存在正交矩阵 $Q$（$Q^{T}Q=E$）使 $$Q^{T}AQ=\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n).$$ 令 $x=Qy$，则 $f=y^{T}\Lambda y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_iy_i^2$。这里 $Q^{-1}=Q^{T}$，所以合同与相似同时发生；标准形的系数恰为特征值，且 $\|x\|=\|Qy\|=\|y\|$，变换只是旋转或反射。

配方法：若某个 $a_{ii}
e0$，把含 $x_i$ 的项写成 $$ egin{aligned}&a_{ii}\left(x_i+\sum_{j
e i} rac{a_{ij}}{a_{ii}}x_jight)^2\&\quad+	ext{(不含 }x_i	ext{ 的二次型)}.\end{aligned}$$ 所用替换 $y_i=x_i+\sum_{j
e i} rac{a_{ij}}{a_{ii}}x_j$、$y_j=x_j\ (j
e i)$ 的矩阵对角元全为 $1$、非对角元只出现在第 $i$ 行，行列式为 $1$，故可逆。对剩余变量重复此过程；若某一步所有平方项系数为零而余项非零，则转入第 5 步的替换。最终得 $f=\sum d_iy_i^2$，非零 $d_i$ 的个数等于二次型的秩。

若所有 $a_{ii}=0$ 但 $f
ot\equiv0$，则存在 $a_{ij}
e0$（$i
e j$）。作可逆替换 $x_i=y_i+y_j$、$x_j=y_i-y_j$，其余 $x_k=y_k$；其矩阵行列式为 $-2
e0$。于是 $$2a_{ij}x_ix_j=2a_{ij}(y_i^2-y_j^2),$$ 产生了非零平方项，再回到上一步配方。例如 $f=2x_1x_2$ 经此替换化为 $2y_1^2-2y_2^2$。

两条路径给出的标准形可以不同：正交变换给 $\sum\lambda_iy_i^2$，配方法给 $\sum d_iz_i^2$，系数一般不相等。但两者由可逆变换互相联系，故秩相同；由惯性定理，正、负平方项的个数 $(p,q)$ 也相同，并且都能进一步化为规范形 $$z_1^2+\cdots+z_p^2-z_{p+1}^2-\cdots-z_r^2,\qquad r=p+q=\operatorname{rank}(A).$$ 所以标准形不唯一，正、负惯性指数唯一；合同保持秩与惯性指数，但不保持特征值。
derivationEn: Let $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=\sum_{1\le i\le j\le n}c_{ij}x_ix_j$. Set $a_{ii}=c_{ii}$ and, for $i<j$, $a_{ij}=a_{ji}=\frac12c_{ij}$; then $f=x^{T}Ax$ with $A^{T}=A$. Conversely, starting from any matrix $B$, the scalar $x^{T}Bx$ equals its transpose $x^{T}B^{T}x$, so $x^{T}Bx=x^{T}\frac{B+B^{T}}2x$; hence a symmetric matrix may always be used, and it is uniquely determined by $a_{ij}=\frac12\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}$. Under the requirement that $A$ be symmetric, a cross-term coefficient must be split equally, not assigned entirely to $a_{ij}$.

For an invertible linear change $x=Py$, $$f=x^{T}Ax=(Py)^{T}A(Py)=y^{T}(P^{T}AP)y.$$ The new matrix $P^{T}AP$ is still symmetric, since $(P^{T}AP)^{T}=P^{T}A^{T}P=P^{T}AP$. Also $\operatorname{rank}(P^{T}AP)=\operatorname{rank}(A)$, because multiplication by an invertible matrix on either side preserves rank. Thus congruence preserves the rank of the form but generally changes eigenvalues (similarity, not congruence, preserves them): for $A=\operatorname{diag}(1,4)$ and $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,\frac12)$, $P^{T}AP=\operatorname{diag}(1,1)$.

Orthogonal method: since $A$ is real symmetric, the spectral theorem gives an orthogonal $Q$ ($Q^{T}Q=E$) with $$Q^{T}AQ=\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n).$$ Setting $x=Qy$ yields $f=y^{T}\Lambda y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_iy_i^2$. Here $Q^{-1}=Q^{T}$, so congruence and similarity occur simultaneously; the coefficients are exactly the eigenvalues, and $\|x\|=\|Qy\|=\|y\|$, so the change is only a rotation or reflection.

Completing the square: if some $a_{ii}
e0$, group all terms containing $x_i$ as $$ egin{aligned}&a_{ii}\left(x_i+\sum_{j
e i} rac{a_{ij}}{a_{ii}}x_jight)^2\&\quad+	ext{(a quadratic form not containing }x_i	ext{)}.\end{aligned}$$ The substitution $y_i=x_i+\sum_{j
e i} rac{a_{ij}}{a_{ii}}x_j$, $y_j=x_j$ $(j
e i)$ has all diagonal entries equal to $1$, with off-diagonal entries only in row $i$; its determinant is $1$, so it is invertible. Repeat on the remaining variables; if at some stage all square coefficients vanish while the remaining form is nonzero, use the substitution of Step 5. The result is $f=\sum d_iy_i^2$, and the number of nonzero $d_i$ equals the rank.

If all $a_{ii}=0$ but $f
ot\equiv0$, then some $a_{ij}
e0$ with $i
e j$. Use the invertible substitution $x_i=y_i+y_j$, $x_j=y_i-y_j$, and $x_k=y_k$ for $k
e i,j$; its matrix has determinant $-2
e0$. Then $$2a_{ij}x_ix_j=2a_{ij}(y_i^2-y_j^2),$$ which creates nonzero square terms, and we return to the previous step. For example, $f=2x_1x_2$ becomes $2y_1^2-2y_2^2$ under this substitution.

The two routes may produce different canonical forms: the orthogonal method gives $\sum\lambda_iy_i^2$, while completing the square gives $\sum d_iz_i^2$, and the coefficients generally differ. Since the two are related by invertible changes, the rank is the same; by the law of inertia the numbers $(p,q)$ of positive and negative squares are also the same, and both reduce further to the normal form $$z_1^2+\cdots+z_p^2-z_{p+1}^2-\cdots-z_r^2,\qquad r=p+q=\operatorname{rank}(A).$$ Thus a canonical form is not unique, but the inertia indices are; congruence preserves rank and inertia, not eigenvalues.

formulas.note: 二次型的两种写法；写成矩阵形式时必须把 A 取成对称矩阵，否则矩阵与二次型不能一一对应。
formulas.noteEn: The two ways to write a quadratic form; the matrix A must be taken symmetric, otherwise forms and matrices do not correspond one-to-one.

formulas.note: cᵢⱼ 表示 f 中 xᵢxⱼ 的系数：交叉项系数平分给 aᵢⱼ 与 aⱼᵢ（各一半），平方项系数直接放对角线——这一步最容易写错。
formulas.noteEn: Here cᵢⱼ is the coefficient of xᵢxⱼ in f: a cross-term coefficient is split equally between aᵢⱼ and aⱼᵢ, while a square-term coefficient goes straight to the diagonal — the most error-prone step.

formulas.note: 可逆线性变换下二次型的矩阵按合同 CᵀAC 变化；C 可逆时二次型的秩不变。
formulas.noteEn: Under an invertible linear change the matrix of the form transforms by the congruence CᵀAC; invertible C preserves the rank of the form.

formulas.note: 正交变换法：令 x=Qy，标准形的系数就是 A 的特征值，且变换保持长度（只是旋转或反射）。
formulas.noteEn: The orthogonal method: with x=Qy the coefficients of the canonical form are the eigenvalues of A, and the transformation preserves length (it is a rotation or reflection).

formulas.note: 配方法示意：先按 x₁ 配成完全平方，剩下的 x₂² 已是平方项；所用替换呈三角形式，因此可逆。
formulas.noteEn: A sample completion of the square: complete the square in x₁ first, and the leftover x₂² is already a square; the substitution is triangular, hence invertible.

properties: 二次型与实对称矩阵一一对应：平方项系数进对角线，交叉项系数平分给对称的两个位置。
标准形只含平方项，一般不唯一；但正、负平方项的个数（正、负惯性指数）由惯性定理唯一确定。
对二次型作可逆线性变换就是作合同变换 CᵀAC：它保持秩、保持正负惯性指数，但不保持特征值。
正交变换法得到的标准形系数恰为特征值，变换保长度与内积；配方法无需解特征方程，但同样必须保证变换可逆。
合同（CᵀAC，C 可逆）与相似（P⁻¹AP）是两种不同的等价关系：相似保持特征值，合同保持正负惯性指数。
propertiesEn: Quadratic forms correspond one-to-one with real symmetric matrices: square coefficients go on the diagonal and cross coefficients are split equally between symmetric positions.
A canonical form contains only squares and is generally not unique, but the numbers of positive and negative squares (the inertia indices) are unique by the law of inertia.
An invertible linear change of variables for a form is a congruence CᵀAC: it preserves the rank and the inertia indices, but not the eigenvalues.

The orthogonal method produces coefficients equal to the eigenvalues and preserves lengths and inner products; completing the square avoids the characteristic equation but must also use invertible transformations.
Congruence (CᵀAC with invertible C) and similarity (P⁻¹AP) are different equivalence relations: similarity preserves eigenvalues, congruence preserves the inertia indices.

positive-definite-inertia.definition:
设 $f(x)=x^{T}Ax$（$A$ 对称）。若对一切 $x\neq 0$ 都有 $f(x)>0$，就称 $f$ 是**正定二次型**，$A$ 是**正定矩阵**，记作 $A>0$。这个定义要求「处处为正」，比「有最小值」强得多；它等价于 $A$ 的特征值全为正，也等价于 $A$ 与单位矩阵 $E$ 合同。

只用特征值判定往往要解高次方程，于是有纯代数的**顺序主子式判别法**：$A$ 正定当且仅当 $A$ 的各阶顺序主子式全大于零：$$D_1=a_{11}>0,\quad D_2=\begin{vmatrix}a_{11}&a_{12}\\a_{21}&a_{22}\end{vmatrix}>0,\quad\dots,\quad D_n=|A|>0.$$ 注意两个细节：必须是**顺序**主子式（左上角的 $k$ 阶子式），而且不等式是严格大于 0 而不是「非负」；前者漏掉会误判一部分矩阵，后者会把半正定混进来。

**惯性定理**：不论用什么可逆线性变换把二次型化成标准形，标准形里正平方项的个数 $p$ 与负平方项的个数 $q$ 都是唯一确定的，分别称为**正惯性指数**与**负惯性指数**；再作一次缩放 $y_i\mapsto y_i/\sqrt{|d_i|}$ 就得到**规范形** $z_1^2+\cdots+z_p^2-z_{p+1}^2-\cdots-z_r^2$，其中 $r=p+q=\operatorname{rank}(A)$。也就是说，同一个二次型的所有标准形共享同一个「正负结构」：系数可以变，正负号的个数不能变。

由此得到完整分类：正定（特征值全 >0，$p=n$）；负定（特征值全 <0，$q=n$，等价于奇数阶顺序主子式 <0 且偶数阶顺序主子式 >0）；半正定（特征值全 ≥0，当 $|A|=0$ 时只是半正定而非正定）；不定（正、负特征值都有）。可逆线性变换（合同变换）既保持正定性、也保持惯性指数，这正是配方法与正交变换法结论一致的原因。正定矩阵在优化（二阶充分条件要求 Hessian 正定）、最小二乘、数值分析（对称正定方程组）中都是核心对象。
positive-definite-inertia.definitionEn:
Let $f(x)=x^{T}Ax$ with $A$ symmetric. If $f(x)>0$ for every $x\neq 0$, the form is **positive definite** and $A$ is a **positive definite matrix**, written $A>0$. This demands positivity everywhere, much stronger than merely having a minimum; it is equivalent to all eigenvalues of $A$ being positive, and to $A$ being congruent to the identity matrix $E$.

Testing eigenvalues may require solving a high-degree equation, so there is a purely algebraic criterion using **leading principal minors**: $A$ is positive definite exactly when all its leading principal minors are positive: $$D_1=a_{11}>0,\quad D_2=\begin{vmatrix}a_{11}&a_{12}\\a_{21}&a_{22}\end{vmatrix}>0,\quad\dots,\quad D_n=|A|>0.$$ Two details matter: the minors must be the **leading** ones (top-left $k\times k$), and the inequalities are strict, not '≥'; missing the first point misjudges some matrices, while using '≥' mixes in semidefinite forms.

The **law of inertia**: no matter which invertible linear change turns the form into a canonical form, the number $p$ of positive squares and the number $q$ of negative squares are uniquely determined; they are the **positive and negative inertia indices**. One further rescaling $y_i\mapsto y_i/\sqrt{|d_i|}$ produces the **normal form** $z_1^2+\cdots+z_p^2-z_{p+1}^2-\cdots-z_r^2$, where $r=p+q=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. In other words all canonical forms of one quadratic form share the same sign structure: coefficients may change, but the numbers of plus and minus signs may not.

This yields the full classification: positive definite (all eigenvalues >0, $p=n$); negative definite (all <0, $q=n$, equivalently odd-order leading principal minors <0 and even-order ones >0); positive semidefinite (all eigenvalues ≥0; when $|A|=0$ it is semidefinite but not definite); and indefinite (eigenvalues of both signs). Invertible linear changes (congruences) preserve both definiteness and the inertia indices, which is exactly why completing the square and orthogonal transformations always give the same verdict. Positive definite matrices are central to optimization (the second-order condition requires a positive definite Hessian), to least squares, and to numerical analysis (symmetric positive definite linear systems).
derivation: 设 $A$ 实对称，$f(x)=x^{T}Ax$。若对一切 $x\ne0$ 都有 $f(x)>0$，就称 $A$ 正定。取 $x=e_i$ 得 $a_{ii}=e_i^{T}Ae_i>0$。若 $Ax=0$ 有非零解 $x$，则 $f(x)=x^{T}Ax=0$，与正定性矛盾，故 $A$ 可逆、$|A|\ne0$。注意 $f(0)=0$ 是允许的：正定性只要求非零向量上的值严格为正。

由谱定理写 $A=Q\Lambda Q^{T}$，其中 $Q$ 正交，$\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$。令 $x=Qy$，则 $$f(x)=x^{T}Ax=y^{T}\Lambda y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_iy_i^2,\qquad \|x\|=\|y\|.$$ 若所有 $\lambda_i>0$，则对 $x
e0$（从而 $y
e0$）有 $f\ge(\min_i\lambda_i)\|y\|^2>0$。反之，若某个 $\lambda_k\le0$，取 $x=Qe_k
e0$，得 $f=\lambda_k\le0$，故不正定。因此 $A$ 正定 $\iff$ 全部特征值 $>0$。

必要性（Sylvester 判据的一半）：设 $A$ 正定，$A_k$ 为其左上角 $k$ 阶顺序主子矩阵。对任意 $0\ne y\in\mathbb{R}^k$，令 $\tilde y=(y,0,\dots,0)^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^n$，则 $y^{T}A_ky=\tilde y^{T}A\tilde y>0$，故 $A_k$ 正定。由第 2 步，$A_k$ 的特征值全为正，于是 $$D_k=\det A_k=\prod_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(A_k)>0.$$ 这对 $k=1,\dots,n$ 都成立。

充分性：设 $D_1,\dots,D_n>0$。对对称矩阵作不换行的消元，可得 $$A=LDL^{T},\qquad L\ \text{为单位下三角矩阵},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_n),$$ 其中 $d_1=D_1$，$d_k=D_k/D_{k-1}$（$k\ge2$）。这些等式由顺序主子式在消元中的变化直接得到；$D_k>0$ 保证所有 $d_k>0$ 且消元不中断。对 $x\ne0$，$L$ 可逆给出 $L^{T}x\ne0$，于是 $$x^{T}Ax=x^{T}LDL^{T}x=\sum_{k=1}^{n}d_k(L^{T}x)_k^2>0.$$ 故 $A$ 正定。

惯性定理：设同一二次型在两个基下分别化为 $$\begin{aligned}f&=\sum_{i=1}^{p}z_i^2-\sum_{i=p+1}^{p+q}z_i^2\\&=\sum_{i=1}^{p'}w_i^2-\sum_{i=p'+1}^{p'+q'}w_i^2,\end{aligned}$$ 其中 $r=p+q=p'+q'=\operatorname{rank}(A)$。若 $p>p'$，取 $U=\{z_{p+1}=\cdots=z_n=0\}$（$\dim U=p$）与 $Z=\{w_1=\cdots=w_{p'}=0\}$（$\dim Z=n-p'$）。因 $\dim U+\dim Z=p+n-p'>n$，存在 $0\ne v\in U\cap Z$。在 $U$ 上 $f\ge0$，在 $Z$ 上 $f\le0$，故 $f(v)=0$；但 $U$ 上 $f=0$ 迫使 $z_1=\cdots=z_p=0$，结合 $U$ 的定义得 $v=0$，矛盾。所以 $p\le p'$；对称地 $p'\le p$，故 $p=p'$，$q=q'$。

由惯性定理，正定等价于 $p=n$（此时 $q=0$），即 $A$ 与 $E$ 合同：存在可逆 $P$ 使 $P^{T}AP=E$。于是 $A=(P^{-1})^{T}P^{-1}$，取 $C=P^{-1}$ 得 $A=C^{T}C$，且 $f=\|Cx\|^2$。反过来，若 $A=C^{T}C$ 且 $C$ 可逆，则 $x\ne0\Rightarrow Cx\ne0\Rightarrow f=\|Cx\|^2>0$。故正定 $\iff A\cong E\iff A=C^{T}C$（$C$ 可逆）。反例：$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ 有 $D_1=1>0$、$D_2=0$，特征值为 $0,2$，$f=(x_1+x_2)^2$ 在直线 $x_1+x_2=0$ 上为零，故只是半正定而非正定。
derivationEn: Let $A$ be real symmetric and $f(x)=x^{T}Ax$. If $f(x)>0$ for every $x\ne0$, then $A$ is positive definite. Taking $x=e_i$ gives $a_{ii}=e_i^{T}Ae_i>0$. If $Ax=0$ had a nonzero solution $x$, then $f(x)=x^{T}Ax=0$, contradicting positive definiteness; hence $A$ is invertible and $|A|\ne0$. Note that $f(0)=0$ is allowed: positive definiteness requires strict positivity only on nonzero vectors.

By the spectral theorem write $A=Q\Lambda Q^{T}$ with $Q$ orthogonal and $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$. For $x=Qy$, $$f(x)=x^{T}Ax=y^{T}\Lambda y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_iy_i^2,\qquad \|x\|=\|y\|.$$ If all $\lambda_i>0$, then for $x
e0$ (hence $y
e0$), $f\ge(\min_i\lambda_i)\|y\|^2>0$. Conversely, if some $\lambda_k\le0$, take $x=Qe_k
e0$; then $f=\lambda_k\le0$, so the form is not positive definite. Therefore $A$ is positive definite iff all eigenvalues are positive.

Necessity (one half of Sylvester's criterion): let $A$ be positive definite and let $A_k$ be its top-left $k\times k$ principal submatrix. For any $0\ne y\in\mathbb{R}^k$, put $\tilde y=(y,0,\dots,0)^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^n$; then $y^{T}A_ky=\tilde y^{T}A\tilde y>0$, so $A_k$ is positive definite. By Step 2 all eigenvalues of $A_k$ are positive, hence $$D_k=\det A_k=\prod_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(A_k)>0.$$ This holds for every $k=1,\dots,n$.

Sufficiency: assume $D_1,\dots,D_n>0$. Gaussian elimination without row exchanges gives $$A=LDL^{T},\qquad L\ \text{unit lower triangular},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_n),$$ where $d_1=D_1$ and $d_k=D_k/D_{k-1}$ for $k\ge2$. These identities follow from how leading principal minors change under elimination; $D_k>0$ ensures every $d_k>0$ and no elimination step breaks down. For $x\ne0$, invertibility of $L$ gives $L^{T}x\ne0$, so $$x^{T}Ax=x^{T}LDL^{T}x=\sum_{k=1}^{n}d_k(L^{T}x)_k^2>0.$$ Hence $A$ is positive definite.

Law of inertia: suppose the same form is reduced in two bases to $$\begin{aligned}f&=\sum_{i=1}^{p}z_i^2-\sum_{i=p+1}^{p+q}z_i^2\\&=\sum_{i=1}^{p'}w_i^2-\sum_{i=p'+1}^{p'+q'}w_i^2,\end{aligned}$$ with $r=p+q=p'+q'=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. If $p>p'$, set $U=\{z_{p+1}=\cdots=z_n=0\}$ (dimension $p$) and $Z=\{w_1=\cdots=w_{p'}=0\}$ (dimension $n-p'$). Since $\dim U+\dim Z=p+n-p'>n$, there is $0\ne v\in U\cap Z$. On $U$ we have $f\ge0$, while on $Z$ we have $f\le0$, so $f(v)=0$. But on $U$, $f=0$ forces $z_1=\cdots=z_p=0$, and with $z_{p+1}=\cdots=z_n=0$ this gives $v=0$, a contradiction. Hence $p\le p'$; symmetrically $p'\le p$, so $p=p'$ and $q=q'$.

By the law of inertia, positive definiteness is exactly $p=n$ (then $q=0$), i.e. $A$ is congruent to $E$: there is an invertible $P$ with $P^{T}AP=E$. Then $A=(P^{-1})^{T}P^{-1}$; setting $C=P^{-1}$ gives $A=C^{T}C$ and $f=\|Cx\|^2$. Conversely, if $A=C^{T}C$ with $C$ invertible, then $x\ne0$ implies $Cx\ne0$, so $f=\|Cx\|^2>0$. Thus positive definite $\iff A\cong E\iff A=C^{T}C$ for some invertible $C$. Counterexample: $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ has $D_1=1>0$ and $D_2=0$, eigenvalues $0,2$, and $f=(x_1+x_2)^2$ vanishes on the line $x_1+x_2=0$; it is positive semidefinite but not positive definite.

formulas.note: 正定的特征值判据：全部特征值为正。反过来特征值有零或负值就不正定。
formulas.noteEn: Eigenvalue criterion: positive definite ⟺ all eigenvalues are positive; a zero or negative eigenvalue rules it out.

formulas.note: 顺序主子式判别法：Dₖ 是左上角 k 阶子式；全部严格大于 0 当且仅当正定。
formulas.noteEn: Leading principal minor criterion: Dₖ is the top-left k×k minor; all strictly positive ⟺ positive definite.

formulas.note: 规范形：正惯性指数 p、负惯性指数 q 唯一，秩 r 等于两者之和。
formulas.noteEn: The normal form: the positive index p and negative index q are unique, and the rank r equals their sum.

formulas.note: 正定 ⟺ A 与单位矩阵 E 合同；相应地，半正定 ⟺ A 与 diag(1,…,1,0,…,0) 合同。
formulas.noteEn: Positive definite ⟺ A is congruent to the identity E; likewise, positive semidefinite ⟺ A is congruent to diag(1,…,1,0,…,0).

formulas.note: 正定的等价刻画：A 可分解为可逆矩阵的转置乘积（取 C 为 Cholesky 因子即可），此时 f=‖Cx‖²>0。
formulas.noteEn: An equivalent description: A factors as CᵀC with invertible C (take the Cholesky factor); then f=‖Cx‖²>0.

properties: 正定 ⟺ 特征值全 >0 ⟺ 各阶顺序主子式全 >0 ⟺ 与单位矩阵合同 ⟺ 存在可逆矩阵 C 使 A=CᵀC。
可逆线性变换（合同变换）既保持二次型的正定性，也保持正、负惯性指数不变。
负定 ⟺ 特征值全 <0 ⟺ 奇数阶顺序主子式 <0 且偶数阶顺序主子式 >0；半正定 ⟺ 特征值全 ≥0，此时 |A|≥0，若 |A|=0 则只是半正定而非正定。
惯性定理：标准形不唯一，但正惯性指数 p 与负惯性指数 q 唯一，秩 r=p+q；两个二次型合同当且仅当它们的 p、q 相同（规范形相同）。
正定矩阵必可逆，且对角元 aᵢᵢ>0；不但各阶顺序主子式为正，它的所有主子式都大于 0。
propertiesEn: Positive definite ⟺ all eigenvalues >0 ⟺ all leading principal minors >0 ⟺ congruent to the identity ⟺ A=CᵀC for some invertible C.
Invertible linear changes (congruences) preserve positive definiteness and both inertia indices of a quadratic form.

Negative definite ⟺ all eigenvalues <0 ⟺ odd-order leading principal minors <0 and even-order ones >0; positive semidefinite ⟺ all eigenvalues ≥0, in which case |A|≥0, and |A|=0 means semidefinite but not definite.

Law of inertia: canonical forms are not unique, but the positive index p and the negative index q are; the rank is r=p+q, and two forms are congruent ⟺ they share the same p and q (equivalently the same normal form).
A positive definite matrix is invertible and has positive diagonal entries; moreover all of its principal minors (not just the leading ones) are positive.

examples.problem: 判断 $f(x_1,x_2,x_3)=5x_1^2+x_2^2+5x_3^2+4x_1x_2-8x_1x_3-4x_2x_3$ 是否正定，并在正定时用配方法求出标准形。
求 $t$ 的取值范围，使二次型 $f=t(x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2)+2x_1x_2+2x_1x_3-2x_2x_3$ 正定；并说明 $t$ 取其它值时它的正、负惯性指数。

linear-space-general.definition:
设 $F$ 是数域（本节点取 $F=\mathbb{R}$ 或 $\mathbb{C}$），$V$ 是非空集合。如果在 $V$ 上定义了两种运算——**加法**（任意 $\alpha,\beta\in V$ 对应 $V$ 中的一个元素 $\alpha+\beta$）与**数乘**（任意 $k\in F$、$\alpha\in V$ 对应 $V$ 中的一个元素 $k\alpha$）——并且对任意 $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in V$、$k,l\in F$ 满足下面八条公理，就称 $V$ 为数域 $F$ 上的**线性空间**（也叫向量空间），$V$ 中的元素称为**向量**。

八条公理分两组。**加法四条**：① 结合律 $(\alpha+\beta)+\gamma=\alpha+(\beta+\gamma)$；② 交换律 $\alpha+\beta=\beta+\alpha$；③ 存在零向量 $\mathbf{0}$，使 $\alpha+\mathbf{0}=\alpha$；④ 每个 $\alpha$ 都有负向量 $-\alpha$，使 $\alpha+(-\alpha)=\mathbf{0}$。**数乘四条**：⑤ 数乘结合律 $k(l\alpha)=(kl)\alpha$；⑥ 单位元 $1\alpha=\alpha$；⑦ 分配律 $k(\alpha+\beta)=k\alpha+k\beta$；⑧ 分配律 $(k+l)\alpha=k\alpha+l\alpha$。两种运算都必须「运算结果仍在 $V$ 中」（封闭性）——这是检验反例时的第一站。

典型例子：$\mathbb{R}^n$（数组空间）；次数不超过 $n$ 的实多项式全体 $P_n(\mathbb{R})$（含零多项式）；$m\times n$ 实矩阵全体 $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$；闭区间上的连续函数全体 $C[a,b]$。它们的加法与数乘都按「逐点」进行，八条公理逐条可见。反例：$V=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2: x\ge 0\}$ 按通常运算不是线性空间——取 $k=-1$，$(1,1)\in V$ 但 $k(1,1)=(-1,-1)\notin V$，对数乘不封闭。

由公理可直接推出：零向量与负向量都唯一、$0\alpha=\mathbf{0}$、$k\mathbf{0}=\mathbf{0}$、$(-1)\alpha=-\alpha$（左边的 $0$ 是数零，右边是零向量，别混）。**子空间判定**：$V$ 的非空子集 $W$ 是子空间，当且仅当三条同时成立——① $W\neq\varnothing$（验证 $\mathbf{0}\in W$ 通常最省事）；② 对加法封闭：$\alpha,\beta\in W\Rightarrow\alpha+\beta\in W$；③ 对数乘封闭：$\alpha\in W,\ k\in F\Rightarrow k\alpha\in W$。三条缺一不可：第一象限非空、对加法也封闭，但对 $k=-1$ 不封闭；空集虽然使两条封闭性空真成立，却不是子空间（三条里第一条就不满足）。$\{\mathbf{0}\}$ 与 $V$ 本身叫**平凡子空间**；子空间的交仍是子空间，而两个子空间的并一般不是子空间。
linear-space-general.definitionEn:
Let $F$ be a number field ($F=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$) and $V$ a nonempty set. If two operations are defined on $V$ — **addition**, turning any $\alpha,\beta\in V$ into some $\alpha+\beta\in V$, and **scalar multiplication**, turning $k\in F$ and $\alpha\in V$ into some $k\alpha\in V$ — and the following eight axioms hold for all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in V$ and $k,l\in F$, then $V$ is called a **linear space** (or vector space) over $F$, and its elements are called **vectors**.

The axioms form two groups. **Four for addition**: (1) associativity $(\alpha+\beta)+\gamma=\alpha+(\beta+\gamma)$; (2) commutativity $\alpha+\beta=\beta+\alpha$; (3) a zero vector $\mathbf{0}$ with $\alpha+\mathbf{0}=\alpha$; (4) a negative $-\alpha$ for each $\alpha$ with $\alpha+(-\alpha)=\mathbf{0}$. **Four for scalar multiplication**: (5) $k(l\alpha)=(kl)\alpha$; (6) the unit law $1\alpha=\alpha$; (7) $k(\alpha+\beta)=k\alpha+k\beta$; (8) $(k+l)\alpha=k\alpha+l\alpha$. Both operations must stay inside $V$ (closure) — the first thing to test in a counterexample.

Standard examples: $\mathbb{R}^n$; real polynomials of degree at most $n$, $P_n(\mathbb{R})$ (including the zero polynomial); all real $m\times n$ matrices $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$; all continuous functions $C[a,b]$ on a closed interval. Addition and scalar multiplication act pointwise, and the axioms are visible term by term. A counterexample: $V=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2: x\ge 0\}$ with the usual operations is not a linear space, since with $k=-1$ the vector $(1,1)\in V$ gives $k(1,1)=(-1,-1)\notin V$.

Immediate consequences: the zero vector and each negative are unique, and $0\alpha=\mathbf{0}$, $k\mathbf{0}=\mathbf{0}$, $(-1)\alpha=-\alpha$ (keep the scalar $0$ and the zero vector $\mathbf{0}$ apart). **Subspace test**: a nonempty subset $W\subseteq V$ is a subspace iff all three conditions hold — (1) $W\neq\varnothing$ (showing $\mathbf{0}\in W$ is usually easiest); (2) closed under addition; (3) closed under scalar multiplication. None can be dropped: the first quadrant is nonempty and closed under addition but fails for $k=-1$, while the empty set vacuously satisfies both closure rules yet is not a subspace. $\{\mathbf{0}\}$ and $V$ are the **trivial subspaces**; intersections of subspaces are subspaces, but a union of two subspaces generally is not.
derivation: 设 $F=\mathbb{R}$ 或 $\mathbb{C}$，$V$ 是非空集合。若加法 $V\times V\to V$ 与数乘 $F\times V\to V$ 对任意 $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in V$、$k,l\in F$ 满足八条公理：$$\begin{aligned}&(\alpha+\beta)+\gamma=\alpha+(\beta+\gamma),\qquad \alpha+\beta=\beta+\alpha,\\ &\exists\,\mathbf 0\in V\ \forall\alpha:\ \alpha+\mathbf 0=\alpha,\\ &\forall\alpha\ \exists(-\alpha):\ \alpha+(-\alpha)=\mathbf 0,\\ &k(l\alpha)=(kl)\alpha,\qquad 1\alpha=\alpha,\\ &k(\alpha+\beta)=k\alpha+k\beta,\qquad (k+l)\alpha=k\alpha+l\alpha,\end{aligned}$$ 则称 $V$ 为 $F$ 上的线性空间，$V$ 的元素称为向量。两个运算的取值必须仍在 $V$ 内（封闭性），这是检验反例的第一站；公理只约束运算，不要求元素是数组。

由公理推出基本事实。零向量唯一：若 $\mathbf 0,\mathbf 0'$ 都是零向量，则 $\mathbf 0=\mathbf 0+\mathbf 0'=\mathbf 0'$。负向量唯一：若 $\beta,\gamma$ 都是 $\alpha$ 的负向量，则 $$\beta=\beta+\mathbf 0=\beta+(\alpha+\gamma)=(\beta+\alpha)+\gamma=\mathbf 0+\gamma=\gamma.$$ 又 $0\alpha=(0+0)\alpha=0\alpha+0\alpha$，两边加 $-(0\alpha)$ 得 $0\alpha=\mathbf 0$；于是 $\alpha+(-1)\alpha=(1-1)\alpha=0\alpha=\mathbf 0$，由负向量唯一得 $(-1)\alpha=-\alpha$。

若 $k\alpha=\mathbf 0$ 且 $k\ne0$，则 $k$ 在数域中可逆，且 $k^{-1}\mathbf 0=\mathbf 0$（因为 $k\mathbf 0=k(0\mathbf 0)=(k\cdot0)\mathbf 0=0\mathbf 0=\mathbf 0$），于是 $$\alpha=1\alpha=(k^{-1}k)\alpha=k^{-1}(k\alpha)=k^{-1}\mathbf 0=\mathbf 0.$$ 反之 $k=0$ 或 $\alpha=\mathbf 0$ 都使 $k\alpha=\mathbf 0$。所以 $k\alpha=\mathbf 0\iff k=0$ 或 $\alpha=\mathbf 0$。这一步用到「数域中非零元可逆」，在一般环上不成立。

设 $W\subseteq V$ 非空。$W$ 是子空间当且仅当：① 对加法封闭，$u,v\in W\Rightarrow u+v\in W$；② 对数乘封闭，$k\in F,\ u\in W\Rightarrow ku\in W$。必要性由子空间本身是线性空间得到。充分性：取 $w\in W$（非空），由②得 $\mathbf 0=0w\in W$，又得 $(-1)w=-w\in W$，故零向量与负向量都在 $W$ 中；其余公理在 $V$ 中成立，限制在 $W$ 上仍成立，而①②保证运算不越出 $W$。

三条判定（非空、加法封闭、数乘封闭）缺一不可。$W=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x\ge0\}$ 非空且对加法封闭，但取 $k=-1$、$(1,1)\in W$ 得 $(-1,-1)\notin W$，故不是子空间；空集对两条封闭性空真成立，却不非空。正面例子：$\mathbb{R}^n$、次数不超过 $n$ 的多项式全体 $P_n(\mathbb{R})$（含零多项式）、$m\times n$ 实矩阵全体 $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$、闭区间上的连续函数全体 $C[a,b]$，都按逐点运算构成线性空间。

子空间的交仍是子空间：若 $W_1,W_2$ 是子空间，则 $\mathbf 0\in W_1\cap W_2$；$u,v\in W_1\cap W_2$、$k\in F$ 时 $u+v,ku$ 同时属于 $W_1$ 与 $W_2$，故属于交集。并一般不是子空间：$\mathbb{R}^2$ 中 $x$ 轴与 $y$ 轴的并集含 $(1,0)$、$(0,1)$，却不含 $(1,1)$。把「包含 $S$ 的所有子空间的交」记为 $\operatorname{span}(S)$，它就是包含 $S$ 的最小子空间；基、维数、线性相关等概念全部由八条公理推出，因此对多项式、矩阵与函数空间同样有效。
derivationEn: Let $F=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $V$ be a nonempty set. If addition $V\times V\to V$ and scalar multiplication $F\times V\to V$ satisfy, for all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in V$ and $k,l\in F$, the eight axioms $$\begin{aligned}&(\alpha+\beta)+\gamma=\alpha+(\beta+\gamma),\qquad \alpha+\beta=\beta+\alpha,\\ &\exists\,\mathbf 0\in V\ \forall\alpha:\ \alpha+\mathbf 0=\alpha,\\ &\forall\alpha\ \exists(-\alpha):\ \alpha+(-\alpha)=\mathbf 0,\\ &k(l\alpha)=(kl)\alpha,\qquad 1\alpha=\alpha,\\ &k(\alpha+\beta)=k\alpha+k\beta,\qquad (k+l)\alpha=k\alpha+l\alpha,\end{aligned}$$ then $V$ is called a linear space over $F$ and its elements are called vectors. Both operations must take values in $V$ (closure), the first checkpoint when testing a counterexample; the axioms constrain the operations, not the nature of the elements.

The axioms yield basic facts. The zero vector is unique: if $\mathbf 0$ and $\mathbf 0'$ are both zero vectors, then $\mathbf 0=\mathbf 0+\mathbf 0'=\mathbf 0'$. The negative is unique: if $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are both negatives of $\alpha$, then $$\beta=\beta+\mathbf 0=\beta+(\alpha+\gamma)=(\beta+\alpha)+\gamma=\mathbf 0+\gamma=\gamma.$$ Also $0\alpha=(0+0)\alpha=0\alpha+0\alpha$; adding $-(0\alpha)$ to both sides gives $0\alpha=\mathbf 0$. Hence $\alpha+(-1)\alpha=(1-1)\alpha=0\alpha=\mathbf 0$, and uniqueness of the negative gives $(-1)\alpha=-\alpha$.

If $k\alpha=\mathbf 0$ and $k\ne0$, then $k$ is invertible in the field and $k^{-1}\mathbf 0=\mathbf 0$ (since $k\mathbf 0=k(0\mathbf 0)=(k\cdot0)\mathbf 0=0\mathbf 0=\mathbf 0$), so $$\alpha=1\alpha=(k^{-1}k)\alpha=k^{-1}(k\alpha)=k^{-1}\mathbf 0=\mathbf 0.$$ Conversely, $k=0$ or $\alpha=\mathbf 0$ both give $k\alpha=\mathbf 0$. Therefore $k\alpha=\mathbf 0\iff k=0$ or $\alpha=\mathbf 0$. This step uses invertibility of nonzero field elements and fails over a general ring.

Let $W\subseteq V$ be nonempty. Then $W$ is a subspace if and only if (1) it is closed under addition, $u,v\in W\Rightarrow u+v\in W$, and (2) it is closed under scalar multiplication, $k\in F,\ u\in W\Rightarrow ku\in W$. Necessity follows because a subspace is itself a linear space. For sufficiency, choose $w\in W$ (nonempty); by (2), $\mathbf 0=0w\in W$ and $(-1)w=-w\in W$, so the zero vector and negatives lie in $W$. The remaining axioms hold in $V$ and restrict to $W$, while (1) and (2) keep both operations inside $W$.

The three tests (nonempty, closed under addition, closed under scalar multiplication) are all indispensable. The set $W=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x\ge0\}$ is nonempty and closed under addition, but $k=-1$ and $(1,1)\in W$ give $(-1,-1)\notin W$, so it is not a subspace. The empty set satisfies both closure conditions vacuously but is not nonempty. Standard examples: $\mathbb{R}^n$; all polynomials of degree at most $n$, $P_n(\mathbb{R})$ (including the zero polynomial); all real $m\times n$ matrices $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$; and all continuous functions $C[a,b]$ on a closed interval, each with pointwise operations.

An intersection of subspaces is a subspace: if $W_1,W_2$ are subspaces, then $\mathbf 0\in W_1\cap W_2$; for $u,v\in W_1\cap W_2$ and $k\in F$, both $u+v$ and $ku$ belong to $W_1$ and to $W_2$, hence to the intersection. A union is generally not a subspace: in $\mathbb{R}^2$ the union of the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis contains $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ but not $(1,1)$. The intersection of all subspaces containing a set $S$, written $\operatorname{span}(S)$, is the smallest subspace containing $S$; bases, dimension and linear dependence all follow from the eight axioms, so they apply equally to polynomial, matrix and function spaces.

formulas.note: 加法结合律与交换律（公理①、②）。
formulas.noteEn: Associativity and commutativity of addition (axioms 1 and 2).

formulas.note: 零向量与负向量（公理③、④）：两者都由 α 唯一确定。
formulas.noteEn: Zero vector and negatives (axioms 3 and 4); each is uniquely determined by α.

formulas.note: 数乘结合律与单位元（公理⑤、⑥）。
formulas.noteEn: Associativity of scalar multiplication and the unit law (axioms 5 and 6).

formulas.note: 两条分配律（公理⑦、⑧）：数乘对向量加法分配，数加法也对数乘分配。
formulas.noteEn: The two distributive laws (axioms 7 and 8): scalars distribute over vector addition, and scalar addition distributes over scalar multiplication.

formulas.note: 由公理推出的常用结论；最后一条用到数域中非零元可作除数。
formulas.noteEn: Standard consequences of the axioms; the last one uses that nonzero scalars are invertible in a number field.

properties: 零向量与每个向量的负向量都唯一；0α = 0、(−1)α = −α 是公理的推论，不是追加假设。
kα = 0（零向量）当且仅当 k = 0 或 α = 0；这条结论用到数域里非零数可作除数，是「数域」而非一般环上的性质。
子空间的判定三条（非空、对加法封闭、对数乘封闭）缺一不可；一个非空却不含零向量的集合必违反某条封闭性（否则 0α = 0 会落入其中），对加法不封闭的反例常取 α + β 越出集合。
{0} 与 V 是每个线性空间的平凡子空间；子空间的交仍是子空间，两个子空间的并一般不是（除非一个包含另一个）。
线性组合、线性表出、线性相关、基与维数等概念只用八条公理推出，因此对数组、多项式、矩阵、函数空间同样适用——这正是公理化定义的价值。
propertiesEn: The zero vector and the negative of each vector are unique; 0α = 0 and (−1)α = −α are consequences of the axioms rather than extra assumptions.
kα = 0 (the zero vector) holds iff k = 0 or α = 0; this relies on dividing by a nonzero scalar, so it is a property of a number field rather than of a general ring.

The three subspace conditions — nonempty, closed under addition, closed under scalar multiplication — are all indispensable; a nonempty set missing the zero vector must violate some closure (otherwise 0α = 0 would land in it), and typical addition failures take α + β outside the set.
{0} and V are the trivial subspaces of every linear space; an intersection of subspaces is a subspace, whereas a union of two subspaces generally is not (unless one contains the other).

Linear combinations, span, independence, bases and dimension follow from the eight axioms alone, so they apply equally to arrays, polynomials, matrices and function spaces — the payoff of the axiomatic definition.

examples.problem: 判断 $W=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{R}^3: x+2y-z=0\}$ 是否为 $\mathbb{R}^3$ 的子空间，并说明 $W$ 的几何形状。
examples.solution: 按三条逐一检查。① 非空：代入原点得 $0+0-0=0$，所以 $(0,0,0)\in W$。② 对加法封闭：设 $u=(x_1,y_1,z_1)$、$v=(x_2,y_2,z_2)\in W$，则 $x_1+2y_1-z_1=0$、$x_2+2y_2-z_2=0$，于是 $u+v$ 的坐标满足 $(x_1+x_2)+2(y_1+y_2)-(z_1+z_2)=0+0=0$，故 $u+v\in W$。③ 对数乘封闭：设 $k\in\mathbb{R}$，则 $(kx_1)+2(ky_1)-(kz_1)=k\cdot 0=0$，故 $ku\in W$。三条全过，$W$ 是子空间。事实上 $z=x+2y$，所以 $W=\{(x,y,x+2y): x,y\in\mathbb{R}\}=\operatorname{span}\{(1,0,1),(0,1,2)\}$，是 $\mathbb{R}^3$ 中过原点的一张平面，维数为 2。

对 $W_1$：零函数满足 $f(0)=0$，非空；若 $f,g\in W_1$，则 $(f+g)(0)=f(0)+g(0)=0$；若 $k\in\mathbb{R}$，则 $(kf)(0)=k\cdot 0=0$。三条全过，$W_1$ 是子空间。对 $W_2$：取 $f,g\in W_2$，则 $(f+g)(0)=1+1=2\neq 1$，对加法不封闭；等价地，$0\cdot f$ 是零函数而不在 $W_2$ 中，说明只要非空却不含零向量，就至少违反一条封闭性。$W_2$ 不是子空间——它是子空间 $W_1$ 的一个平移，属于「仿射集」而不是线性子空间。

basis-change.definition:
设 $V$ 是数域上的 $n$ 维线性空间，$\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ 与 $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n$ 是 $V$ 的两组基。每个 $\beta_j$ 都能唯一地用 $\alpha$ 组线性表出；把这些坐标按列排成矩阵 $P$，记作 $$(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)P,$$ 即 $P$ 的第 $j$ 列恰是 $\beta_j$ 在旧基 $\alpha$ 下的坐标。这个 $P$ 称为从旧基 $\alpha$ 到新基 $\beta$ 的**过渡矩阵**（换基矩阵）。

本节点的约定（与库内其它节点保持一致）：$P$ 的列 = 新基向量在旧基下的坐标。由此得到核心公式「**旧坐标 = P × 新坐标**」：设 $\xi$ 在旧基下的坐标为 $x$、在新基下的坐标为 $x'$，则 $x=Px'$，反向换算为 $x'=P^{-1}x$。这个方向极易写反——做题第一步先把 $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ 写下来，再代坐标。

$P$ 一定**可逆**。理由：若 $Pc=\mathbf{0}$ 且 $c\neq\mathbf{0}$，则 $(\beta)c=(\alpha)Pc=\mathbf{0}$，说明 $\beta$ 组线性相关，与「$\beta$ 是基」矛盾。反过来，若 $\alpha$ 是基、$P$ 可逆，则由上式定义的 $\beta$ 组也自动是基（一般结论：$n$ 个向量构成基，当且仅当它们关于某组基的坐标矩阵可逆）。于是从新基回到旧基的过渡矩阵是 $P^{-1}$：$$(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)=(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)P^{-1}.$$

坐标公式的推导：把 $\xi=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)x=(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)x'$ 中的 $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ 代入，得 $\xi=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)(Px')$。由于 $\alpha$ 组线性无关，表示系数唯一，比较即得 $x=Px'$。若再换一组基 $\gamma$ 且 $(\gamma)=(\beta)Q$，则 $(\gamma)=(\alpha)PQ$——过渡矩阵可以接力相乘。特别地，$\mathbb{R}^n$ 中把基向量按列排成矩阵 $A$（在标准基下），则从标准基到该基的过渡矩阵就是 $A$。
basis-change.definitionEn:
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional linear space over a number field, with two bases $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ and $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n$. Each $\beta_j$ is uniquely a linear combination of the $\alpha$'s; arranging those coordinates as the $j$-th column of a matrix $P$ gives $$(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)P,$$ so column $j$ of $P$ holds the coordinates of $\beta_j$ in the old basis. The matrix $P$ is called the **transition matrix** from the old basis $\alpha$ to the new basis $\beta$.

The convention of this node (consistent across the library): the columns of $P$ are the coordinates of the new basis vectors in the old basis. It yields the core rule **old coordinates = P × new coordinates**: if $\xi$ has coordinates $x$ in the old basis and $x'$ in the new one, then $x=Px'$, and conversely $x'=P^{-1}x$. The direction is easily reversed by mistake — always write $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ first, then substitute the coordinates.

$P$ is always **invertible**. Indeed, if $Pc=\mathbf{0}$ with $c\neq\mathbf{0}$, then $(\beta)c=(\alpha)Pc=\mathbf{0}$, contradicting linear independence of the $\beta$'s. Conversely, if $\alpha$ is a basis and $P$ is invertible, the $\beta$'s defined above form a basis too (in general, $n$ vectors form a basis iff their coordinate matrix with respect to some basis is invertible). Hence the transition matrix from the new basis back to the old one is $P^{-1}$.

Derivation of the coordinate rule: substitute $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ into $\xi=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)x=(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)x'$ to get $\xi=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)(Px')$. Uniqueness of coordinates in the independent set $\alpha$ gives $x=Px'$. For a further basis $\gamma$ with $(\gamma)=(\beta)Q$, one has $(\gamma)=(\alpha)PQ$, so transition matrices compose by multiplication. In particular, in $\mathbb{R}^n$, placing the basis vectors as the columns of a matrix $A$ (in the standard basis) makes $A$ the transition matrix from the standard basis.
derivation: 设 $V$ 是 $n$ 维线性空间，$\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ 与 $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n$ 是两组基。每个 $\beta_j$ 在 $\alpha$ 基下有唯一坐标，把这些坐标按列排成 $P=(p_{ij})$：$$\begin{aligned}\beta_j&=\sum_{i=1}^n p_{ij}\alpha_i,\\ (\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)&=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)P.\end{aligned}$$ 称 $P$ 为从旧基 $\alpha$ 到新基 $\beta$ 的过渡矩阵。约定：$P$ 的第 $j$ 列是新基向量 $\beta_j$ 在旧基下的坐标。

$P$ 必可逆。若 $Pc=\mathbf 0$ 且 $c\ne\mathbf 0$，则 $(\beta)c=(\alpha)Pc=\mathbf 0$，即 $\sum_j c_j\beta_j=\mathbf 0$ 有非平凡系数，与 $\beta$ 线性无关矛盾。反之，若 $\alpha$ 是基且 $P$ 可逆，由上式定义的 $\beta$ 组也线性无关：$(\beta)c=\mathbf 0$ 推出 $Pc=\mathbf 0$，故 $c=\mathbf 0$；$n$ 个无关向量构成 $n$ 维空间的基。于是从 $\beta$ 回到 $\alpha$ 的过渡矩阵是 $P^{-1}$：$(\alpha)=(\beta)P^{-1}$。

坐标变换：设向量 $\xi$ 在旧基下坐标为 $x$、在新基下为 $x'$，即 $\xi=(\alpha)x=(\beta)x'$。代入 $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ 得 $\xi=(\alpha)Px'$。由于 $\alpha$ 线性无关，表示系数唯一，故 $$x=Px',\qquad x'=P^{-1}x.$$ 口诀：旧坐标 $=P\times$ 新坐标，新坐标 $=P^{-1}\times$ 旧坐标。方向写反会让所有坐标出错。

例子：$\mathbb{R}^2$ 中取标准基 $\alpha_1=(1,0),\alpha_2=(0,1)$，新基 $\beta_1=(1,1),\beta_2=(1,-1)$。则 $$\begin{aligned}P&=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\\ P^{-1}&=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}$$ 对 $\xi=(3,1)$，$x'=P^{-1}x=\frac12(4,2)^{\mathsf T}=(2,1)^{\mathsf T}$。验算：$2\beta_1+\beta_2=(2,2)+(1,-1)=(3,1)=\xi$。若误用 $x'=Px$，会得到 $(4,2)^{\mathsf T}$，对应 $4\beta_1+2\beta_2=(6,2)\ne\xi$。

连续换基：若 $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$、$(\gamma)=(\beta)Q$，则 $(\gamma)=(\alpha)PQ$，即 $\alpha\to\gamma$ 的过渡矩阵是 $PQ$，顺序与基的书写顺序一致；反向为 $(PQ)^{-1}=Q^{-1}P^{-1}$。特别地，在 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 中把新基向量按列排成矩阵 $A$，则 $A$ 就是从标准基到该基的过渡矩阵，标准坐标 $x=Ax'$。

换基的应用：设 $T:V\to V$ 在旧基下矩阵为 $A$、新基下为 $A'$。由 $y=Ax$ 与 $x=Px'$、$y=Py'$ 得 $Py'=APx'$，故 $$[T]_{\mathcal B'}=P^{-1}[T]_{\mathcal B}P.$$ 这说明换基把矩阵变成相似矩阵，且 $\det A'=\det A$、$\operatorname{tr}A'=\operatorname{tr}A$、$\operatorname{rank}A'=\operatorname{rank}A$，特征多项式也相同。选基的目的正是让 $A'$ 尽量简单（例如对角形或若尔当形），而 $P$ 的列就是新基。
derivationEn: Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional linear space and let $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ and $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n$ be two bases. Each $\beta_j$ has unique coordinates in the $\alpha$-basis; arranging these coordinates as the $j$-th column of a matrix $P=(p_{ij})$ gives $$\begin{aligned}\beta_j&=\sum_{i=1}^n p_{ij}\alpha_i,\\ (\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)&=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)P.\end{aligned}$$ The matrix $P$ is called the transition matrix from the old basis $\alpha$ to the new basis $\beta$. Convention: column $j$ of $P$ holds the coordinates of the new basis vector $\beta_j$ in the old basis.

$P$ is necessarily invertible. If $Pc=\mathbf 0$ with $c\ne\mathbf 0$, then $(\beta)c=(\alpha)Pc=\mathbf 0$, i.e. $\sum_j c_j\beta_j=\mathbf 0$ with nontrivial coefficients, contradicting linear independence of the $\beta$'s. Conversely, if $\alpha$ is a basis and $P$ is invertible, the $\beta$'s defined above are independent: $(\beta)c=\mathbf 0$ implies $Pc=\mathbf 0$, hence $c=\mathbf 0$; $n$ independent vectors form a basis of an $n$-dimensional space. Therefore the transition matrix from $\beta$ back to $\alpha$ is $P^{-1}$: $(\alpha)=(\beta)P^{-1}$.

Coordinate transformation: let a vector $\xi$ have coordinates $x$ in the old basis and $x'$ in the new one, so $\xi=(\alpha)x=(\beta)x'$. Substituting $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ gives $\xi=(\alpha)Px'$. Since $\alpha$ is linearly independent, the coefficients are unique, hence $$x=Px',\qquad x'=P^{-1}x.$$ In words: old coordinates $=P\times$ new coordinates, and new coordinates $=P^{-1}\times$ old coordinates. Reversing this direction corrupts every coordinate.

Example: in $\mathbb{R}^2$ take the standard basis $\alpha_1=(1,0),\alpha_2=(0,1)$ and the new basis $\beta_1=(1,1),\beta_2=(1,-1)$. Then $$\begin{aligned}P&=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\\ P^{-1}&=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}$$ For $\xi=(3,1)$, $x'=P^{-1}x=\frac12(4,2)^{\mathsf T}=(2,1)^{\mathsf T}$. Check: $2\beta_1+\beta_2=(2,2)+(1,-1)=(3,1)=\xi$. Using $x'=Px$ by mistake would give $(4,2)^{\mathsf T}$, corresponding to $4\beta_1+2\beta_2=(6,2)\ne\xi$.

Successive changes: if $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ and $(\gamma)=(\beta)Q$, then $(\gamma)=(\alpha)PQ$, so the transition matrix from $\alpha$ to $\gamma$ is $PQ$, in the same order as the bases are written; the reverse is $(PQ)^{-1}=Q^{-1}P^{-1}$. In particular, in $\mathbb{R}^n$, placing the new basis vectors as the columns of a matrix $A$ makes $A$ the transition matrix from the standard basis, and standard coordinates satisfy $x=Ax'$.

Application to linear maps: let $T:V\to V$ have matrix $A$ in the old basis and $A'$ in the new basis. From $y=Ax$, $x=Px'$ and $y=Py'$ we get $Py'=APx'$, hence $$[T]_{\mathcal B'}=P^{-1}[T]_{\mathcal B}P.$$ Thus a change of basis turns the matrix into a similar one, with $\det A'=\det A$, $\operatorname{tr}A'=\operatorname{tr}A$, $\operatorname{rank}A'=\operatorname{rank}A$, and the same characteristic polynomial. The purpose of choosing a basis is to make $A'$ as simple as possible (diagonal or Jordan form, for instance), and the columns of $P$ are the new basis vectors.

formulas.note: 换基约定：P 的第 j 列是 βⱼ 在旧基 α 下的坐标。
formulas.noteEn: Change-of-basis convention: column j of P gives the coordinates of β_j in the old basis α.

formulas.note: 坐标变换核心公式：旧坐标 = P × 新坐标；新坐标 = P⁻¹ × 旧坐标。
formulas.noteEn: Core coordinate rule: old coordinates = P × new coordinates; new coordinates = P⁻¹ × old.

formulas.note: 分量形式：P 的第 i 行与新坐标列向量做内积，得到旧坐标的第 i 个分量。
formulas.noteEn: Component form: row i of P dotted with the new coordinate vector gives the i-th old coordinate.

formulas.note: P 一定可逆；从新基回到旧基的过渡矩阵是 P⁻¹。
formulas.noteEn: P is always invertible; the matrix P⁻¹ takes the new basis back to the old one.

formulas.note: 连续换基：过渡矩阵相乘，顺序与基的书写顺序一致（α→β→γ 对应 PQ）。
formulas.noteEn: Successive changes compose: for α→β→γ the transition matrix is PQ, in the same order as the bases are written.

properties: 过渡矩阵一定可逆；反之，若 (β) = (α)P 而 P 不可逆，则 β 组线性相关，不能是基。
方向约定：「旧坐标 = P × 新坐标」，即 x = Px′、x′ = P⁻¹x；写反方向会让全部坐标出错。
复合律：α→β 用 P、β→γ 用 Q，则 α→γ 用 PQ；从新基回旧基用 P⁻¹。
ℝⁿ 中把新基向量按列排成矩阵 A，则 A 就是从标准基到新基的过渡矩阵，标准坐标 = A × 新坐标（可用它快速心算验证方向）。
换基只改变坐标、不改变向量本身；许多问题（对角化、二次型化简、正交化）本质上都是「选一组好基」。
propertiesEn: A transition matrix is always invertible; conversely, if (β) = (α)P with P singular, the β's are linearly dependent and cannot be a basis.
Direction of the convention: old coordinates = P × new coordinates, x = Px′ and x′ = P⁻¹x; reversing it corrupts every coordinate.
Composition: α→β uses P and β→γ uses Q, so α→γ uses PQ, while going back from a new basis to the old one uses P⁻¹.

In ℝⁿ, putting the new basis vectors as columns of a matrix A makes A the transition matrix from the standard basis, with standard coordinates = A × new coordinates (a quick way to double-check the direction).
A change of basis changes coordinates but never the vector itself; many problems (diagonalization, reducing quadratic forms, orthogonalization) are really about choosing a good basis.

examples.problem: 在 $\mathbb{R}^2$ 中取旧基 $\alpha_1=(1,0)$、$\alpha_2=(0,1)$（标准基），新基 $\beta_1=(1,1)$、$\beta_2=(1,-1)$。(1) 写出过渡矩阵 $P$；(2) 求向量 $\xi=(3,1)$ 在新基下的坐标。
examples.solution: (1) 按约定，$P$ 的列是新基向量在标准基下的坐标，故 $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$。(2) 由 $x=Px'$ 得 $x'=P^{-1}x$。$\det P=1\cdot(-1)-1\cdot 1=-2$，$P^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{-2}\begin{pmatrix}-1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}=\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$。于是 $x'=\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}3\\1\end{pmatrix}=\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}4\\2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\end{pmatrix}$。验算：$2\beta_1+1\beta_2=(2,2)+(1,-1)=(3,1)=\xi$。

examples.problem: 设两组基满足 $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ 与 $(\gamma)=(\beta)Q$，其中 $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$，$Q=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$。已知 $\xi$ 在 $\alpha$ 下的坐标为 $x=(1,1)^{\mathrm T}$，求 $\xi$ 在 $\gamma$ 下的坐标。
examples.solution: 先求 $\alpha\to\gamma$ 的过渡矩阵 $R=PQ=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&3\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3&3\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$。由 $x=Rx_\gamma$ 得 $x_\gamma=R^{-1}x$。$\det R=9-3=6$，$R^{-1}=\dfrac16\begin{pmatrix}3&-3\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}$，故 $x_\gamma=\dfrac16\begin{pmatrix}3-3\\-1+3\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1/3\end{pmatrix}$。分步验算：先去 β 系，$x_\beta=P^{-1}x=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix}$，即 $\xi=\beta_2$；再由 $x_\gamma=Q^{-1}x_\beta$，$Q^{-1}=\dfrac16\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$，得 $x_\gamma=\dfrac16\begin{pmatrix}0\\2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1/3\end{pmatrix}$，一致。最后核对：$\xi=\beta_2=\alpha_1+\alpha_2$，而 $\gamma_2=3\beta_2=3(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)$，所以 $\dfrac13\gamma_2=\alpha_1+\alpha_2=\xi$。

linear-transformation.definition:
设 $V,W$ 是数域 $F$ 上的线性空间。映射 $T:V\to W$ 如果对任意 $\alpha,\beta\in V$ 和任意 $k,l\in F$ 都满足 $$T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta),$$ 就称为从 $V$ 到 $W$ 的**线性变换**（线性映射）。这条定义等价于两条：**保加法** $T(\alpha+\beta)=T(\alpha)+T(\beta)$ 与**保数乘** $T(k\alpha)=kT(\alpha)$。取 $k=l=0$ 立即得到 $T(\mathbf{0})=\mathbf{0}$，所以「$T(0)=0$」是线性的必要条件，但不是充分条件。当 $W=V$ 时称 $T$ 为 $V$ 上的线性变换。

典型例子：恒等变换 $I$、数乘变换 $T(\alpha)=k\alpha$、投影 $P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$、多项式空间上的求导算子 $D(p)=p'$、积分算子 $T(f)(x)=\int_0^x f(t)\,\mathrm dt$、以及「左乘矩阵」$T(x)=Ax$。非线性反例：$T(x)=x+1$（连原点都不固定）、$T(x)=x^2$、$T(x)=\lVert x\rVert$。

**矩阵表示**：设 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ 是 $V$ 的基，$\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m$ 是 $W$ 的基。把每个像 $T(\alpha_j)$ 用 $\beta$ 基表出：$T(\alpha_j)=a_{1j}\beta_1+\cdots+a_{mj}\beta_m$，以这些系数为第 $j$ 列排成 $m\times n$ 矩阵 $A$，就得到 $T$ 在给定基下的矩阵。坐标公式：若 $\xi=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)x$，则 $T(\xi)=(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m)(Ax)$——**矩阵的第 j 列就是 T(αⱼ) 的坐标**，矩阵乘法一次性完成「变换 + 换坐标」。取定基后 $T\mapsto A$ 是一一对应：复合对应矩阵乘法 $T_2T_1\leftrightarrow A_2A_1$，可逆变换对应可逆矩阵。

**换基下的变化**：设 $T$ 是 $V$ 上的线性变换，在旧基 $\alpha$ 下矩阵为 $A$，在新基 $\beta$ 下矩阵为 $A'$，且 $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$（约定同「基变换与坐标变换」节点：$P$ 的列是新基在旧基下的坐标）。则 $$A'=P^{-1}AP,$$ 即同一线性变换在不同基下的矩阵**相似**，$P$ 正是那个过渡矩阵。推导：旧基下坐标满足 $y=Ax$；由于 $x=Px'$、$y=Py'$，代入得 $Py'=APx'$，于是 $y'=P^{-1}APx'$。
linear-transformation.definitionEn:
Let $V,W$ be linear spaces over a number field $F$. A map $T:V\to W$ is called a **linear transformation** (linear map) if $$T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)$$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in V$ and all $k,l\in F$. The definition is equivalent to two rules: $T(\alpha+\beta)=T(\alpha)+T(\beta)$ (preserving addition) and $T(k\alpha)=kT(\alpha)$ (preserving scalar multiplication). Taking $k=l=0$ gives $T(\mathbf{0})=\mathbf{0}$, so $T(0)=0$ is necessary for linearity but far from sufficient. If $W=V$, one says $T$ is a linear transformation on $V$.

Examples: the identity $I$, scalar maps $T(\alpha)=k\alpha$, the projection $P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$, the derivative operator $D(p)=p'$ on polynomials, the integral operator $T(f)(x)=\int_0^x f(t)\,\mathrm dt$, and left multiplication by a matrix $T(x)=Ax$. Non-linear counterexamples: $T(x)=x+1$ (it does not even fix the origin), $T(x)=x^2$, $T(x)=\lVert x\rVert$.

**Matrix representation**: let $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ be a basis of $V$ and $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m$ a basis of $W$. Express each image, $T(\alpha_j)=a_{1j}\beta_1+\cdots+a_{mj}\beta_m$, and arrange the coefficients as the $j$-th column of an $m\times n$ matrix $A$. Coordinate formula: if $\xi=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)x$ then $T(\xi)=(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m)(Ax)$ — **column j of A is the coordinate vector of $T(\alpha_j)$**, and one matrix multiplication performs the transformation and the coordinate bookkeeping at once. With bases fixed, $T\mapsto A$ is a bijection: composition corresponds to matrix multiplication $T_2T_1\leftrightarrow A_2A_1$, and invertibility to invertible matrices.

**Under a change of basis**: let $T$ be a linear transformation on $V$, with matrix $A$ in the old basis $\alpha$ and $A'$ in the new basis $\beta$, where $(\beta)=(\alpha)P$ (same convention as in the change-of-basis node: columns of $P$ are the new basis vectors in the old basis). Then $$A'=P^{-1}AP,$$ i.e. matrices of the same transformation in different bases are **similar**, with $P$ the transition matrix. Derivation: coordinates in the old basis satisfy $y=Ax$; since $x=Px'$ and $y=Py'$, substitution gives $Py'=APx'$, hence $y'=P^{-1}APx'$. For a map between two different spaces, changing the basis of $V$ by $P$ and that of $W$ by $Q$ gives $A'=Q^{-1}AP$ instead; the similarity formula above is the special case $V=W$ with the same transition matrix applied on both sides.
derivation: 设 $V,W$ 是 $F$ 上的线性空间。映射 $T:V\to W$ 称为线性变换，若对任意 $\alpha,\beta\in V$、$k,l\in F$ 有 $T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)$。取 $k=l=1$ 得保加法，取 $l=0$ 得保数乘，故定义等价于这两条。取 $k=l=0$ 得 $T(\mathbf 0)=\mathbf 0$，所以「原点不动」是必要条件；但它不充分，例如 $T(x,y)=(x^2,y)$ 满足 $T(0,0)=(0,0)$，却因 $T(2,1)=(4,1)\ne2T(1,1)=(2,2)$ 而不是线性的。

取定 $V$ 的基 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ 与 $W$ 的基 $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m$。把每个像按 $\beta$ 基展开：$T(\alpha_j)=\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ij}\beta_i$，以 $a_{ij}$ 为第 $j$ 列排成 $m\times n$ 矩阵 $A$，称 $A$ 为 $T$ 在这两组基下的矩阵。若 $\xi=\sum_j x_j\alpha_j$，则 $$T(\xi)=\sum_j x_jT(\alpha_j)=\sum_{i=1}^m\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}x_j\Bigr)\beta_i,$$ 即 $T(\xi)$ 的坐标是 $y=Ax$。矩阵的第 $j$ 列就是 $T(\alpha_j)$ 的坐标，这一口诀是写出矩阵表示的最快方式。

例子：$P_2(\mathbb{R})$ 取基 $1,x,x^2$，求导算子 $D(p)=p'$ 满足 $D(1)=0$、$D(x)=1$、$D(x^2)=2x$，故 $$[D]=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&2\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ 对 $p=3+2x-x^2$，坐标 $x=(3,2,-1)^{\mathsf T}$，$[D]x=(2,-2,0)^{\mathsf T}$，对应 $2-2x$，与直接求导一致；并且 $[D]^3=O$，说明求导三次是零算子。

核与像：$\ker T=\{\alpha:T(\alpha)=\mathbf 0\}$ 与 $\operatorname{Im}T=\{T(\alpha):\alpha\in V\}$ 分别是 $V$ 与 $W$ 的子空间。若 $V$ 有限维，秩–零化度定理给出 $$\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim V.$$ 证明要点：取 $\ker T$ 的基 $v_1,\dots,v_r$ 并扩充为 $V$ 的基 $v_1,\dots,v_r,v_{r+1},\dots,v_n$；若 $\sum_{i>r}c_iT(v_i)=0$，则 $\sum_{i>r}c_iv_i\in\ker T$，写成前 $r$ 个基向量的组合，由基的无关性得所有 $c_i=0$，故这 $n-r$ 个像无关；任取 $T(v)\in\operatorname{Im}T$，把 $v$ 按上述基展开并去掉核分量，即知 $T(v)$ 是这些像的线性组合，故它们张成 $\operatorname{Im}T$。于是 $T$ 单射 $\iff\ker T=\{\mathbf 0\}$，$T$ 满射 $\iff\operatorname{Im}T=W$；当 $\dim V=\dim W<\infty$ 时，单射、满射、可逆三者等价。

复合与逆：若 $T_1:V\to W$ 在基 $\alpha,\beta$ 下矩阵为 $A_1$，$T_2:W\to U$ 在基 $\beta,\gamma$ 下矩阵为 $A_2$，则 $T_2T_1$ 在 $\alpha,\gamma$ 下的矩阵为 $A_2A_1$——先作用的变换在右边。取定基后 $T\mapsto A$ 是线性同构，$T$ 可逆当且仅当 $A$ 可逆，且 $T^{-1}$ 的矩阵为 $A^{-1}$。

矩阵表示依赖基。设 $T:V\to V$，旧基 $\alpha$ 下矩阵为 $A=[T]_{\mathcal B}$，新基 $\beta$ 下为 $A'=[T]_{\mathcal B'}$，且 $(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)P$，即 $P$ 的列是新基在旧基下的坐标。旧、新坐标满足 $x=Px'$、$y=Py'$。由 $y=Ax$ 得 $Py'=APx'$，左乘 $P^{-1}$ 得 $$y'=P^{-1}APx',\qquad [T]_{\mathcal B'}=P^{-1}[T]_{\mathcal B}P.$$ 所以同一变换在不同基下的矩阵相似；$\det A'=\det A$、$\operatorname{tr}A'=\operatorname{tr}A$、秩与特征多项式都不随基改变。若 $V,W$ 不同且分别换基 $P,Q$，则公式改为 $A'=Q^{-1}AP$。
derivationEn: Let $V,W$ be linear spaces over $F$. A map $T:V\to W$ is called a linear transformation if $T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in V$ and $k,l\in F$. Taking $k=l=1$ gives additivity and taking $l=0$ gives homogeneity, so the definition is equivalent to those two rules. Taking $k=l=0$ gives $T(\mathbf 0)=\mathbf 0$, so fixing the origin is necessary; it is not sufficient: $T(x,y)=(x^2,y)$ satisfies $T(0,0)=(0,0)$ but $T(2,1)=(4,1)\ne2T(1,1)=(2,2)$, so it is not linear.

Fix a basis $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ of $V$ and a basis $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m$ of $W$. Expand each image in the $\beta$-basis: $T(\alpha_j)=\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ij}\beta_i$, and arrange the coefficients $a_{ij}$ as the $j$-th column of an $m\times n$ matrix $A$. Then $A$ is the matrix of $T$ in these bases. If $\xi=\sum_j x_j\alpha_j$, then $$T(\xi)=\sum_j x_jT(\alpha_j)=\sum_{i=1}^m\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}x_j\Bigr)\beta_i,$$ so the coordinates of $T(\xi)$ are $y=Ax$. Column $j$ of $A$ is the coordinate vector of $T(\alpha_j)$; this motto is the fastest way to write the matrix down.

Example: on $P_2(\mathbb{R})$ with basis $1,x,x^2$, the derivative $D(p)=p'$ satisfies $D(1)=0$, $D(x)=1$ and $D(x^2)=2x$, hence $$[D]=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&2\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ For $p=3+2x-x^2$ with coordinate vector $x=(3,2,-1)^{\mathsf T}$, we get $[D]x=(2,-2,0)^{\mathsf T}$, corresponding to $2-2x$, in agreement with direct differentiation; moreover $[D]^3=O$, so differentiating three times is the zero operator.

Kernel and image: $\ker T=\{\alpha:T(\alpha)=\mathbf 0\}$ and $\operatorname{Im}T=\{T(\alpha):\alpha\in V\}$ are subspaces of $V$ and $W$, respectively. If $V$ is finite-dimensional, the rank–nullity theorem gives $$\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim V.$$ Proof sketch: take a basis $v_1,\dots,v_r$ of $\ker T$ and extend it to a basis $v_1,\dots,v_r,v_{r+1},\dots,v_n$ of $V$. If $\sum_{i>r}c_iT(v_i)=0$, then $\sum_{i>r}c_iv_i\in\ker T$, so it is a combination of the first $r$ basis vectors; independence forces all $c_i=0$. Thus the $n-r$ images are independent; moreover, any $T(v)\in\operatorname{Im}T$ becomes a linear combination of these images after expanding $v$ in the basis and removing its kernel component, so they span $\operatorname{Im}T$. Consequently $T$ is injective $\iff\ker T=\{\mathbf 0\}$, and surjective $\iff\operatorname{Im}T=W$; when $\dim V=\dim W<\infty$, injective, surjective and invertible are equivalent.

Composition and inverses: if $T_1:V\to W$ has matrix $A_1$ in bases $\alpha,\beta$, and $T_2:W\to U$ has matrix $A_2$ in bases $\beta,\gamma$, then $T_2T_1$ has matrix $A_2A_1$ in bases $\alpha,\gamma$ — the map applied first sits on the right. Once bases are fixed, $T\mapsto A$ is a linear isomorphism; $T$ is invertible if and only if $A$ is invertible, and then $T^{-1}$ has matrix $A^{-1}$.

The matrix representation depends on the basis. Let $T:V\to V$ have matrix $A=[T]_{\mathcal B}$ in the old basis $\alpha$ and $A'=[T]_{\mathcal B'}$ in the new basis $\beta$, where $(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n)=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)P$; the columns of $P$ are the new basis vectors in the old basis. Old and new coordinates satisfy $x=Px'$ and $y=Py'$. From $y=Ax$ we get $Py'=APx'$, and left multiplication by $P^{-1}$ gives $$y'=P^{-1}APx',\qquad [T]_{\mathcal B'}=P^{-1}[T]_{\mathcal B}P.$$ Thus matrices of the same transformation in different bases are similar; $\det A'=\det A$, $\operatorname{tr}A'=\operatorname{tr}A$, and the rank and characteristic polynomial are unchanged. If $V$ and $W$ are different and their bases are changed by $P$ and $Q$ respectively, the formula becomes $A'=Q^{-1}AP$.

formulas.note: 线性变换的定义式；等价于保加法 + 保数乘。
formulas.noteEn: The defining identity of a linear transformation; equivalent to preserving addition and scalar multiplication.

formulas.note: 矩阵表示：A 的第 j 列是 T(αⱼ) 在给定基下的坐标。
formulas.noteEn: Matrix representation: column j of A is the coordinate vector of T(α_j) in the chosen bases.

formulas.note: 坐标公式：用矩阵乘法计算线性变换的作用（先取坐标，再乘矩阵）。
formulas.noteEn: Coordinate formula: matrix multiplication computes the action of T (take coordinates, then multiply).

formulas.note: 换基公式：同一变换在新基下的矩阵是 P⁻¹AP，P 为过渡矩阵（方向与「旧坐标 = P × 新坐标」一致）。
formulas.noteEn: Change-of-basis formula: in a new basis the matrix becomes P⁻¹AP, with P the transition matrix (the same P as in old coordinates = P × new coordinates).

formulas.note: 复合与逆的对应：复合顺序与矩阵乘法顺序一致（先作用的在右边）。
formulas.noteEn: Composition and inverses: the order of composition matches matrix multiplication (the map applied first sits on the right).

properties: T 线性 ⟺ 保加法且保数乘；线性一定把零向量映为零向量，但 T(0) = 0 不代表线性（例如 T(x,y) = (x², y)，原点不动却不是线性映射）。
取定 V 与 W 的基后，线性变换与 m×n 矩阵一一对应；口诀「第 j 列 = T(αⱼ) 的坐标」是写出矩阵的快捷方式。
复合对应矩阵乘法：T₁: V→W 的矩阵为 A₁（基 α→β），T₂: W→U 的矩阵为 A₂（基 β→γ），则 T₂T₁ 的矩阵为 A₂A₁。
同空间换基：A′ = P⁻¹AP，P 是基变换的过渡矩阵；相似矩阵是同一变换的不同基版本，所以行列式、迹、秩、特征多项式都是相似不变量。
线性变换的核与像都是子空间；T 可逆 ⟺ 在任意给定基下其矩阵可逆，且此时 T⁻¹ 的矩阵为 A⁻¹。
propertiesEn: T is linear iff it preserves addition and scalar multiplication; linearity forces T(0) = 0, but T(0) = 0 does not imply linearity (e.g. T(x,y) = (x², y) fixes the origin yet is not linear).
With bases of V and W fixed, linear maps correspond one-to-one to m×n matrices; the motto column j = coordinates of T(α_j) is the fastest way to write the matrix down.
Composition corresponds to matrix multiplication: T₁: V→W with matrix A₁ (bases α→β) and T₂: W→U with matrix A₂ (bases β→γ) compose to T₂T₁ with matrix A₂A₁.

For transformations of one space, a change of basis gives A′ = P⁻¹AP with P the transition matrix; similar matrices are two views of the same transformation, so determinant, trace, rank and characteristic polynomial are similarity invariants.
The kernel and the image of a linear map are subspaces; T is invertible iff its matrix in any chosen bases is invertible, and then T⁻¹ has matrix A⁻¹.

examples.problem: 设 $P_2(\mathbb{R})$ 是次数不超过 2 的多项式空间（取基 $1,x,x^2$），$D(p)=p'$ 是求导算子。求 $D$ 在该基下的矩阵，并用矩阵乘法计算 $D$ 作用于 $p=3+2x-x^2$ 的结果。
examples.solution: $D(1)=0$、$D(x)=1$、$D(x^2)=2x$，按列排坐标得 $D$ 的矩阵 $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&2\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$。$p$ 的坐标向量为 $x=(3,2,-1)^{\mathrm T}$，逐行相乘得 $Ax=(0\cdot 3+1\cdot 2+0\cdot(-1),\ 0+0+2\cdot(-1),\ 0)^{\mathrm T}=(2,-2,0)^{\mathrm T}$，对应多项式 $2-2x$，与直接求导 $p'=2-2x$ 一致。另外 $A^3=O$：求导作用三次就是零算子，这是幂零变换的典型例子（与若尔当标准型相呼应）。

examples.problem: 在 $\mathbb{R}^2$ 中，$T$ 是逆时针旋转 $90^\circ$，在标准基 $\alpha_1=(1,0)$、$\alpha_2=(0,1)$ 下矩阵为 $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$。取新基 $\beta_1=(1,1)$、$\beta_2=(1,-1)$，求 $T$ 在新基下的矩阵 $A'$。
examples.solution: 过渡矩阵 $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$（列 = 新基在标准基下的坐标），$P^{-1}=\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$。由换基公式 $A'=P^{-1}AP$：先算 $AP=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$，再算 $A'=\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}-1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}=\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\-2&0\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$。验算：$T(\beta_1)=(-1,1)=0\cdot\beta_1-1\cdot\beta_2$，$T(\beta_2)=(1,1)=1\cdot\beta_1+0\cdot\beta_2$，故矩阵两列分别为 $(0,-1)^{\mathrm T}$ 与 $(1,0)^{\mathrm T}$，与 $A'$ 一致。

rank-nullity.definition:
设 $T:V\to W$ 是数域上的线性变换。称 $$\ker T=\{\alpha\in V: T(\alpha)=\mathbf{0}\}$$ 为 $T$ 的**核**（零空间），称 $$\operatorname{Im}T=\{T(\alpha):\alpha\in V\}=T(V)$$ 为 $T$ 的**像**（值域）。$\ker T$ 是 $V$ 的子空间，$\operatorname{Im}T$ 是 $W$ 的子空间：核含零向量，且当 $\alpha,\beta\in\ker T$ 时 $T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=\mathbf{0}$，仍落在核中；当 $u=T(\alpha),v=T(\beta)\in\operatorname{Im}T$ 时 $ku+lv=T(k\alpha+l\beta)$，仍落在像中。

**维数定理**（秩零化度定理）：设 $V$ 是有限维线性空间，$T:V\to W$ 是线性变换，则 $$\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim V.$$ 其中 $\dim\operatorname{Im}T$ 称为 $T$ 的**秩**，$\dim\ker T$ 称为**零化度**。注意等号右边是**定义域 $V$ 的维数**，不是 $W$ 的维数——这是最容易记错的地方。矩阵版本：$m\times n$ 矩阵 $A$ 满足 $\operatorname{rank}(A)+\operatorname{nullity}(A)=n$；把 $A$ 看成 $T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$，$x\mapsto Ax$，则 $\operatorname{rank}(A)=\dim\operatorname{Im}T$，而齐次方程组 $Ax=0$ 的解空间正是 $\ker T$，其维数为 $n-\operatorname{rank}(A)$。

**单射与满射**：$T$ 是单射 $\iff\ker T=\{\mathbf{0}\}$（即 $Ax=0$ 只有零解）；$T$ 是满射 $\iff\operatorname{Im}T=W\iff\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim W$；当 $\dim V=\dim W<\infty$ 时，「单射」「满射」「可逆（同构）」三者互相等价。直观理解：核度量被 $T$ 压成零的「信息量」，像度量 $T$ 能到达的范围，两者维数之和恒等于 $\dim V$——压掉多少，到达的就少多少。

**两个模型与不变子空间**：投影 $P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$ 的核是 $z$ 轴（1 维），像是 $xy$ 平面（2 维），$1+2=3$；求导 $D:P_n\to P_n$ 的核是常数多项式（1 维），像是次数不超过 $n-1$ 的多项式（$n$ 维），$1+n=n+1$。若子空间 $W_0\subseteq V$ 满足 $T(W_0)\subseteq W_0$，就称 $W_0$ 为 $T$ 的**不变子空间**：$\ker T$、$\operatorname{Im}T$、以及后面要学的特征子空间都是典型例子。把 $W_0$ 的基扩充成 $V$ 的基，$T$ 的矩阵呈**分块上三角** $\begin{pmatrix}B&C\\O&D\end{pmatrix}$，左下角的零块 $O$ 正是 $T(W_0)\subseteq W_0$ 的矩阵体现；反过来，矩阵若关于某组基呈这种形状，则前 $\dim W_0$ 个基向量张成的子空间是不变子空间。
rank-nullity.definitionEn:
Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear transformation over a number field. The **kernel** (null space) and **image** (range) are $$\ker T=\{\alpha\in V: T(\alpha)=\mathbf{0}\},\qquad \operatorname{Im}T=\{T(\alpha):\alpha\in V\}=T(V).$$ The kernel is a subspace of $V$ and the image is a subspace of $W$: the kernel contains the zero vector and is closed under $k\alpha+l\beta$ (whose image is zero), while for $u=T(\alpha)$ and $v=T(\beta)$ the combination $ku+lv=T(k\alpha+l\beta)$ is again an image.

**Rank–nullity theorem**: if $V$ is finite-dimensional and $T:V\to W$ is linear, then $$\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim V.$$ Here $\dim\operatorname{Im}T$ is the **rank** of $T$ and $\dim\ker T$ its **nullity**. Note that the right-hand side is the dimension of the **domain** $V$, not of $W$ — the most commonly misremembered point. Matrix form: an $m\times n$ matrix $A$ satisfies $\operatorname{rank}(A)+\operatorname{nullity}(A)=n$; viewing $A$ as $T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, $x\mapsto Ax$, the rank is $\dim\operatorname{Im}T$ and the solution space of $Ax=0$ is exactly $\ker T$, of dimension $n-\operatorname{rank}(A)$.

**Injectivity and surjectivity**: $T$ is injective iff $\ker T=\{\mathbf{0}\}$ (i.e. $Ax=0$ has only the trivial solution); $T$ is surjective iff $\operatorname{Im}T=W$ iff $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim W$; when $\dim V=\dim W<\infty$, injective, surjective and invertible (isomorphism) are all equivalent. Intuitively, the kernel measures how much information is crushed to zero, the image measures how much of the target is reached, and the two dimensions always add up to $\dim V$.

**Two models and invariant subspaces**: the projection $P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$ has kernel the $z$-axis (dimension 1) and image the $xy$-plane (dimension 2), and $1+2=3$; the derivative $D:P_n\to P_n$ has kernel the constant polynomials (dimension 1) and image the polynomials of degree at most $n-1$ (dimension $n$), and $1+n=n+1$. A subspace $W_0\subseteq V$ with $T(W_0)\subseteq W_0$ is called an **invariant subspace** of $T$; $\ker T$, $\operatorname{Im}T$ and eigenspaces are the standard examples. Extending a basis of $W_0$ to a basis of $V$ makes the matrix of $T$ **block upper triangular** $\begin{pmatrix}B&C\\O&D\end{pmatrix}$ (the entries below the first $\dim W_0$ columns vanish); conversely, a matrix of that shape with respect to some basis exhibits the span of the first $\dim W_0$ basis vectors as an invariant subspace.
derivation:
设 $V,W$ 是数域上的线性空间，$T:V\to W$ 线性。核与像定义为
$$\ker T=\{\alpha\in V:T(\alpha)=\boldsymbol{0}\},\qquad \operatorname{Im}T=\{T(\alpha):\alpha\in V\}.$$
核是 $V$ 的子空间：$T(\boldsymbol{0})=\boldsymbol{0}$，且 $T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=\boldsymbol{0}$。像是 $W$ 的子空间：$kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=T(k\alpha+l\beta)$ 仍是某个向量的像。$\dim\operatorname{Im}T$ 称为 $T$ 的秩，$\dim\ker T$ 称为零化度。

维数定理：若 $V$ 有限维，$\dim V=n$，则
$$\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n.$$
证明：设 $\dim\ker T=k$，取核的基 $u_1,\dots,u_k$，由基扩充定理把它扩充为 $V$ 的基 $u_1,\dots,u_k,v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$。先证 $T(v_1),\dots,T(v_{n-k})$ 张成 $\operatorname{Im}T$：任取 $T(x)$，写 $x=\sum a_i u_i+\sum b_j v_j$，则 $T(x)=\sum b_jT(v_j)$。再证它们无关：若 $\sum c_jT(v_j)=\boldsymbol{0}$，则 $T(\sum c_jv_j)=\boldsymbol{0}$，故 $\sum c_jv_j\in\ker T$，可写成 $\sum a_i u_i$；由 $V$ 的基无关性得所有 $c_j=0$。所以它们是 $\operatorname{Im}T$ 的基，$\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n-k$，定理成立。

矩阵版本是同一结论的坐标化。$m\times n$ 矩阵 $A$ 定义 $T_A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$，$T_A(\boldsymbol{x})=A\boldsymbol{x}$。此时 $\operatorname{Im}T_A=\{A\boldsymbol{x}:\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\}=\operatorname{Col}(A)$，故 $\dim\operatorname{Im}T_A=r(A)$；而 $\ker T_A=N(A)$ 正是齐次方程组的解空间。代入维数定理得
$$r(A)+\dim N(A)=n,\qquad \dim N(A)=n-r(A).$$
右边是 $n$（列数、未知数个数），不是 $m$（行数、方程个数）；这是最常见的记错点。

维数定理给出单射与满射的判别。$T$ 单射 $\iff\ker T=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$：若单射且 $T(\alpha)=0=T(0)$，则 $\alpha=0$；反之若核为零且 $T(\alpha)=T(\beta)$，则 $T(\alpha-\beta)=0$，故 $\alpha=\beta$。$T$ 满射 $\iff\operatorname{Im}T=W$，有限维时等价于 $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim W$。当 $\dim V=\dim W=n<\infty$ 时，结合 $\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n$ 得：单射 $\iff\dim\ker T=0\iff\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n\iff$ 满射 $\iff T$ 可逆。维数不同的有限维空间没有这个等价链：此时单射与满射一般不能互推。

两个模型可以直接核对。投影 $P:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$，$P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$：$\ker P=\{(0,0,z)\}$ 是 $z$ 轴，维数 1；$\operatorname{Im}P=\{(x,y,0)\}$ 是 $xy$ 平面，维数 2；$1+2=3=\dim\mathbb{R}^3$。求导 $D:P_n\to P_n$（$n\ge1$，$P_n$ 为次数不超过 $n$ 的多项式，维数 $n+1$）：$\ker D$ 是常数多项式，维数 1；$\operatorname{Im}D=P_{n-1}$，维数 $n$；$1+n=n+1$。两例都说明右边是定义域的维数，而不是到达域的维数。

最后看不变子空间与矩阵形状。若 $W_0\subseteq V$ 满足 $T(W_0)\subseteq W_0$，取 $W_0$ 的基 $w_1,\dots,w_k$ 并扩充为 $V$ 的基 $w_1,\dots,w_k,v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$。对 $j\le k$，$T(w_j)\in W_0$，故其在 $v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$ 方向的坐标全为零，矩阵的前 $k$ 列下方为零块，呈
$$\begin{pmatrix}B&C\\O&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
反之，若矩阵关于某组基呈此分块形状，则前 $k$ 个基向量张成的子空间在 $T$ 下不变。还要注意：维数定理的证明用了 $V$ 的有限基，无限维时不能直接套用，且单射与满射的等价链会失效；例如右移算子 $(x_1,x_2,\dots)\mapsto(0,x_1,x_2,\dots)$ 单射但不满射，左移算子满射但不单射。
derivationEn:
Let $V,W$ be vector spaces over a field and $T:V\to W$ linear. The kernel and image are
$$\ker T=\{\alpha\in V:T(\alpha)=\boldsymbol{0}\},\qquad \operatorname{Im}T=\{T(\alpha):\alpha\in V\}.$$
The kernel is a subspace of $V$: $T(\boldsymbol{0})=\boldsymbol{0}$, and $T(k\alpha+l\beta)=kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=\boldsymbol{0}$. The image is a subspace of $W$: $kT(\alpha)+lT(\beta)=T(k\alpha+l\beta)$ is again an image. The number $\dim\operatorname{Im}T$ is the rank of $T$ and $\dim\ker T$ is its nullity.

Rank–nullity theorem: if $V$ is finite-dimensional with $\dim V=n$, then
$$\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n.$$
Proof: let $\dim\ker T=k$ and take a basis $u_1,\dots,u_k$ of the kernel; extend it by the basis extension theorem to a basis $u_1,\dots,u_k,v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$ of $V$. First, $T(v_1),\dots,T(v_{n-k})$ span $\operatorname{Im}T$: for $T(x)$ write $x=\sum a_i u_i+\sum b_j v_j$, then $T(x)=\sum b_jT(v_j)$. Second, they are independent: if $\sum c_jT(v_j)=\boldsymbol{0}$, then $T(\sum c_jv_j)=\boldsymbol{0}$, so $\sum c_jv_j\in\ker T$ and equals $\sum a_i u_i$; independence of the basis of $V$ forces all $c_j=0$. Hence they form a basis of $\operatorname{Im}T$, so $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n-k$ and the theorem follows.

The matrix version is the same statement in coordinates. An $m\times n$ matrix $A$ defines $T_A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, $T_A(\boldsymbol{x})=A\boldsymbol{x}$. Here $\operatorname{Im}T_A=\{A\boldsymbol{x}:\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\}=\operatorname{Col}(A)$, so $\dim\operatorname{Im}T_A=r(A)$, while $\ker T_A=N(A)$ is exactly the solution space of the homogeneous system. Substituting into the theorem gives
$$r(A)+\dim N(A)=n,\qquad \dim N(A)=n-r(A).$$
The right-hand side is $n$ (the number of columns and unknowns), not $m$ (the number of rows and equations); this is the most common point to misremember.

The theorem yields tests for injectivity and surjectivity. $T$ is injective iff $\ker T=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$: if $T$ is injective and $T(\alpha)=0=T(0)$, then $\alpha=0$; conversely, if the kernel is zero and $T(\alpha)=T(\beta)$, then $T(\alpha-\beta)=0$, so $\alpha=\beta$. $T$ is surjective iff $\operatorname{Im}T=W$, which in finite dimension is equivalent to $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim W$. When $\dim V=\dim W=n<\infty$, combining this with $\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n$ gives: injective $\iff\dim\ker T=0\iff\dim\operatorname{Im}T=n\iff$ surjective $\iff T$ invertible. For finite-dimensional spaces of different dimensions this chain fails: injectivity and surjectivity no longer imply each other.

Two models confirm the bookkeeping. The projection $P:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$, $P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$: $\ker P=\{(0,0,z)\}$ is the $z$-axis of dimension 1; $\operatorname{Im}P=\{(x,y,0)\}$ is the $xy$-plane of dimension 2; $1+2=3=\dim\mathbb{R}^3$. The derivative $D:P_n\to P_n$ ($n\ge1$; polynomials of degree at most $n$, dimension $n+1$): $\ker D$ is the constant polynomials, dimension 1; $\operatorname{Im}D=P_{n-1}$, dimension $n$; $1+n=n+1$. Both examples show that the right-hand side is the dimension of the domain, not of the codomain.

Finally, invariant subspaces and matrix shape. If $W_0\subseteq V$ satisfies $T(W_0)\subseteq W_0$, take a basis $w_1,\dots,w_k$ of $W_0$ and extend it to a basis $w_1,\dots,w_k,v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$ of $V$. For $j\le k$, $T(w_j)\in W_0$, so its coordinates in the $v_1,\dots,v_{n-k}$ directions all vanish; the first $k$ columns of the matrix therefore have a zero block below, giving
$$\begin{pmatrix}B&C\\O&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
Conversely, if the matrix has this block form with respect to some basis, the span of the first $k$ basis vectors is invariant under $T$. Note also that the proof of the dimension theorem uses a finite basis of $V$; in infinite dimension it cannot be applied directly, and the equivalence of injectivity and surjectivity fails: the right shift $(x_1,x_2,\dots)\mapsto(0,x_1,x_2,\dots)$ is injective but not surjective, while the left shift is surjective but not injective.

formulas.note: 核与像的定义；核是 V 的子空间，像是 W 的子空间。
formulas.noteEn: Definitions of kernel and image; the kernel is a subspace of V and the image a subspace of W.

formulas.note: 维数定理（秩零化度定理）：右边恒为定义域 V 的维数，与 W 的维数无关。
formulas.noteEn: The rank–nullity theorem: the right-hand side is always dim V, the dimension of the domain, independent of W.

formulas.note: 矩阵版本：rank 是像的维数，nullity 是 Ax = 0 解空间的维数，两数之和等于未知数个数 n。
formulas.noteEn: Matrix version for an m×n matrix A: rank is the dimension of the image and nullity the dimension of the solution space of Ax = 0; the two add up to the number of unknowns n.

formulas.latex: T\ \text{单射}\iff\ker T=\{\mathbf{0}\},\qquad T\ \text{满射}\iff\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim W
formulas.note: 单射与满射判别；在 dim V = dim W 的有限维情形，单射、满射、可逆三者等价。
formulas.noteEn: Tests for injectivity and surjectivity; for finite-dimensional V, W with dim V = dim W the three notions injective, surjective, invertible coincide.

formulas.latex: T(W_0)\subseteq W_0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A\ \text{在适当基下为}\ \begin{pmatrix}B&C\\O&D\end{pmatrix}
formulas.note: 不变子空间与分块上三角：取 W₀ 的基再扩充为 V 的基，前 dim W₀ 列的下方为零块；反之亦然。
formulas.noteEn: Invariant subspaces and block upper triangular form: extend a basis of W₀ to a basis of V and the lower block below the first dim W₀ columns vanishes; the converse also holds.

properties: ker T 与 Im T 都是子空间，分别落在定义域 V 与到达域 W 中。
维数定理：dim ker T + dim Im T = dim V；由此自动有 dim Im T ≤ min(dim V, dim W) 与 dim Im T = dim V − dim ker T。
T 单射 ⟺ ker T = {0}；T 满射 ⟺ dim Im T = dim W；有限维且 dim V = dim W 时，单射、满射、可逆三者互相等价。
对矩阵 A：rank(A) = dim Im T = 列空间的维数；Ax = 0 的解空间维数 = n − rank(A)；当 Ax = b 相容时，解集是「特解 + 齐次解空间」的仿射集。
不变子空间：T(W₀) ⊆ W₀；取 W₀ 的基扩充为全空间的基后矩阵为分块上三角，反之分块上三角矩阵对应一个不变子空间；特征子空间是不变子空间的最典型例子。
propertiesEn: ker T and Im T are subspaces, living in the domain V and the codomain W respectively.
Rank–nullity: dim ker T + dim Im T = dim V; hence dim Im T ≤ min(dim V, dim W) and dim Im T = dim V − dim ker T.
T is injective iff ker T = {0}; T is surjective iff dim Im T = dim W; for finite-dimensional spaces with dim V = dim W, injective, surjective and invertible are equivalent.

For a matrix A: rank(A) = dim Im T = dimension of the column space; the solution space of Ax = 0 has dimension n − rank(A); if Ax = b is consistent, its solution set is the affine set obtained by adding the solution space to any particular solution.

Invariant subspace: T(W₀) ⊆ W₀; extending a basis of W₀ to the whole space gives a block upper triangular matrix, and conversely such a block matrix exhibits an invariant subspace; eigenspaces are the archetypal examples.

examples.problem: 设投影 $P:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$，$P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)$。求 $\ker P$、$\operatorname{Im}P$ 及其维数，验证维数定理，并写出 $P$ 在标准基下的矩阵及其秩。
examples.solution: 解方程 $P(x,y,z)=(0,0,0)$ 得 $x=y=0$、$z$ 任意，故 $\ker P=\{(0,0,z): z\in\mathbb{R}\}=\operatorname{span}\{e_3\}$，$\dim\ker P=1$。像由全体 $(x,y,0)$ 组成，即 $xy$ 平面，$\operatorname{Im}P=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,e_2\}$，$\dim\operatorname{Im}P=2$。于是 $\dim\ker P+\dim\operatorname{Im}P=1+2=3=\dim\mathbb{R}^3$，维数定理成立。$P$ 在标准基下的矩阵为 $A=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,0)$，其秩 $\operatorname{rank}(A)=2=\dim\operatorname{Im}P$。$P$ 既不是单射（$(0,0,1)\mapsto\mathbf{0}$，核非零）也不是满射（$z$ 方向的向量取不到）。

examples.problem: 设 $A$ 是 $4\times 5$ 矩阵，$\operatorname{rank}(A)=3$。求齐次方程组 $Ax=0$ 解空间的维数；并说明 $Ax=b$ 是否有解能否由这些信息判定；若某个 $b$ 使方程组相容，解集是几维的？
examples.solution: 把 $A$ 看成线性变换 $T:\mathbb{R}^5\to\mathbb{R}^4$，$x\mapsto Ax$，$Ax=0$ 的解空间就是 $\ker T$。由维数定理，$\dim\ker T=5-\dim\operatorname{Im}T=5-\operatorname{rank}(A)=5-3=2$，即解空间是 2 维的（通解含 2 个自由参数）。至于 $Ax=b$：满射要求 $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\dim\mathbb{R}^4=4$，但 $\dim\operatorname{Im}T=\operatorname{rank}(A)=3<4$，所以 $T$ 不满射，必存在使 $Ax=b$ 无解的 $b$——是否相容取决于 $b$ 是否落在 $A$ 的列空间中，无法仅凭秩判定。若某个 $b$ 使方程组相容，则解集为 $\{x_0+\xi: \xi\in\ker T\}$（特解加 2 维解空间），是 2 维仿射子空间，仍含 2 个自由参数。

jordan-form.definition:
对角化失败的根源是特征向量不够用：例如 $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ 只有一维特征子空间。若尔当标准型把「对角」放宽为「准对角」。$k$ 阶**若尔当块**定义为 $$J_k(\lambda)=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&1&&\\&\lambda&\ddots&\\&&\ddots&1\\&&&\lambda\end{pmatrix}_{k\times k},$$ 即主对角元全为 $\lambda$、**上副对角线**（主对角线正上方紧邻的那条对角线，第 $i$ 行第 $i+1$ 列）全为 1、其余全为 0。**约定说明**：本库统一采用「1 放在上副对角线」的约定；有些教材把 1 放在下副对角线，两者互为转置，做任何具体计算时都不能混用。

**若尔当标准型定理**：设 $A$ 是 $n$ 阶**复**矩阵，则存在可逆矩阵 $P$，使 $$P^{-1}AP=J=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(J_{k_1}(\lambda_1),\dots,J_{k_r}(\lambda_r)\bigr),\qquad k_1+\cdots+k_r=n,$$ 其中 $\lambda_i$ 是 $A$ 的特征值（可以重复；同一特征值出现的次数等于它对应的若尔当块个数）。不计块的排列次序时 $J$ 由 $A$ 唯一确定。**存在性与域有关，表述必须严谨**：在复数域上，任意方阵都相似于若尔当标准型（复特征多项式总能完全分解）；在实数域上，只有当 $A$ 的特征值全为实数时才保证有实过渡矩阵的实若尔当形，否则要到复空间去求，或改用「实若尔当形」（复特征值用 2×2 的旋转—伸缩块代替）。

**块的结构怎么数**：对特征值 $\lambda$，$J$ 中 $\lambda$ 的若尔当块个数等于几何重数 $$\#\{\lambda\ \text{的若尔当块}\}=n-r(\lambda E-A)=\dim\ker(\lambda E-A),$$ 各块阶数之和等于 $\lambda$ 的代数重数（$|\lambda E-A|=0$ 中 $\lambda$ 的重数）；若尔当块的总数等于 $A$ 的线性无关特征向量的总数。于是 $A$ 可对角化 $\iff$ 每个特征值的若尔当块全是一阶 $\iff$ 对每个 $\lambda$ 都有 $n-r(\lambda E-A)$ 等于代数重数。特别地，$n$ 个互不相同的特征值一定保证可对角化；不可对角化时，用 $(\lambda E-A)^2$ 等的秩还能进一步分出 2 阶及以上块的个数。

**怎么用**：若尔当基由特征向量与广义特征向量链组成——对属于 $J_k(\lambda)$ 的块，取向量链 $p_1,\dots,p_k$ 满足 $(A-\lambda E)p_1=\mathbf{0}$、$(A-\lambda E)p_{j+1}=p_j$（$j=1,\dots,k-1$），把这些列排成 $P$ 就有 $P^{-1}AP=J$。若尔当型让矩阵幂与矩阵指数有显式公式（$A^m=PJ^mP^{-1}$、$\mathrm e^{tA}=P\,\mathrm e^{tJ}P^{-1}$），是求解线性微分方程组 $\frac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}=Ax$、分析幂零部分的标准工具。
jordan-form.definitionEn:
Diagonalization fails when there are too few eigenvectors: e.g. $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ has a one-dimensional eigenspace. The Jordan form relaxes diagonal to almost diagonal. The **Jordan block** of order $k$ is $$J_k(\lambda)=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&1&&\\&\lambda&\ddots&\\&&\ddots&1\\&&&\lambda\end{pmatrix}_{k\times k},$$ with $\lambda$ on the main diagonal, 1's on the **superdiagonal** (the diagonal immediately above the main one, entry $(i,i+1)$) and 0's elsewhere. **Convention**: this library always puts the 1's on the superdiagonal; some textbooks use the subdiagonal instead, which is just the transpose — never mix the two in a computation.

**Jordan normal form theorem**: for every $n\times n$ **complex** matrix $A$ there is an invertible $P$ with $$P^{-1}AP=J=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(J_{k_1}(\lambda_1),\dots,J_{k_r}(\lambda_r)\bigr),\qquad k_1+\cdots+k_r=n,$$ where the $\lambda_i$ are the eigenvalues of $A$ (possibly repeated; the number of occurrences of an eigenvalue equals the number of its Jordan blocks). The form $J$ is unique up to reordering the blocks. **Existence depends on the field, so the statement must be precise**: over $\mathbb{C}$ every matrix has a Jordan form (the characteristic polynomial splits); over $\mathbb{R}$ a real Jordan form with a real transition matrix is guaranteed only when all eigenvalues are real — otherwise one passes to the complexification or uses a real Jordan form whose complex eigenvalues appear as $2\times2$ rotation-dilation blocks.

**Counting the blocks**: for an eigenvalue $\lambda$, the number of Jordan blocks of $\lambda$ equals the geometric multiplicity $$\#\{\text{Jordan blocks of}\ \lambda\}=n-r(\lambda E-A)=\dim\ker(\lambda E-A),$$ and the sizes of those blocks sum to the algebraic multiplicity of $\lambda$ (its multiplicity as a root of $|\lambda E-A|=0$); the total number of Jordan blocks equals the number of linearly independent eigenvectors of $A$. Hence $A$ is diagonalizable iff every Jordan block has order 1 iff $n-r(\lambda E-A)$ equals the algebraic multiplicity for each $\lambda$. In particular, $n$ distinct eigenvalues always give diagonalizability; when $A$ is not diagonalizable, ranks of $(\lambda E-A)^2$ and higher powers resolve the numbers of blocks of order 2 and above.

**How it is used**: a Jordan basis consists of eigenvectors together with chains of generalized eigenvectors — for a block $J_k(\lambda)$ take $p_1,\dots,p_k$ with $(A-\lambda E)p_1=\mathbf{0}$ and $(A-\lambda E)p_{j+1}=p_j$ for $j=1,\dots,k-1$, and arrange them as the columns of $P$ to obtain $P^{-1}AP=J$. The Jordan form yields explicit formulas for powers and exponentials ($A^m=PJ^mP^{-1}$, $\mathrm e^{tA}=P\,\mathrm e^{tJ}P^{-1}$), the standard tool for linear ODE systems $\frac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}=Ax$ and for analyzing the nilpotent part.
derivation: 对角化失败的根源是特征向量不够。$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ 的特征多项式为 $(\lambda-1)^2$，但 $r(A-E)=1$，几何重数 $2-1=1<2$，凑不齐两个线性无关特征向量。若尔当块把「对角」放宽为「准对角」：$$J_k(\lambda)=\lambda E_k+N_k,$$ 其中 $N_k$ 的上副对角线全为 $1$、其余为 $0$。直接计算可知 $N_k^j$ 把 $1$ 移到第 $j$ 条上副对角线，故 $N_k^k=O$，且 $j<k$ 时 $N_k^j\neq O$。

若尔当标准型定理：设 $A$ 是 $n$ 阶复矩阵，则存在可逆 $P$ 使 $$P^{-1}AP=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(J_{k_1}(\lambda_1),\dots,J_{k_r}(\lambda_r)\bigr),$$ 且 $k_1+\cdots+k_r=n$；不计块的排列次序时 $J$ 唯一。存在性思路：对每个互异特征值 $\lambda$，广义特征子空间 $G_\lambda=\ker((A-\lambda E)^n)$ 是 $A$-不变的，且 $\mathbb{C}^n=\oplus_\lambda G_\lambda$；在 $G_\lambda$ 上 $A-\lambda E$ 幂零，幂零算子的循环链分解给出若干块 $J_k(\lambda)$。在实数域上，若特征值不全为实，需用复过渡矩阵，或改用含 $2\times2$ 旋转—伸缩块的实若尔当形。

链与矩阵：若 $p_1,\dots,p_k$ 满足 $$(A-\lambda E)p_1=0,\qquad (A-\lambda E)p_{j+1}=p_j\ (1\le j<k),$$ 且 $p_1\ne0$，令 $p_0=0$，则 $Ap_j=\lambda p_j+p_{j-1}$。于是 $$A(p_1,\dots,p_k)=(p_1,\dots,p_k)J_k(\lambda):$$ 第 $1$ 列给出 $Ap_1=\lambda p_1$，第 $j$ 列给出 $Ap_j=\lambda p_j+p_{j-1}$，正好是对角元 $\lambda$ 与上副对角线 $1$。这些 $p_j$ 线性无关：若相关，取最小的 $j$ 使 $p_j$ 可由 $p_1,\dots,p_{j-1}$ 表示，作用 $(A-\lambda E)^{j-1}$ 得 $p_1=0$，与 $p_1\ne0$ 矛盾。

块数公式：在若尔当形 $J$ 中，每个 $k$ 阶块满足 $J_k(\lambda)-\lambda E=N_k$，其核为 $\operatorname{span}(e_1)$，一维；特征值不同的块 $J_k(\mu)-\lambda E$（$\mu\neq\lambda$）可逆。因此 $$\dim\ker(J-\lambda E)=\lambda\ \text{的若尔当块个数}.$$ 相似保持核的维数，故 $$\#\{\lambda\ \text{的块}\}=n-r(\lambda E-A)=g_\lambda,$$ 即块数等于几何重数。又 $f_J(\lambda')=\prod_i(\lambda'-\lambda_i)^{k_i}$，故各块阶数之和等于 $\lambda$ 的代数重数；块的总数等于线性无关特征向量的总数。

可对角化判据：$$A\ \text{可对角化}\iff\text{所有若尔当块为 }1\text{ 阶}\iff g_\lambda=m_\lambda\ (\forall\lambda).$$ 特别地，$n$ 个互异特征值使 $m_\lambda=1$，而 $g_\lambda\ge1$，故必可对角化。例：$A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$，$f_A=(\lambda-2)^2$，$r(A-2E)=1$，故 $\lambda=2$ 的块数为 $2-1=1$，只能是一个 $2$ 阶块 $J_2(2)$。取 $p_1=(1,1)^T$ 解 $(A-2E)p_1=0$，$(A-2E)(1,0)^T=(1,1)^T$，取 $p_2=(1,0)^T$；令 $P=(p_1,p_2)$，则 $AP=PJ_2(2)$。

幂与指数：$J_k(\lambda)=\lambda E+N$，$N^k=O$，且 $\lambda E$ 与 $N$ 交换，故二项式展开有效。对 $m\ge k$，$$J_k(\lambda)^m=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{m}{i}\lambda^{m-i}N^i,$$ 而 $$e^{tJ_k(\lambda)}=e^{\lambda t}\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\frac{t^i}{i!}N^i.$$ 于是 $A^m=PJ^mP^{-1}$、$e^{tA}=Pe^{tJ}P^{-1}$；指数中出现 $t^ie^{\lambda t}$ 型项，正是不可对角化时 $\dot x=Ax$ 解的特征。注意这些公式依赖复若尔当形；实矩阵若需实运算，应使用实若尔当形。
derivationEn: The failure of diagonalization comes from too few eigenvectors. For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, the characteristic polynomial is $(\lambda-1)^2$, but $r(A-E)=1$, so the geometric multiplicity is $2-1=1<2$ and there are not two independent eigenvectors. A Jordan block relaxes 'diagonal' to 'almost diagonal': $$J_k(\lambda)=\lambda E_k+N_k,$$ where $N_k$ has $1$'s on the superdiagonal and $0$'s elsewhere. A direct computation shows that $N_k^j$ moves the $1$'s to the $j$-th superdiagonal, so $N_k^k=O$ and $N_k^j\neq O$ for $j<k$.

Jordan normal form theorem: for every $n\times n$ complex matrix $A$ there is an invertible $P$ with $$P^{-1}AP=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(J_{k_1}(\lambda_1),\dots,J_{k_r}(\lambda_r)\bigr),$$ where $k_1+\cdots+k_r=n$; the form is unique up to the order of the blocks. Idea of existence: for each distinct eigenvalue $\lambda$, the generalized eigenspace $G_\lambda=\ker((A-\lambda E)^n)$ is $A$-invariant and $\mathbb{C}^n=\oplus_\lambda G_\lambda$; on $G_\lambda$ the operator $A-\lambda E$ is nilpotent, and the cyclic-chain decomposition of a nilpotent operator yields blocks $J_k(\lambda)$. Over $\mathbb{R}$, if not all eigenvalues are real, one needs a complex transition matrix or a real Jordan form with $2\times2$ rotation-dilation blocks.

Chains and matrices: if $p_1,\dots,p_k$ satisfy $$(A-\lambda E)p_1=0,\qquad (A-\lambda E)p_{j+1}=p_j\ (1\le j<k),$$ and $p_1\ne0$, then with $p_0=0$ we have $Ap_j=\lambda p_j+p_{j-1}$. Hence $$A(p_1,\dots,p_k)=(p_1,\dots,p_k)J_k(\lambda):$$ the first column gives $Ap_1=\lambda p_1$, and the $j$-th column gives $Ap_j=\lambda p_j+p_{j-1}$, exactly the diagonal $\lambda$ and superdiagonal $1$. The $p_j$ are linearly independent: if they were dependent, take the least $j$ with $p_j$ in the span of $p_1,\dots,p_{j-1}$ and apply $(A-\lambda E)^{j-1}$ to get $p_1=0$, contradicting $p_1\ne0$.

Counting blocks: in a Jordan form $J$, each block satisfies $J_k(\lambda)-\lambda E=N_k$, whose kernel is $\operatorname{span}(e_1)$, one-dimensional; a block $J_k(\mu)-\lambda E$ with $\mu\neq\lambda$ is invertible. Therefore $$\dim\ker(J-\lambda E)=\text{the number of Jordan blocks of }\lambda.$$ Similarity preserves kernel dimension, so $$\#\{\text{blocks of }\lambda\}=n-r(\lambda E-A)=g_\lambda,$$ the geometric multiplicity. Also $f_J(\lambda')=\prod_i(\lambda'-\lambda_i)^{k_i}$, so the block sizes sum to the algebraic multiplicity of $\lambda$, and the total number of blocks equals the number of linearly independent eigenvectors.

Diagonalizability criterion: $$A\ \text{is diagonalizable}\iff\text{all Jordan blocks have order }1\iff g_\lambda=m_\lambda\ (\forall\lambda).$$ In particular, $n$ distinct eigenvalues give $m_\lambda=1$ while $g_\lambda\ge1$, so diagonalizability is automatic.
