Either alternative contradicts Perron's theorem for the positive matrix $A^k$ (unique and simple). Hence $h=1$. Primitivity is sufficient; for irreducible matrices it is in fact equivalent to a single-point peripheral spectrum. Without irreducibility it is not necessary: $\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ is not primitive yet has the unique dominant eigenvalue $1$. An irreducible but non-primitive example is the permutation matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, whose eigenvalues $1,-1$ both have modulus $\rho=1$.

Example: $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\3&1\end{pmatrix}$. Its characteristic polynomial is $\lambda^2-\lambda-6=(\lambda-3)(\lambda+2)$, so the eigenvalues are $3,-2$ and $\rho(A)=3$. Solving $(A-3I)x=0$ gives $-3x_1+2x_2=0$; take $x=(2,3)^{\mathsf T}\ge0$ and check $A(2,3)^{\mathsf T}=(6,9)^{\mathsf T}=3(2,3)^{\mathsf T}$. The directed graph of $A$ is strongly connected ($1\leftrightarrow2$, with a loop $2\to2$), so $A$ is irreducible; $A^2=\begin{pmatrix}6&2\\3&7\end{pmatrix}>0$, so $A$ is primitive. Hence $\rho=3$ is a simple eigenvalue, the Perron vector is strictly positive and unique up to a positive multiple, and the other eigenvalue $-2$ satisfies $|-2|=2<3$, consistent with the strict inequality in the primitive case.

Applications and limits. A row-stochastic matrix has row sums $1$, so $A\boldsymbol 1=\boldsymbol 1$ and $\rho(A)=1$; for a column-stochastic matrix, $\boldsymbol 1^{\mathsf T}A=\boldsymbol 1^{\mathsf T}$, and the all-ones vector is a left eigenvector. An irreducible row-stochastic matrix has a unique stationary distribution, obtained from the left eigenvector equation $\pi^{\mathsf T}A=\pi^{\mathsf T}$, not the right eigenvector equation; the two directions must not be mixed. Monotonicity: $0\le B\le A$ entrywise implies $\rho(B)\le\rho(A)$. If $A\ge0$ is primitive, then $\rho^{-k}A^k$ converges to the rank-one matrix $xy^{\mathsf T}$, where $Ax=\rho x$, $y^{\mathsf T}A=\rho y^{\mathsf T}$ and $y^{\mathsf T}x=1$; also $A^k\to0\iff\rho(A)<1$. Finally, the statement that $\rho(A)$ is an eigenvalue holds for nonnegative matrices but cannot be extended to general real matrices (the $90^\circ$ rotation in Step 1 is a counterexample).

formulas.latex: A\ge 0,\ A\ne 0\ \Longrightarrow\ \rho(A)\ \text{是 }A\text{ 的特征值},\qquad \exists\, x\ge 0,\ x\ne 0:\ Ax=\rho(A)x
formulas.note: Perron–Frobenius 最基础的形式：非负矩阵的谱半径一定是特征值，且总有非负特征向量（允许有零分量）。这是「非负」才有的结论。
formulas.noteEn: The most basic form of Perron–Frobenius: the spectral radius of a nonnegative matrix is an eigenvalue, and a nonnegative eigenvector (zeros allowed) always exists. This conclusion is special to nonnegativity.

formulas.latex: A\ge0\ \text{不可约}\ \Longrightarrow\ \rho(A)>0,\qquad Ax=\rho(A)x\ \text{有严格正解 } x>0,\ \text{且解在不计正倍数下唯一},\ \rho(A)\ \text{是单特征值}
formulas.note: 不可约情形：Perron 向量严格为正且唯一（不计正倍数），$\rho(A)$ 的代数重数为 1。可约矩阵没有这些保证（单位矩阵 $I$ 的 $\rho=1$ 重数就是 $n$）。
formulas.noteEn: The irreducible case: the Perron vector is strictly positive and unique up to a positive multiple, and $\rho(A)$ has algebraic multiplicity one. Reducible matrices offer no such guarantees — the identity matrix has $\rho=1$ with multiplicity $n$.

formulas.note: 行随机矩阵：全 1 向量是右特征向量，$A\boldsymbol{1}=\boldsymbol{1}$；列随机矩阵：全 1 向量是左特征向量。方向别混——它决定了平稳分布是行向量还是列向量。
formulas.noteEn: Row-stochastic: the all-ones vector is a right eigenvector, $A\boldsymbol{1}=\boldsymbol{1}$; column-stochastic: it is a left eigenvector. Do not swap the two — the direction determines whether the stationary distribution is stored as a row or a column.

formulas.latex: \exists\, k\ge1:\ A^k>0\ \Longrightarrow\ \rho(A)\ \text{是唯一满足 } |\lambda|=\rho(A)\ \text{的特征值},\qquad \lambda\ne\rho(A)\Rightarrow |\lambda|<\rho(A)
formulas.note: 本原矩阵的加强结论（「唯一模长最大」）。本原性是充分条件而非必要：不可约但非本原时，模长等于 $\rho$ 的特征值可以按单位根成组出现，例如置换矩阵。
formulas.noteEn: The sharpened primitive case: a unique dominant eigenvalue. Primitivity is sufficient but not necessary; an irreducible but imprimitive matrix may have several eigenvalues of modulus $\rho$ placed at roots of unity, as permutation matrices do.

formulas.note: Collatz–Wielandt 公式：给谱半径一个可计算的变分刻画，任意正向量 $x$ 的「最大比值」都是 $\rho$ 的上界，「最小比值」都是下界，也是幂法估计 $\rho$ 的基础。
formulas.noteEn: The Collatz–Wielandt formula: a computable variational characterization of $\rho$. For any positive $x$, the maximal ratio bounds $\rho$ above and the minimal ratio bounds it below; this underlies power-iteration estimation of $\rho$.

properties: 对任意实方阵都有 $|\lambda|\le\rho(A)$；但「$\rho(A)$ 是特征值」只对非负矩阵保证——平面旋转 $90^\circ$ 的矩阵特征值为 $\pm i$，$\rho=1$ 不是特征值。不要把这条结论推广到一般矩阵。
不可约非负矩阵：$\rho>0$ 是单特征值，Perron 向量严格正且在不计正倍数下唯一；可约非负矩阵可以没有正特征向量，$\rho$ 的重数可以大于 1（如 $I$）。
行随机的非负矩阵满足 $A\boldsymbol{1}=\boldsymbol{1}$，故 $\rho=1$ 是特征值；不可约时平稳分布唯一，它就是列侧的左特征向量（$\pi^{\mathsf T}A=\pi^{\mathsf T}$，链接 markov-chain 与 stationary-distribution）。行和 1 给右特征向量、列和 1 给左特征向量，两个方向不能互换。
单调性：$0\le B\le A$（逐元素）蕴含 $\rho(B)\le\rho(A)$，即矩阵元素变大，谱半径不会变小。
极限与秩一收敛：$A\ge0$ 时 $A^k\to0$ 当且仅当 $\rho(A)<1$；若 $A$ 本原，则 $\rho^{-k}A^k$ 收敛到秩一矩阵 $xy^{\mathsf T}$，其中 $Ax=\rho x$、$y^{\mathsf T}A=\rho y^{\mathsf T}$、$y^{\mathsf T}x=1$——这是幂法与 PageRank 收敛性的依据。
propertiesEn: Every real square matrix satisfies $|\lambda|\le\rho(A)$, but the statement 「$\rho(A)$ is an eigenvalue」 is guaranteed only for nonnegative matrices: the $90^\circ$ rotation has eigenvalues $\pm i$ and $\rho=1$ is not one of them. Do not generalize this to arbitrary matrices.

For an irreducible nonnegative matrix: $\rho>0$ is a simple eigenvalue and the Perron vector is strictly positive and unique up to a positive multiple. For a reducible nonnegative matrix there may be no positive eigenvector, and $\rho$ can have multiplicity greater than one (take $I$).

A row-stochastic nonnegative matrix satisfies $A\boldsymbol{1}=\boldsymbol{1}$, so $\rho=1$ is an eigenvalue; when it is irreducible the stationary distribution is unique and equals the left eigenvector on the column side ($\pi^{\mathsf T}A=\pi^{\mathsf T}$, see markov-chain and stationary-distribution). Row sums give the right eigenvector, column sums the left one; the two cannot be interchanged.
Monotonicity: $0\le B\le A$ entrywise implies $\rho(B)\le\rho(A)$; enlarging entries never decreases the spectral radius.

Limits and rank-one convergence: for $A\ge0$, $A^k\to0$ if and only if $\rho(A)<1$; if $A$ is primitive then $\rho^{-k}A^k$ converges to the rank-one matrix $xy^{\mathsf T}$, where $Ax=\rho x$, $y^{\mathsf T}A=\rho y^{\mathsf T}$ and $y^{\mathsf T}x=1$ — the basis for the convergence of the power method and PageRank.

examples.problem: 设 $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\3&1\end{pmatrix}$。验证谱半径 $\rho(A)$ 是 $A$ 的特征值，求一个非负特征向量，并把另一个特征值的模长与 $\rho$ 比较。
examples.solution:
特征多项式：$\det(A-\lambda I)=\lambda^2-\lambda-6=(\lambda-3)(\lambda+2)$，特征值为 $3$ 与 $-2$，故 $\rho(A)=3$，它确实是特征值（Perron–Frobenius）✓。
求特征向量：$A-3I=\begin{pmatrix}-3&2\\3&-2\end{pmatrix}$，方程 $-3x_1+2x_2=0$，取 $x=(2,3)^{\mathsf T}\ge0$。代回验证：$A\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0\cdot2+2\cdot3\\3\cdot2+1\cdot3\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\9\end{pmatrix}=3\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}$ ✓。
另一特征值 $-2$ 的模长为 $2\le3=\rho(A)$ ✓，符合 $|\lambda|\le\rho$；并且 $A>0$ 从而本原，$\rho$ 是唯一模长最大的特征值，$|-2|=2<3$ 与此一致。

examples.problem: 设 $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1&1\\1&2&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}=I+J$（$J$ 为三阶全 1 矩阵）。求 $\rho(A)$ 并给出非负特征向量；说明 $A/4$ 是行随机矩阵，其平稳分布是什么。
examples.solution:
因 $J^2=3J$，$J$ 的特征值为 $3,0,0$（$3$ 对应向量 $(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}$），而 $A=I+J$ 与 $J$ 可交换、同时对角化，故 $A$ 的特征值为 $1+3=4$ 与 $1+0=1$（二重），$\rho(A)=4$ 是特征值 ✓。直接验证：$A\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2+1+1\\1+2+1\\1+1+2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\4\\4\end{pmatrix}=4\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}$ ✓，故 $(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}$ 是严格正特征向量；由于 $A>0$ 不可约，它在不计正倍数下唯一。
$A$ 每行和为 4，故 $A/4$ 每行和为 1，是行随机矩阵，其特征值为 $1,\tfrac14,\tfrac14$，$\rho(A/4)=1$。由 $\pi^{\mathsf T}(A/4)=\pi^{\mathsf T}$（列侧左特征向量）解得均匀平稳分布 $\pi=(\tfrac13,\tfrac13,\tfrac13)$——行随机矩阵的方向是 $A\boldsymbol{1}=\boldsymbol{1}$，平稳分布则解左特征方程，两者方向不同。又因 $A$ 本原，除 $4$ 之外的特征值模长 $1$ 严格小于 $4$，与定理的加强结论一致。

quotient-space.definition:
设 $V$ 是域 $K$ 上的线性空间，$W\le V$ 是一个子空间。对每个向量 $\alpha\in V$，集合 $\alpha+W=\{\alpha+w:\ w\in W\}$ 称为一个**陪集**，几何上就是「过 $\alpha$ 且平行于 $W$」的仿射平层。全体陪集组成的集合记作 $V/W$，称为 $V$ 关于 $W$ 的**商空间**。直观上，商空间就是把 $W$ 方向的信息整体「压扁成一个点」之后得到的空间，这正好与子空间的方向形成互补。

要在 $V/W$ 上定义加法与数乘：$(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=(\alpha+\beta)+W$，$k(\alpha+W)=k\alpha+W$。这里最关键的一步是**良定义性**——陪集有多个代表元，必须验证换用 $\alpha'=\alpha+w_1$、$\beta'=\beta+w_2$ 后结果不变：$(\alpha'+W)+(\beta'+W)=(\alpha+w_1+\beta+w_2)+W=(\alpha+\beta)+W$，因为 $w_1+w_2\in W$；同理 $k\alpha'=k\alpha+kw_1$，而 $kw_1\in W$。验证完毕，$V/W$ 才真正成为一个线性空间。这一步不能省，它是商空间理论全部的技术难点所在。

两个陪集何时相等有简单的判别法：$\alpha+W=\beta+W\iff\alpha-\beta\in W$。由此得维数公式 $\dim(V/W)=\dim V-\dim W$（有限维情形）：陪集的自由度恰好由 $W$ 之外的方向提供。**自然投影** $\pi:V\to V/W$、$\pi(\alpha)=\alpha+W$ 是满射线性映射，且 $\ker\pi=W$——商空间是「恰好抹掉 $W$」的典范构造。

**第一同构定理**：对任意线性映射 $T:V\to Y$ 都有 $V/\ker T\cong\operatorname{Im}T$，同构由 $\bar\alpha\mapsto T(\alpha)$ 给出（良定义性同样来自 $\ker T$ 的定义）。它把线性方程组的结构说得很清楚：映射 $x\mapsto Ax$ 诱导 $K^n/\ker A\cong\operatorname{Im}A$，而 $Ax=b$ 的解集是 $\ker A$ 的一个陪集（一个特解加上全部齐次解）——这正是「特解 + 齐次解」背后的空间结构。
quotient-space.definitionEn:
Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$ and $W\le V$ a subspace. For each vector $\alpha\in V$ the set $\alpha+W=\{\alpha+w:\ w\in W\}$ is called a **coset**, geometrically the affine layer through $\alpha$ parallel to $W$. The set of all cosets, denoted $V/W$, is the **quotient space** of $V$ by $W$. Intuitively it is obtained by collapsing the whole direction $W$ to a single point, complementing the information carried by the subspace itself.

One defines addition and scalar multiplication on $V/W$ by $(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=(\alpha+\beta)+W$ and $k(\alpha+W)=k\alpha+W$. The critical step is **well-definedness**: cosets have many representatives, so one must check that replacing $\alpha$ by $\alpha'=\alpha+w_1$ and $\beta$ by $\beta'=\beta+w_2$ changes nothing. Indeed $(\alpha'+W)+(\beta'+W)=(\alpha+w_1+\beta+w_2)+W=(\alpha+\beta)+W$ because $w_1+w_2\in W$, and likewise $k\alpha'=k\alpha+kw_1$ with $kw_1\in W$. Only after this verification is $V/W$ genuinely a vector space; the step is not a formality but the technical heart of the whole theory.

Equality of cosets has a simple test: $\alpha+W=\beta+W\iff\alpha-\beta\in W$. From it one obtains the dimension formula $\dim(V/W)=\dim V-\dim W$ in finite dimension: the degrees of freedom of a coset come exactly from the directions outside $W$. The **natural projection** $\pi:V\to V/W$, $\pi(\alpha)=\alpha+W$, is linear and surjective with $\ker\pi=W$; the quotient is the canonical way of killing exactly $W$.

**First isomorphism theorem.** For every linear map $T:V\to Y$ one has $V/\ker T\cong\operatorname{Im}T$, the isomorphism being $\bar\alpha\mapsto T(\alpha)$. This clarifies the structure of linear systems: the map $x\mapsto Ax$ induces $K^n/\ker A\cong\operatorname{Im}A$, while the solution set of $Ax=b$ is a coset of $\ker A$ — one particular solution plus all homogeneous solutions, the space structure behind the familiar recipe.
derivation: 设 $W\le V$ 是子空间。对 $\alpha\in V$ 定义陪集 $\alpha+W=\{\alpha+w:w\in W\}$，全体陪集记作 $V/W$。陪集相等有判别法：$$\alpha+W=\beta+W\iff\alpha-\beta\in W.$$ 若 $\alpha-\beta=w\in W$，则对任意 $u\in W$，$\alpha+u=\beta+(w+u)\in\beta+W$，且 $w+W=W$，故两陪集相等；反之若相等，由 $\alpha=\alpha+0\in\beta+W$ 得 $\alpha=\beta+w$，即 $\alpha-\beta\in W$。

在 $V/W$ 上定义 $$(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=(\alpha+\beta)+W,\qquad k(\alpha+W)=k\alpha+W.$$ 必须验证良定义：若换代表元 $\alpha'=\alpha+w_1$、$\beta'=\beta+w_2$（$w_1,w_2\in W$），则 $$\alpha'+\beta'=(\alpha+\beta)+(w_1+w_2),\qquad k\alpha'=k\alpha+kw_1,$$ 而 $w_1+w_2\in W$、$kw_1\in W$。由第 1 步，$(\alpha'+\beta')+W=(\alpha+\beta)+W$、$k\alpha'+W=k\alpha+W$，结果与代表元选取无关。

验证线性空间公理：加法结合律与交换律、零元 $0+W=W$、负元 $(-\alpha)+W$ 都从 $V$ 的相应性质逐项继承。例如 $$(\alpha+W)+W=(\alpha+0)+W=\alpha+W.$$ 数乘分配律同样逐项验证：$(k+l)(\alpha+W)=(k+l)\alpha+W=(k\alpha+l\alpha)+W=k(\alpha+W)+l(\alpha+W)$，且 $k(l(\alpha+W))=(kl)(\alpha+W)$、$1(\alpha+W)=\alpha+W$。因运算已良定义，这些等式在陪集层面成立，故 $V/W$ 是 $K$ 上的线性空间。

自然投影 $\pi:V\to V/W$，$\pi(\alpha)=\alpha+W$。由定义 $\pi(\alpha+\beta)=(\alpha+\beta)+W=(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=\pi(\alpha)+\pi(\beta)$，$\pi(k\alpha)=k\pi(\alpha)$，故线性；任意陪集 $\alpha+W$ 等于 $\pi(\alpha)$，故满射。核为 $$\ker\pi=\{\alpha:\alpha+W=W\}=\{\alpha:\alpha\in W\}=W.$$ 对有限维 $V$，秩–零化度定理给出 $\dim V=\dim\ker\pi+\dim\operatorname{Im}\pi=\dim W+\dim(V/W)$，即 $$\dim(V/W)=\dim V-\dim W.$$

第一同构定理：设 $T:V\to Y$ 线性。定义 $$\varphi:V/\ker T\to\operatorname{Im}T,\qquad \varphi(\alpha+\ker T)=T\alpha.$$ 良定义：若 $\alpha+\ker T=\beta+\ker T$，则 $\alpha-\beta\in\ker T$，故 $T\alpha=T\beta$。$\varphi$ 线性：$\varphi((\alpha+\ker T)+(\beta+\ker T))=T(\alpha+\beta)=T\alpha+T\beta$，数乘同理。核为零：$\varphi(\alpha+\ker T)=0\Rightarrow T\alpha=0\Rightarrow\alpha\in\ker T$，即该陪集是零陪集。满射由值域定义。因此 $V/\ker T\cong\operatorname{Im}T$，取维数得 $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T$。

商空间的普遍性质：若 $T:V\to Y$ 线性且 $W\subseteq\ker T$，定义 $\bar T:V/W\to Y$、$\bar T(\alpha+W)=T\alpha$。由 $W\subseteq\ker T$ 知其良定义，且 $T=\bar T\circ\pi$；因 $\pi$ 满射，满足此分解的 $\bar T$ 唯一。取 $W=\ker T$ 就回到第一同构定理。线性方程组的情形：$Ax=b$ 若有解 $x_0$，则解集为 $x_0+\ker A$——两个解之差是齐次解；同时 $K^n/\ker A\cong\operatorname{Im}A$，商空间把「核的自由度」与「像」分开。
derivationEn: Let $W\le V$ be a subspace. For $\alpha\in V$ define the coset $\alpha+W=\{\alpha+w:w\in W\}$; the set of all cosets is denoted $V/W$. Cosets satisfy the equality test $$\alpha+W=\beta+W\iff\alpha-\beta\in W.$$ If $\alpha-\beta=w\in W$, then for every $u\in W$, $\alpha+u=\beta+(w+u)\in\beta+W$, and $w+W=W$, so the cosets coincide. Conversely, if they are equal, then $\alpha=\alpha+0\in\beta+W$, so $\alpha=\beta+w$ and $\alpha-\beta\in W$.

Define on $V/W$ $$(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=(\alpha+\beta)+W,\qquad k(\alpha+W)=k\alpha+W.$$ Well-definedness must be checked: if representatives are changed to $\alpha'=\alpha+w_1$ and $\beta'=\beta+w_2$ with $w_1,w_2\in W$, then $$\alpha'+\beta'=(\alpha+\beta)+(w_1+w_2),\qquad k\alpha'=k\alpha+kw_1,$$ and $w_1+w_2\in W$, $kw_1\in W$. By Step 1, $(\alpha'+\beta')+W=(\alpha+\beta)+W$ and $k\alpha'+W=k\alpha+W$, so the result is independent of the representatives.

Vector-space axioms: associativity and commutativity of addition, the zero element $0+W=W$, and the inverse $-\alpha+W$ are inherited term by term from $V$. For example, $$(\alpha+W)+W=(\alpha+0)+W=\alpha+W.$$ The scalar distributive laws are checked similarly: $(k+l)(\alpha+W)=(k+l)\alpha+W=(k\alpha+l\alpha)+W=k(\alpha+W)+l(\alpha+W)$, and $k(l(\alpha+W))=(kl)(\alpha+W)$, $1(\alpha+W)=\alpha+W$. Since the operations are well defined, these identities hold at the level of cosets, so $V/W$ is a vector space over $K$.

The natural projection $\pi:V\to V/W$, $\pi(\alpha)=\alpha+W$, is linear: $\pi(\alpha+\beta)=(\alpha+\beta)+W=(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=\pi(\alpha)+\pi(\beta)$, and $\pi(k\alpha)=k\pi(\alpha)$; it is surjective because every coset is $\pi(\alpha)$. Its kernel is $$\ker\pi=\{\alpha:\alpha+W=W\}=\{\alpha:\alpha\in W\}=W.$$ For finite-dimensional $V$, rank–nullity gives $\dim V=\dim\ker\pi+\dim\operatorname{Im}\pi=\dim W+\dim(V/W)$, hence $$\dim(V/W)=\dim V-\dim W.$$

First isomorphism theorem: let $T:V\to Y$ be linear. Define $$\varphi:V/\ker T\to\operatorname{Im}T,\qquad \varphi(\alpha+\ker T)=T\alpha.$$ It is well defined: if $\alpha+\ker T=\beta+\ker T$, then $\alpha-\beta\in\ker T$, so $T\alpha=T\beta$. It is linear, since $\varphi((\alpha+\ker T)+(\beta+\ker T))=T(\alpha+\beta)=T\alpha+T\beta$, and similarly for scalars. Its kernel is zero: $\varphi(\alpha+\ker T)=0$ implies $T\alpha=0$, so $\alpha\in\ker T$ and the coset is the zero coset. It is surjective onto its codomain by definition. Therefore $V/\ker T\cong\operatorname{Im}T$, and taking dimensions gives $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T$.

Universal property of the quotient: if $T:V\to Y$ is linear and $W\subseteq\ker T$, define $\bar T:V/W\to Y$ by $\bar T(\alpha+W)=T\alpha$. The inclusion $W\subseteq\ker T$ makes it well defined, and $T=\bar T\circ\pi$; since $\pi$ is surjective, such a $\bar T$ is unique. Taking $W=\ker T$ recovers the first isomorphism theorem. For linear systems, if $Ax=b$ has a solution $x_0$, its solution set is $x_0+\ker A$—two solutions differ by a homogeneous solution—and $K^n/\ker A\cong\operatorname{Im}A$ separates the degrees of freedom in the kernel from the image.

formulas.note: 陪集相等的判别法：两个代表元之差属于 $W$ 就是同一个陪集。它把「集合相等」化归为「差向量属于子空间」。
formulas.noteEn: The coset equality test: two representatives give the same coset exactly when their difference lies in $W$, reducing set equality to membership of a difference vector.

formulas.note: 商空间的加法与数乘定义；必须验证它们与代表元的选取无关（良定义性），验证过程正是「$w_1+w_2\in W$、$kw_1\in W$」。
formulas.noteEn: The definitions of addition and scalar multiplication on the quotient; both must be shown independent of the chosen representatives, the verification being precisely $w_1+w_2\in W$ and $kw_1\in W$.

formulas.note: 有限维商空间的维数公式：维数「被减掉」的部分正来自 $W$；若 $V=W\oplus U$，则投影 $U\to V/W$ 是同构，商空间与补空间同维且同构。
formulas.noteEn: Dimension formula in finite dimension: the quotient loses exactly the dimensions of $W$. If $V=W\oplus U$, the projection $U\to V/W$ is an isomorphism, so the quotient is modeled on a complement.

formulas.note: 自然投影把每个向量送到它所在的陪集：它是满的线性映射，核恰好是 $W$，因此 $V/W$ 是「把 $W$ 压成 0」的普遍构造。
formulas.noteEn: The natural projection sends each vector to its coset: it is linear and surjective with kernel exactly $W$, so $V/W$ is the universal construction that crushes $W$ to zero.

formulas.latex: V/\ker T\cong \operatorname{Im}T,\qquad \bar\alpha\mapsto T(\alpha)\quad (\text{第一同构定理})
formulas.note: 第一同构定理：把定义域按核「约掉」后与像同构。取维数立刻得到秩-零化度定理 $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T$。
formulas.noteEn: The first isomorphism theorem: dividing the domain by the kernel yields the image. Taking dimensions gives rank–nullity, $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T$.

properties: 良定义性必须显式验证：陪集的加法与数乘都要检查「换代表元结果不变」。这不是形式主义——一旦 $W$ 不是子空间，这样定义的运算立刻失效。
维数公式 $\dim(V/W)=\dim V-\dim W$；若 $V=W\oplus U$，则 $u\mapsto u+W$ 给出 $U\cong V/W$，商空间可以具体地理解为「补空间」。
自然投影的普适性质：任何满足 $T(W)=0$ 的线性映射 $T:V\to Y$ 都能唯一地分解为 $T=\bar T\circ\pi$（其中 $\bar T:V/W\to Y$ 线性）。这说清了商空间是「把 $W$ 压成 0」的最一般线性方式。
第一同构定理的两要点：映射 $\bar\alpha\mapsto T\alpha$ 良定义（$\alpha-\beta\in\ker T\Rightarrow T\alpha=T\beta$）且是线性同构；取维数立得秩-零化度定理 $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T$。
与线性方程组呼应：$Ax=b$ 的解集若非空，就是一个陪集 $x_0+\ker A$，不同的解正好相差一个齐次解；商空间把「掉进核的自由度」与「像」分开，$K^n/\ker A\cong\operatorname{Im}A$。
propertiesEn: Well-definedness must be verified explicitly: for both addition and scalar multiplication one checks that the result does not depend on the representatives. This is no formality — if $W$ is not a subspace the operations break down immediately.
Dimension formula $\dim(V/W)=\dim V-\dim W$; if $V=W\oplus U$, then $u\mapsto u+W$ is an isomorphism $U\cong V/W$, so the quotient can be modeled concretely on a complement.

Universal property of the projection: every linear map $T:V\to Y$ with $T(W)=0$ factors uniquely as $T=\bar T\circ\pi$ with $\bar T:V/W\to Y$ linear. This says that the quotient is the most general linear way of crushing $W$ to zero.

Two essential points of the first isomorphism theorem: the map $\bar\alpha\mapsto T\alpha$ is well defined ($\alpha-\beta\in\ker T$ implies $T\alpha=T\beta$) and is a linear isomorphism; counting dimensions gives rank–nullity, $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T$.

Link with linear systems: when nonempty, the solution set of $Ax=b$ is the coset $x_0+\ker A$, and two solutions differ by a homogeneous solution; the quotient separates the degrees of freedom swallowed by the kernel from the image, giving $K^n/\ker A\cong\operatorname{Im}A$.

examples.problem: 在 $V=\mathbb{R}^2$ 中取 $W=\{(t,t):\ t\in\mathbb{R}\}$（过原点的直线）。验证 $(2,0)+W=(3,1)+W$ 但 $(0,1)+W\ne(2,0)+W$；再验证数乘与代表元无关，并求 $\dim(\mathbb{R}^2/W)$ 与一组基。
设 $T:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^2$，$T(x,y,z)=(x-y,\ y-z)$。求 $\ker T$ 与 $\operatorname{Im}T$，并用第一同构定理说明 $\mathbb{R}^3/\ker T\cong\mathbb{R}^2$。
examples.solution:
核：$T(x,y,z)=0$ 即 $x=y$ 且 $y=z$，故 $\ker T=\{(t,t,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}=\operatorname{span}\{(1,1,1)\}$，$\dim\ker T=1$。
像：对任意 $(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^2$，取 $(x,y,z)=(u,0,-v)$，则 $T(u,0,-v)=(u-0,\ 0-(-v))=(u,v)$，故 $T$ 是满射，$\operatorname{Im}T=\mathbb{R}^2$，$\dim\operatorname{Im}T=2$。
由第一同构定理 $\mathbb{R}^3/\ker T\cong\operatorname{Im}T=\mathbb{R}^2$，同构为 $\overline{(x,y,z)}\mapsto(x-y,\ y-z)$；维数核对 $3-1=2$ ✓，与秩-零化度定理一致。直观上：模去对角线方向后，每个陪集由两个差值 $(x-y,\ y-z)$ 唯一刻画。

tensor-product.definition:
**先划清范围**：本节讲的是代数里的**张量积** $V\otimes W$——把两个线性空间「合并」成一个新线性空间的纯代数构造。物理与工程里常说的「张量」通常指随坐标变换的**张量场**（在每一点处放一个多重线性量），两者名字相同但层次不同；张量积是那些张量场的代数底层，也是抽象指标记号能够运转的原因。

构造的要点是把「双线性」编码成一个新的乘法 $\otimes$。形式上，$V\otimes W$ 由所有形式符号 $\alpha\otimes\beta$ 张成，再按双线性规则作商；四条规则是 $(k\alpha)\otimes\beta=\alpha\otimes(k\beta)=k(\alpha\otimes\beta)$、$(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)\otimes\beta=\alpha_1\otimes\beta+\alpha_2\otimes\beta$ 以及它对第二变量的对称版本 $\alpha\otimes(\beta_1+\beta_2)=\alpha\otimes\beta_1+\alpha\otimes\beta_2$。也就是说，$\otimes$ 对两个变量分别线性，除此之外不假设任何关系：$\alpha\otimes\beta$ 与 $\beta\otimes\alpha$ 一般不等；$\alpha\otimes\beta=0$ 当且仅当 $\alpha=0$ 或 $\beta=0$（这一点与一般环上的模张量积不同——那里两个非零因子的积也可能为 0）。

**泛性质**是张量积的灵魂：对任何双线性映射 $B:V\times W\to U$，存在唯一的线性映射 $\tilde B:V\otimes W\to U$ 使 $B(\alpha,\beta)=\tilde B(\alpha\otimes\beta)$ 对一切 $\alpha,\beta$ 成立。换句话说，「$V\times W$ 上的双线性映射」与「$V\otimes W$ 上的线性映射」一一对应。张量积的全部威力就在于此：把双线性问题升级为线性问题，而线性问题我们已有完整的工具。泛性质在同构意义下唯一确定 $V\otimes W$，因此可以放心把它当作具体空间使用。

有限维时它非常好算：$\dim(V\otimes W)=\dim V\cdot\dim W$，若 $\{e_i\}$、$\{f_j\}$ 分别是 $V$、$W$ 的基，则 $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ 是 $V\otimes W$ 的基，一般元素唯一地写成 $\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}\,e_i\otimes f_j$。能写成单个 $\alpha\otimes\beta$ 的元素称为**纯张量**；纯张量的系数矩阵 $(c_{ij})$ 秩为 1，而 $\dim V,\dim W\ge2$ 时一定存在非纯张量（例如 $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1$）。最贴切的例子是 $\mathbb{R}^m\otimes\mathbb{R}^n\cong M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$：张量就是矩阵，纯张量就是秩一矩阵。
tensor-product.definitionEn:
**Scope first.** Here we discuss the algebraic **tensor product** $V\otimes W$, the purely algebraic construction that merges two vector spaces into a new one. What physicists and engineers call a tensor is usually a **tensor field** — a multilinear quantity attached to each point of a manifold — a different layer of the same name; the tensor product is the algebraic foundation underneath those fields and the reason abstract index notation works.

The construction encodes bilinearity into a new product $\otimes$. Formally $V\otimes W$ is spanned by symbols $\alpha\otimes\beta$ subject to the bilinearity relations: $(k\alpha)\otimes\beta=\alpha\otimes(k\beta)=k(\alpha\otimes\beta)$, $(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)\otimes\beta=\alpha_1\otimes\beta+\alpha_2\otimes\beta$, and symmetrically $\alpha\otimes(\beta_1+\beta_2)=\alpha\otimes\beta_1+\alpha\otimes\beta_2$. Thus $\otimes$ is linear in each variable separately and nothing more: $\alpha\otimes\beta$ need not equal $\beta\otimes\alpha$, and $\alpha\otimes\beta=0$ exactly when one of the factors is $0$ (a contrast with tensor products of modules over rings, where both factors may be nonzero).

The **universal property** is the heart of the matter: for every bilinear map $B:V\times W\to U$ there is a unique linear map $\tilde B:V\otimes W\to U$ with $B(\alpha,\beta)=\tilde B(\alpha\otimes\beta)$ for all $\alpha,\beta$. In other words, bilinear maps on $V\times W$ correspond one-to-one to linear maps on $V\otimes W$. This is where the power of the tensor product lies: it upgrades bilinear problems to linear ones, for which the toolbox is complete. The universal property determines $V\otimes W$ up to isomorphism, so it may safely be treated as a concrete space.

In finite dimension everything is computable: $\dim(V\otimes W)=\dim V\cdot\dim W$, and if $\{e_i\}$ and $\{f_j\}$ are bases of $V$ and $W$, then $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ is a basis of $V\otimes W$, every element being uniquely $\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}\,e_i\otimes f_j$. Elements of the form $\alpha\otimes\beta$ are called **pure tensors**; a pure tensor has a coefficient matrix $(c_{ij})$ of rank one, and non-pure tensors exist as soon as $\dim V,\dim W\ge2$ (for example $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1$). The sharpest example is $\mathbb{R}^m\otimes\mathbb{R}^n\cong M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$: tensors are matrices and pure tensors are rank-one matrices.
derivation: 构造：先取以集合 $V\times W$ 为基的自由向量空间 $F$，即把每个形式符号 $(\alpha,\beta)$ 当作基向量；再令 $R$ 为所有下列关系张成的子空间：$$\begin{aligned}&(k\alpha,\beta)-k(\alpha,\beta),\\&(\alpha,k\beta)-k(\alpha,\beta),\\&(\alpha_1+\alpha_2,\beta)-(\alpha_1,\beta)-(\alpha_2,\beta),\\&(\alpha,\beta_1+\beta_2)-(\alpha,\beta_1)-(\alpha,\beta_2).\end{aligned}$$ 定义 $V\otimes W=F/R$，并记 $\alpha\otimes\beta=(\alpha,\beta)+R$。由商空间构造，$\otimes$ 对两个变量分别线性；构造中没有加入 $\alpha\otimes\beta=\beta\otimes\alpha$ 的关系，所以二者一般不等。

万有性质：设 $B:V\times W\to U$ 双线性。在 $F$ 上定义线性映射 $\Phi$，使基向量 $(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto B(\alpha,\beta)$。因 $B$ 双线性，$\Phi$ 在 $R$ 的每个生成元上取零，故诱导出线性映射 $\tilde B:V\otimes W\to U$，满足 $$\tilde B(\alpha\otimes\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta).$$ 若另有 $\tilde B'$ 满足同样条件，则二者在张成 $V\otimes W$ 的纯张量上一致，故 $\tilde B'=\tilde B$，唯一性成立。反之，任一线性 $\tilde B$ 与 $\otimes$ 复合给出双线性映射，于是双线性映射与线性映射一一对应。

纯张量张成：由构造，$V\otimes W$ 中每个元素都是有限个基向量 $(\alpha,\beta)$ 的像的线性组合，即有限和 $\sum_{r=1}^{N}c_r\,\alpha_r\otimes\beta_r$。它一般不是「两个向量的乘积」，而是纯张量的有限和。取 $V$ 的基 $e_1,\dots,e_m$ 与 $W$ 的基 $f_1,\dots,f_n$，把 $\alpha_r=\sum_i a_{ir}e_i$、$\beta_r=\sum_j b_{jr}f_j$ 代入并用双线性，得 $$\begin{aligned}\sum_{r}c_r\alpha_r\otimes\beta_r&=\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}\,e_i\otimes f_j,\\C_{ij}&=\sum_{r}c_ra_{ir}b_{jr}.\end{aligned}$$ 故 $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ 张成 $V\otimes W$。

证明 $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ 线性无关。对每对 $(i_0,j_0)$，定义双线性型 $B_{i_0j_0}(\alpha,\beta)=a_{i_0}b_{j_0}$，其中 $\alpha=\sum_i a_ie_i$、$\beta=\sum_j b_jf_j$。由万有性质得到线性函数 $\varphi_{i_0j_0}:V\otimes W\to K$，满足 $$\varphi_{i_0j_0}(e_i\otimes f_j)=\delta_{ii_0}\delta_{jj_0}.$$ 若 $\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j=0$，两边作用 $\varphi_{i_0j_0}$ 得 $c_{i_0j_0}=0$。所有系数为零，故 $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ 线性无关。结合第 3 步，它是基，于是 $$\dim(V\otimes W)=mn=\dim V\cdot\dim W.$$

纯张量的判别：若 $\alpha\ne0$、$\beta\ne0$，分别取以 $\alpha$ 为第一个基向量的 $V$ 的基、以 $\beta$ 为第一个基向量的 $W$ 的基，则 $\alpha\otimes\beta=e_1\otimes f_1$，是基元素，故不为零。反之，若某一因子为 $0$，双线性给出 $\alpha\otimes\beta=0$。因此对向量空间 $$\alpha\otimes\beta=0\iff\alpha=0\ \text{或}\ \beta=0.$$ 固定基后，纯张量 $\alpha\otimes\beta$ 的系数矩阵为外积 $\alpha\beta^{T}$，两因子非零时秩为 $1$；反之秩一矩阵都可写成外积。故 $\dim V,\dim W\ge2$ 时存在非纯张量，例如 $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1$ 的系数矩阵 $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ 秩为 $2$。

具体同构：$\mathbb{R}^m\otimes\mathbb{R}^n\cong M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$，由 $e_i\otimes f_j\mapsto E_{ij}$ 线性延拓，其中 $E_{ij}$ 是 $(i,j)$ 位置为 $1$、其余为 $0$ 的矩阵。于是 $\alpha\otimes\beta\mapsto\alpha\beta^{T}$（列乘行），其秩为 $1$；一般张量 $\sum c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j$ 对应矩阵 $(c_{ij})$。两边维数都是 $mn$，与第 4 步一致。有限维时还有 $V^*\otimes W\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$，对应 $f\otimes\beta\mapsto(\alpha\mapsto f(\alpha)\beta)$；这说明线性映射本身也可以写成张量。
derivationEn: Construction: first take the free vector space $F$ on the set $V\times W$, treating each formal symbol $(\alpha,\beta)$ as a basis vector; let $R$ be the subspace spanned by all relations $$\begin{aligned}&(k\alpha,\beta)-k(\alpha,\beta),\\&(\alpha,k\beta)-k(\alpha,\beta),\\&(\alpha_1+\alpha_2,\beta)-(\alpha_1,\beta)-(\alpha_2,\beta),\\&(\alpha,\beta_1+\beta_2)-(\alpha,\beta_1)-(\alpha,\beta_2).\end{aligned}$$ Define $V\otimes W=F/R$ and write $\alpha\otimes\beta=(\alpha,\beta)+R$. By the quotient construction, $\otimes$ is linear in each variable; no relation $\alpha\otimes\beta=\beta\otimes\alpha$ is imposed, so the two are generally unequal.

Universal property: let $B:V\times W\to U$ be bilinear. Define a linear map $\Phi$ on $F$ by sending each basis vector $(\alpha,\beta)$ to $B(\alpha,\beta)$. Because $B$ is bilinear, $\Phi$ vanishes on every generator of $R$, so it induces a linear map $\tilde B:V\otimes W\to U$ satisfying $$\tilde B(\alpha\otimes\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta).$$ If another $\tilde B'$ satisfies the same condition, then $\tilde B'=\tilde B$ on the pure tensors, which span $V\otimes W$, so $\tilde B'=\tilde B$; uniqueness holds. Conversely, any linear $\tilde B$ composed with $\otimes$ gives a bilinear map, so bilinear maps and linear maps correspond one-to-one.

Pure tensors span: by construction every element of $V\otimes W$ is a linear combination of the images of finitely many basis vectors $(\alpha,\beta)$, i.e. a finite sum $\sum_{r=1}^{N}c_r\,\alpha_r\otimes\beta_r$. It is not in general a single product of two vectors, but a finite sum of pure tensors. Take bases $e_1,\dots,e_m$ of $V$ and $f_1,\dots,f_n$ of $W$, write $\alpha_r=\sum_i a_{ir}e_i$ and $\beta_r=\sum_j b_{jr}f_j$, and use bilinearity: $$\begin{aligned}\sum_{r}c_r\alpha_r\otimes\beta_r&=\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}\,e_i\otimes f_j,\\C_{ij}&=\sum_{r}c_ra_{ir}b_{jr}.\end{aligned}$$ Hence $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ spans $V\otimes W$.

Independence of $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$: for each pair $(i_0,j_0)$ define the bilinear form $B_{i_0j_0}(\alpha,\beta)=a_{i_0}b_{j_0}$, where $\alpha=\sum_i a_ie_i$ and $\beta=\sum_j b_jf_j$. The universal property gives a linear functional $\varphi_{i_0j_0}:V\otimes W\to K$ with $$\varphi_{i_0j_0}(e_i\otimes f_j)=\delta_{ii_0}\delta_{jj_0}.$$ If $\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j=0$, applying $\varphi_{i_0j_0}$ gives $c_{i_0j_0}=0$. All coefficients vanish, so the set is linearly independent. Together with Step 3 it is a basis, and $$\dim(V\otimes W)=mn=\dim V\cdot\dim W.$$

Criterion for pure tensors: if $\alpha\ne0$ and $\beta\ne0$, choose a basis of $V$ whose first vector is $\alpha$ and a basis of $W$ whose first vector is $\beta$; then $\alpha\otimes\beta=e_1\otimes f_1$, a nonzero basis element. Conversely, if one factor is $0$, bilinearity gives $\alpha\otimes\beta=0$. Thus for vector spaces $$\alpha\otimes\beta=0\iff\alpha=0\ \text{or}\ \beta=0.$$ In a fixed basis, a pure tensor $\alpha\otimes\beta$ has coefficient matrix the outer product $\alpha\beta^{T}$, of rank $1$ when both factors are nonzero; conversely every rank-one matrix is such an outer product. Hence non-pure tensors exist when $\dim V,\dim W\ge2$: for example $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1$ has coefficient matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, of rank $2$.

Concrete isomorphism: $\mathbb{R}^m\otimes\mathbb{R}^n\cong M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$, determined by $e_i\otimes f_j\mapsto E_{ij}$, where $E_{ij}$ has a $1$ in position $(i,j)$ and zeros elsewhere. Then $\alpha\otimes\beta\mapsto\alpha\beta^{T}$ (column times row), which has rank one; a general tensor $\sum c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j$ corresponds to the matrix $(c_{ij})$. Both sides have dimension $mn$, consistent with Step 4. In finite dimension there is also $V^*\otimes W\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, given by $f\otimes\beta\mapsto(\alpha\mapsto f(\alpha)\beta)$; this shows that linear maps themselves can be written as tensors.

formulas.note: 标量可以自由穿过 $\otimes$：无论缩放出现在左边还是右边，结果都是同一个标量与张量的乘积。
formulas.noteEn: Scalars pass freely through $\otimes$: scaling on either side yields the same scalar multiple of the tensor.

formulas.note: 分配律（加法的双线性）：$\otimes$ 对两个变量分别线性，这两条加上标量规则就是张量积的全部「运算规则」。
formulas.noteEn: Distributivity: $\otimes$ is linear in each variable separately; these two rules together with the scalar rule are the complete set of manipulation rules for tensor products.

formulas.latex: \dim(V\otimes W)=\dim V\cdot\dim W,\qquad \{e_i\otimes f_j\}_{i,j}\ \text{是基（}e_i,f_j\text{ 分别为基）}
formulas.note: 维数相乘是张量积最常用的定量结论：4 维的 $\mathbb{R}^2\otimes\mathbb{R}^2$ 由 4 个基张量 $e_i\otimes e_j$ 张开。
formulas.noteEn: Dimensions multiply: this is the most-used quantitative fact about tensor products. The 4-dimensional space $\mathbb{R}^2\otimes\mathbb{R}^2$ is spanned by the four basis tensors $e_i\otimes e_j$.

formulas.latex: B:V\times W\to U\ \text{双线性}\iff \exists!\ \tilde B:V\otimes W\to U\ \text{线性},\quad \tilde B(\alpha\otimes\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta)
formulas.note: 泛性质：任何一个双线性映射都唯一地「提」为 $V\otimes W$ 上的线性映射。它同时给出张量积的同构唯一性，是理论的主力工具。
formulas.noteEn: The universal property: every bilinear map lifts uniquely to a linear map on $V\otimes W$. It also forces uniqueness of the tensor product up to isomorphism and is the main working tool of the theory.

formulas.latex: \mathbb{R}^m\otimes\mathbb{R}^n\cong M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}),\qquad e_i\otimes f_j\mapsto E_{ij},\qquad \alpha\otimes\beta\mapsto \alpha\beta^{\mathsf T}
formulas.note: 张量即矩阵：基张量对应矩阵单位 $E_{ij}$，而纯张量 $\alpha\otimes\beta$ 对应外积矩阵 $\alpha\beta^{\mathsf T}$（列乘行），秩为 1。
formulas.noteEn: Tensors are matrices: basis tensors correspond to matrix units $E_{ij}$, and a pure tensor $\alpha\otimes\beta$ corresponds to the outer product $\alpha\beta^{\mathsf T}$ (column times row), which has rank one.

properties: 泛性质决定一切：任何「双线性」的陈述都能唯一地翻译成从 $V\otimes W$ 出发的线性映射；这也是张量积在同构意义下唯一、可以在构造细节上「忘记」商空间的理由。
维数相乘：$\dim(V\otimes W)=\dim V\dim W$，基是 $e_i\otimes f_j$；固定基后张量的坐标 $c_{ij}$ 拼成 $m\times n$ 矩阵，张量运算逐项变成矩阵运算。

纯张量与一般张量：$\alpha\otimes\beta$ 的系数矩阵是外积 $\alpha\beta^{\mathsf T}$，秩为 1；$\dim V,\dim W\ge2$ 时存在非纯张量，例如 $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1$（系数矩阵 $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ 秩为 2）。「张量 = 两个向量的乘积」是常见误解——纯张量只是全体张量中的一个低维子集。

对称张量与反对称张量：$\operatorname{Sym}^2V$ 由 $\alpha\otimes\beta+\beta\otimes\alpha$ 张成、$\Lambda^2V$ 由 $\alpha\otimes\beta-\beta\otimes\alpha$ 张成；当域的特征不等于 2 时 $V\otimes V=\operatorname{Sym}^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$，维数分别为 $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ 与 $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$，且反对称一边满足 $\alpha\wedge\alpha=0$（外代数的起点）。
对偶张量：有限维时 $V^*\otimes W\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$，对应 $f\otimes\beta\mapsto(\alpha\mapsto f(\alpha)\beta)$；线性映射因此可以「写成张量」，这也是抽象指标记号与坐标无关张量演算的来源。
propertiesEn: The universal property governs everything: any bilinear statement translates uniquely into a linear map out of $V\otimes W$, which is why the tensor product is unique up to isomorphism and why the quotient construction can be forgotten in practice.

Dimensions multiply: $\dim(V\otimes W)=\dim V\dim W$ with basis $e_i\otimes f_j$; once bases are fixed, the coordinates $c_{ij}$ assemble into an $m\times n$ matrix and tensor operations become entrywise matrix operations.

Pure versus general tensors: $\alpha\otimes\beta$ has coefficient matrix the outer product $\alpha\beta^{\mathsf T}$, of rank one; non-pure tensors exist whenever $\dim V,\dim W\ge2$, e.g. $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1$, whose coefficient matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ has rank two. Saying that 「a tensor is a product of two vectors」 is a common misconception — pure tensors form only a low-dimensional subset.

Symmetric and alternating tensors: $\operatorname{Sym}^2V$ is spanned by $\alpha\otimes\beta+\beta\otimes\alpha$ and $\Lambda^2V$ by $\alpha\otimes\beta-\beta\otimes\alpha$; over a field of characteristic not 2, $V\otimes V=\operatorname{Sym}^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$ with dimensions $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ and $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$, and the alternating side satisfies $\alpha\wedge\alpha=0$ — the starting point of exterior algebra.

Dual tensors: in finite dimension $V^*\otimes W\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$ via $f\otimes\beta\mapsto(\alpha\mapsto f(\alpha)\beta)$, so linear maps can be written as tensors; this is the origin of abstract index notation and coordinate-free tensor calculus.

examples.problem: 写出 $\mathbb{R}^2\otimes\mathbb{R}^2$ 的一组基元素，并把 $(1,2)\otimes(3,-1)$ 展开成基的线性组合，指出它的系数矩阵与秩。
examples.solution:
取 $\mathbb{R}^2$ 的标准基 $e_1=(1,0)$、$e_2=(0,1)$，则基元素为 $e_1\otimes e_1$、$e_1\otimes e_2$、$e_2\otimes e_1$、$e_2\otimes e_2$，共 $2\times2=4$ 个，与 $\dim(V\otimes W)=\dim V\cdot\dim W$ 一致。
展开：$(1,2)\otimes(3,-1)=(e_1+2e_2)\otimes(3e_1-e_2)$，用双线性规则逐项相乘：
$=3\,e_1\otimes e_1-e_1\otimes e_2+6\,e_2\otimes e_1-2\,e_2\otimes e_2$。
系数矩阵为 $\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\6&-2\end{pmatrix}$：第 $(i,j)$ 个元素就是 $e_i\otimes e_j$ 的系数。行列式 $3\cdot(-2)-(-1)\cdot6=0$，故秩为 1（两行成比例、比例为 2），与「纯张量的系数矩阵秩为 1」一致：它确实是纯张量 $(1,2)\otimes(3,-1)$。

examples.problem: 证明 $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1\in\mathbb{R}^2\otimes\mathbb{R}^2$ 不是纯张量。
examples.solution:
反设它是纯张量，即存在实数 $a,b,c,d$ 使 $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1=(a e_1+b e_2)\otimes(c e_1+d e_2)$。
用双线性规则展开右边：$(a e_1+b e_2)\otimes(c e_1+d e_2)=ac\,e_1\otimes e_1+ad\,e_1\otimes e_2+bc\,e_2\otimes e_1+bd\,e_2\otimes e_2$。
左边关于基 $\{e_1\otimes e_1,\ e_1\otimes e_2,\ e_2\otimes e_1,\ e_2\otimes e_2\}$ 的系数为 $(0,1,1,0)$，而基张量线性无关，故比较系数得 $ac=0$、$ad=1$、$bc=1$、$bd=0$。
由 $ad=1$ 知 $a\ne0$ 且 $d\ne0$；由 $bc=1$ 知 $b\ne0$ 且 $c\ne0$。但 $ac=0$ 要求 $a=0$ 或 $c=0$，与上一步矛盾。因此不存在这样的 $a,b,c,d$，该元素不是纯张量。∎
（几何解释：它的系数矩阵 $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ 秩为 2，而纯张量的系数矩阵秩不超过 1。）

matrix-groups.definition:
**矩阵群**就是由矩阵组成、在矩阵乘法下构成群的集合：包含单位矩阵，对乘法封闭，每个元素都可逆且逆元仍在集合中。最基本的例子是**一般线性群** $GL(n,K)=\{A\in M_n(K):\ \det A\ne0\}$——它把「可逆」这件事本身组织成一个群。矩阵群是线性代数与几何、物理的接口：旋转、反射、幺正演化等对称性都可以写成矩阵群中的元素。

在同一条主线上还有一串经典群：**特殊线性群** $SL(n)=\{A:\det A=1\}$、**正交群** $O(n)=\{A: A^{\mathsf T}A=E\}$、**特殊正交群** $SO(n)=\{A\in O(n): \det A=1\}$、**酉群** $U(n)=\{A: A^{\mathsf H}A=E\}$ 与**特殊酉群** $SU(n)=\{A\in U(n): \det A=1\}$。包含关系是 $SO(n)\subset O(n)\subset GL(n)$ 与 $SU(n)\subset U(n)\subset GL(n)$，而 $SL(n)=\{A\in GL(n):\det A=1\}$ 与 $O(n)$ 只在「行列式为 1」这一条约束上相交。

几何意义：正交矩阵满足 $A^{\mathsf T}A=E$，所以保内积与长度（$\langle Ax,Ay\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle$、$\|Ax\|=\|x\|$），是空间中的刚体运动（不含平移）。两边取行列式得 $(\det A)^2=1$，即 $\det A=\pm1$：$\det A=1$ 的是**旋转**（$SO(n)$ 就是旋转群），$\det A=-1$ 的含**反射**。二维情形 $SO(2)$ 可以完全参数化，写成 $R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}$，它与复数乘法和角度加法直接对应。

最后一个必须澄清的点是**群作用**：同一个矩阵在不同情境下要受两种不同的变换。**相似** $A\mapsto P^{-1}AP$ 描述「换基之后线性映射的新矩阵」，保持特征值、迹、行列式与若尔当标准形；**合同** $A\mapsto P^{\mathsf T}AP$ 描述「换基之后二次型的新矩阵」，保持对称性、秩与惯性指数。两者的不变量完全不同，绝不能混用。
matrix-groups.definitionEn:
A **matrix group** is a set of matrices forming a group under matrix multiplication: it contains the identity, is closed under multiplication, and every element is invertible with its inverse again in the set. The basic example is the **general linear group** $GL(n,K)=\{A\in M_n(K):\ \det A\ne0\}$, which turns invertibility itself into a group. Matrix groups are the interface between linear algebra and geometry or physics: rotations, reflections and unitary evolutions are all elements of such groups.

Along the same theme runs a series of classical groups: the **special linear group** $SL(n)=\{A:\det A=1\}$, the **orthogonal group** $O(n)=\{A: A^{\mathsf T}A=E\}$, the **special orthogonal group** $SO(n)=\{A\in O(n): \det A=1\}$, the **unitary group** $U(n)=\{A: A^{\mathsf H}A=E\}$ and the **special unitary group** $SU(n)=\{A\in U(n): \det A=1\}$. The inclusions are $SO(n)\subset O(n)\subset GL(n)$ and $SU(n)\subset U(n)\subset GL(n)$, while $SL(n)$ meets $O(n)$ exactly in the condition $\det A=1$.

Geometrically, an orthogonal matrix satisfies $A^{\mathsf T}A=E$ and therefore preserves inner products and lengths ($\langle Ax,Ay\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle$, $\|Ax\|=\|x\|$): it is a rigid motion fixing the origin, with no translation. Taking determinants gives $(\det A)^2=1$, so $\det A=\pm1$: determinant $+1$ means a **rotation** (indeed $SO(n)$ is the rotation group), determinant $-1$ involves a **reflection**. In dimension two, $SO(2)$ admits a complete parametrization $R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}$, directly linked to complex multiplication and the addition of angles.

A final point that must be kept straight is the **group action**: the same matrix undergoes two quite different transformations depending on the context. **Similarity** $A\mapsto P^{-1}AP$ describes the matrix of a linear map after a change of basis and preserves eigenvalues, trace, determinant and Jordan form. **Congruence** $A\mapsto P^{\mathsf T}AP$ describes the matrix of a quadratic form after a change of basis and preserves symmetry, rank and inertia indices. Their invariants are entirely different and the two must never be confused.
derivation:
设 $K=\mathbb R$ 或 $\mathbb C$，$M_n(K)$ 为 $n$ 阶方阵。子集 $G\subseteq M_n(K)$ 称为**矩阵群**，若：$E_n\in G$；$A,B\in G\Rightarrow AB\in G$；$A\in G\Rightarrow A$ 可逆且 $A^{-1}\in G$。等价地，$G$ 在矩阵乘法下构成群。最基本的例子是
$$GL(n,K)=\{A\in M_n(K):\det A\ne0\},$$
称为**一般线性群**。它确实是群：$\det(AB)=\det A\det B\ne0$，$\det E=1$，且 $\det(A^{-1})=1/\det A$，所以乘法封闭、单位元在、逆元在；结合律由矩阵乘法自动继承。$GL(n,K)$ 的元素正是 $K^n$ 上可逆线性变换在标准基下的矩阵。

行列式给出群同态
$$\det:GL(n,K)\to K^{\times},$$
其中 $K^{\times}=K\setminus\{0\}$ 在乘法下是群；$\det(AB)=\det A\det B$ 说明它是同态。其核
$$SL(n,K)=\{A\in GL(n,K):\det A=1\}$$
称为**特殊线性群**。核自动是正规子群：若 $S\in SL(n,K)$、$P\in GL(n,K)$，则
$$\det(P^{-1}SP)=\det(P)^{-1}\det(S)\det(P)=1,$$
故 $P^{-1}SP\in SL(n,K)$。几何上，$SL(n,\mathbb R)$ 由保持有向体积的线性变换组成；当 $n\ge2$ 时它不是 $O(n)$ 的子群，两者只在
$$SL(n,\mathbb R)\cap O(n)=SO(n)$$
处相交。

**正交群**
$$O(n)=\{A\in M_n(\mathbb R):A^{\mathrm T}A=E_n\}.$$
若 $A,B\in O(n)$，则
$$(AB)^{\mathrm T}(AB)=B^{\mathrm T}A^{\mathrm T}AB=B^{\mathrm T}B=E_n,$$
故 $AB\in O(n)$；$E_n\in O(n)$；$A^{\mathrm T}A=E_n$ 说明 $A$ 可逆且 $A^{-1}=A^{\mathrm T}$，而 $A^{\mathrm T}\in O(n)$，故 $A^{-1}\in O(n)$。所以 $O(n)$ 是矩阵群。取行列式得
$$(\det A)^2=\det(A^{\mathrm T}A)=\det E_n=1,$$
故 $\det A=\pm1$。令
$$SO(n)=\{A\in O(n):\det A=1\}=O(n)\cap SL(n,\mathbb R),$$
它是 $O(n)$ 的指数 $2$ 子群（$n\ge1$）：$\det$ 在 $O(n)$ 上取到 $+1$ 与 $-1$（例如 $E_n$ 与 $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\dots,1)$），两个陪集分别为 $SO(n)$ 与 $\{A\in O(n):\det A=-1\}$。

**酉群**
$$U(n)=\{A\in M_n(\mathbb C):A^{\mathrm H}A=E_n\},\qquad A^{\mathrm H}=\overline{A}^{\mathrm T}.$$
与正交群同样的计算：若 $A,B\in U(n)$，则
$$(AB)^{\mathrm H}(AB)=B^{\mathrm H}A^{\mathrm H}AB=B^{\mathrm H}B=E_n,$$
且 $A^{-1}=A^{\mathrm H}\in U(n)$，故 $U(n)$ 是矩阵群。取行列式得
$$|\det A|^2=\det(A^{\mathrm H}A)=1,$$
即 $\det A$ 是模为 $1$ 的复数；注意这不是 $\det A=\pm1$，复数情形条件更弱。**特殊酉群**为
$$SU(n)=\{A\in U(n):\det A=1\}=U(n)\cap SL(n,\mathbb C).$$
实正交矩阵是酉矩阵的特例：
$$O(n)=U(n)\cap M_n(\mathbb R).$$
$U(n)$ 的元素是 $\mathbb C^n$ 上保持 Hermitian 内积 $\langle x,y\rangle=y^{\mathrm H}x$ 的线性变换的矩阵。

对 $A\in O(n)$ 与 $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$，
$$\langle Ax,Ay\rangle=(Ax)^{\mathrm T}(Ay)=x^{\mathrm T}A^{\mathrm T}Ay=x^{\mathrm T}y=\langle x,y\rangle.$$
取 $y=x$ 得 $\|Ax\|=\|x\|$。反过来，若 $A$ 对所有 $x,y$ 都保内积，取标准基 $e_i,e_j$ 得
$$(A^{\mathrm T}A)_{ij}=\langle Ae_i,Ae_j\rangle=\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=\delta_{ij},$$
故 $A^{\mathrm T}A=E_n$。所以 $O(n)$ 恰好是保长度、保内积的矩阵群。二维情形可完全参数化：若 $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in SO(2)$，由 $A^{\mathrm T}A=E_2$ 与 $\det A=1$ 得 $A^{-1}=A^{\mathrm T}=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\b&d\end{pmatrix}$，而 $A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$，比较得 $d=a$、$c=-b$、$a^2+b^2=1$，故存在唯一 $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ 使
$$A=R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.$$
并且 $R(\theta)R(\varphi)=R(\theta+\varphi)$、$R(0)=E_2$、$R(\theta)^{-1}=R(-\theta)$，所以 $SO(2)\cong U(1)$（映射 $R(\theta)\mapsto e^{i\theta}$）。$SO(3)$ 则不交换：两个不同轴的三维旋转一般不可交换。

固定 $P\in GL(n,K)$，**相似变换** $A\mapsto P^{-1}AP$ 与**合同变换** $A\mapsto P^{\mathrm T}AP$ 都是 $GL(n,K)$ 在矩阵空间上的作用，但作用对象与不变量不同。相似来自换基：若线性变换 $T$ 在基 $\mathcal B$ 下的矩阵为 $A$，在新基 $\mathcal B'$ 下为 $P^{-1}AP$，其中 $P$ 是过渡矩阵；因此相似保持特征多项式、特征值、迹、行列式、秩与 Jordan 标准形。合同来自二次型或双线性型的换基：若 $A$ 对称，则
$$(P^{\mathrm T}AP)^{\mathrm T}=P^{\mathrm T}A^{\mathrm T}P=P^{\mathrm T}AP,$$
仍对称；合同保持秩与惯性指数 $(p,q)$（Sylvester 惯性定理），但一般**不保持特征值**。例如
$$A=\operatorname{diag}(1,1),\qquad P=\operatorname{diag}(2,1),$$
则 $P^{\mathrm T}AP=\operatorname{diag}(4,1)$，特征值从 $(1,1)$ 变为 $(4,1)$，而秩与正惯性指数不变。复 Hermitian 情形把 $P^{\mathrm T}$ 换成 $P^{\mathrm H}$；相似与合同是两种不同的作用，不能混用不变量。
derivationEn:
Let $K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $M_n(K)$ be the set of $n\times n$ matrices. A subset $G\subseteq M_n(K)$ is a **matrix group** if $E_n\in G$; $A,B\in G$ implies $AB\in G$; and $A\in G$ implies $A$ is invertible with $A^{-1}\in G$. Equivalently, $G$ is a group under matrix multiplication. The basic example is
$$GL(n,K)=\{A\in M_n(K):\det A\ne0\},$$
the **general linear group**. It is indeed a group: $\det(AB)=\det A\det B\ne0$, $\det E=1$, and $\det(A^{-1})=1/\det A$, so it is closed under multiplication and contains the identity and inverses; associativity is inherited from matrix multiplication. The elements of $GL(n,K)$ are exactly the matrices of invertible linear transformations of $K^n$ in the standard basis.

The determinant gives a group homomorphism
$$\det:GL(n,K)\to K^{\times},$$
where $K^{\times}=K\setminus\{0\}$ is a group under multiplication; $\det(AB)=\det A\det B$ shows that it is a homomorphism. Its kernel
$$SL(n,K)=\{A\in GL(n,K):\det A=1\}$$
is the **special linear group**. A kernel is automatically normal: if $S\in SL(n,K)$ and $P\in GL(n,K)$, then
$$\det(P^{-1}SP)=\det(P)^{-1}\det(S)\det(P)=1,$$
so $P^{-1}SP\in SL(n,K)$. Geometrically, $SL(n,\mathbb R)$ consists of the linear transformations preserving oriented volume; for $n\ge2$ it is not a subgroup of $O(n)$, and the two meet exactly in
$$SL(n,\mathbb R)\cap O(n)=SO(n).$$

The **orthogonal group** is
$$O(n)=\{A\in M_n(\mathbb R):A^{\mathrm T}A=E_n\}.$$
If $A,B\in O(n)$, then
$$(AB)^{\mathrm T}(AB)=B^{\mathrm T}A^{\mathrm T}AB=B^{\mathrm T}B=E_n,$$
so $AB\in O(n)$; $E_n\in O(n)$; and $A^{\mathrm T}A=E_n$ shows that $A$ is invertible with $A^{-1}=A^{\mathrm T}$, while $A^{\mathrm T}\in O(n)$, so $A^{-1}\in O(n)$. Hence $O(n)$ is a matrix group. Taking determinants,
$$(\det A)^2=\det(A^{\mathrm T}A)=\det E_n=1,$$
so $\det A=\pm1$. Define
$$SO(n)=\{A\in O(n):\det A=1\}=O(n)\cap SL(n,\mathbb R).$$
It has index $2$ in $O(n)$ for $n\ge1$: $\det$ takes both values $+1$ and $-1$ on $O(n)$ (for instance at $E_n$ and $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\dots,1)$), and the two cosets are $SO(n)$ and $\{A\in O(n):\det A=-1\}$.

The **unitary group** is
$$U(n)=\{A\in M_n(\mathbb C):A^{\mathrm H}A=E_n\},\qquad A^{\mathrm H}=\overline{A}^{\mathrm T}.$$
The computation is the same as for the orthogonal group: if $A,B\in U(n)$, then
$$(AB)^{\mathrm H}(AB)=B^{\mathrm H}A^{\mathrm H}AB=B^{\mathrm H}B=E_n,$$
and $A^{-1}=A^{\mathrm H}\in U(n)$, so $U(n)$ is a matrix group. Taking determinants,
$$|\det A|^2=\det(A^{\mathrm H}A)=1,$$
so $\det A$ is a complex number of modulus $1$; this is not the condition $\det A=\pm1$, which is stronger. The **special unitary group** is
$$SU(n)=\{A\in U(n):\det A=1\}=U(n)\cap SL(n,\mathbb C).$$
Real orthogonal matrices are special unitary ones:
$$O(n)=U(n)\cap M_n(\mathbb R).$$
Elements of $U(n)$ are the matrices of linear transformations of $\mathbb C^n$ preserving the Hermitian inner product $\langle x,y\rangle=y^{\mathrm H}x$.

For $A\in O(n)$ and $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$\langle Ax,Ay\rangle=(Ax)^{\mathrm T}(Ay)=x^{\mathrm T}A^{\mathrm T}Ay=x^{\mathrm T}y=\langle x,y\rangle.$$
Taking $y=x$ gives $\|Ax\|=\|x\|$. Conversely, if $A$ preserves all inner products, then taking $x=e_i$, $y=e_j$ in the standard basis gives
$$(A^{\mathrm T}A)_{ij}=\langle Ae_i,Ae_j\rangle=\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=\delta_{ij},$$
so $A^{\mathrm T}A=E_n$. Thus $O(n)$ is exactly the group of matrices preserving lengths and inner products. In dimension two there is a complete parametrization: if $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in SO(2)$, then $A^{\mathrm T}A=E_2$ and $\det A=1$ give $A^{-1}=A^{\mathrm T}=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\b&d\end{pmatrix}$ and $A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$; comparing them yields $d=a$, $c=-b$, and $a^2+b^2=1$, so there is a unique $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ with
$$A=R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.$$
Moreover $R(\theta)R(\varphi)=R(\theta+\varphi)$, $R(0)=E_2$, and $R(\theta)^{-1}=R(-\theta)$, so $SO(2)\cong U(1)$ via $R(\theta)\mapsto e^{i\theta}$. By contrast, $SO(3)$ is not abelian: rotations about different axes generally do not commute.

Fix $P\in GL(n,K)$. The **similarity transformation** $A\mapsto P^{-1}AP$ and the **congruence transformation** $A\mapsto P^{\mathrm T}AP$ are both actions of $GL(n,K)$ on matrix space, but they act on different objects and preserve different invariants. Similarity comes from a change of basis: if a linear map $T$ has matrix $A$ in a basis $\mathcal B$ and matrix $P^{-1}AP$ in a new basis $\mathcal B'$, where $P$ is the transition matrix, then similarity preserves the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues, trace, determinant, rank, and Jordan form. Congruence comes from a change of basis for a quadratic or bilinear form: if $A$ is symmetric, then
$$(P^{\mathrm T}AP)^{\mathrm T}=P^{\mathrm T}A^{\mathrm T}P=P^{\mathrm T}AP,$$
so it remains symmetric. Congruence preserves rank and the inertia indices $(p,q)$ by Sylvester's law of inertia, but it generally **does not preserve eigenvalues**. For example,
$$A=\operatorname{diag}(1,1),\qquad P=\operatorname{diag}(2,1),$$
give $P^{\mathrm T}AP=\operatorname{diag}(4,1)$: the eigenvalues change from $(1,1)$ to $(4,1)$, while the rank and positive inertia index stay the same. For complex Hermitian forms, replace $P^{\mathrm T}$ by $P^{\mathrm H}$. Similarity and congruence are different actions, and their invariants must not be mixed.

formulas.note: 一般线性群与特殊线性群：$GL(n)$ 是可逆矩阵的集合，$SL(n)$ 是其中行列式为 1 的部分，它正是行列式同态的核，因而是正规子群。
formulas.noteEn: General and special linear groups: $GL(n)$ consists of invertible matrices, while $SL(n)$ is the determinant-one part, exactly the kernel of the determinant homomorphism and hence a normal subgroup.

formulas.latex: O(n)=\{A:\ A^{\mathsf T}A=E\},\qquad A\in O(n)\ \Longrightarrow\ \det A=\pm1,\qquad SO(n)=\{A\in O(n):\ \det A=1\}
formulas.note: 正交群由保内积的矩阵组成；取行列式得 $\det A=\pm1$。$SO(n)$ 挑出其中行列式为 1 的旋转，$\det=-1$ 的元素含反射。
formulas.noteEn: The orthogonal group consists of the inner-product preserving matrices; taking determinants gives $\det A=\pm1$. The subgroup $SO(n)$ singles out the rotations, while elements with $\det=-1$ contain reflections.

formulas.note: $SO(2)$ 的完整参数化：$R(\theta)$ 把 $(1,0)$ 送到 $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$，即逆时针旋转 $\theta$（$\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$ 时得到 $(0,1)$）。
formulas.noteEn: The complete parametrization of $SO(2)$: $R(\theta)$ sends $(1,0)$ to $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, a counterclockwise rotation by $\theta$ (for $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$ this is $(0,1)$).

formulas.latex: U(n)=\{A:\ A^{\mathsf H}A=E\},\qquad SU(n)=\{A\in U(n):\ \det A=1\}
formulas.note: 酉群与特殊酉群：复数域上把转置换成共轭转置，$A^{\mathsf H}A=E$ 保证保复内积；$SU(2)$ 是量子力学自旋与 $SO(3)$ 之间的桥梁。
formulas.noteEn: Unitary and special unitary groups: over the complex numbers the transpose is replaced by the conjugate transpose, and $A^{\mathsf H}A=E$ ensures preservation of the Hermitian inner product; $SU(2)$ bridges $SO(3)$ and spin in quantum mechanics.

formulas.latex: A\mapsto P^{-1}AP\quad(\text{相似变换}),\qquad A\mapsto P^{\mathsf T}AP\quad(\text{合同变换})
formulas.note: 两个完全不同的群作用：相似作用于「线性映射的矩阵」，保持特征值与若尔当标准形；合同作用于「二次型的矩阵」，保持秩与惯性指数（复 Hermite 型把 $P^{\mathsf T}$ 换成 $P^{\mathsf H}$）。
formulas.noteEn: Two genuinely different group actions: similarity acts on matrices of linear maps and preserves eigenvalues and Jordan form; congruence acts on matrices of quadratic forms and preserves rank and inertia (for complex Hermitian forms replace $P^{\mathsf T}$ by $P^{\mathsf H}$).

properties: $SL(n)=\ker(\det)$ 是 $GL(n)$ 的正规子群；$SO(n)=O(n)\cap SL(n)$ 在 $O(n)$ 中指数为 2——$O(n)$ 分成 $\det=+1$ 与 $\det=-1$ 两个连通分支，只有前者含单位矩阵。
正交矩阵的几何：$\langle Ax,Ay\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle$、$\|Ax\|=\|x\|$、$|\det A|=1$（保夹角、保长度、保体积）；正交矩阵的行向量与列向量分别构成标准正交基。
$\det=+1$ 是旋转、$\det=-1$ 含反射：$O(2)$ 中 $\det=-1$ 的变换恰是关于某条过原点直线的反射；$O(3)$ 中 $\det=-1$ 的变换是旋转与镜面反射的复合（例如中心对称 $-E$）。
相似与合同是两个不同的作用：相似保持特征值、迹、行列式、若尔当标准形（线性映射的结构不变量）；合同保持对称性、秩与惯性指数（二次型的不变量），但不保持特征值。混用会得到错误的不变量结论。
$SO(2)$ 是交换群且 $R(\theta)R(\varphi)=R(\theta+\varphi)$，与复数单位圆群 $U(1)$ 同构（$R(\theta)\leftrightarrow e^{i\theta}$）；而 $SO(3)$ 不交换。矩阵群由此把几何对称性代数化。
propertiesEn: $SL(n)=\ker(\det)$ is a normal subgroup of $GL(n)$; moreover $SO(n)=O(n)\cap SL(n)$ has index 2 in $O(n)$ — the group $O(n)$ splits into the two connected pieces $\det=+1$ and $\det=-1$, only the first of which contains the identity.

Geometry of orthogonal matrices: $\langle Ax,Ay\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle$, $\|Ax\|=\|x\|$ and $|\det A|=1$ (angles, lengths and volumes are preserved); the rows and the columns of an orthogonal matrix are orthonormal bases.

Determinant $+1$ means rotation, determinant $-1$ involves reflection: in $O(2)$ an element of determinant $-1$ is exactly a reflection in a line through the origin; in $O(3)$ it is a rotation composed with a mirror reflection (for instance the central symmetry $-E$).

Similarity and congruence are different actions: similarity preserves eigenvalues, trace, determinant and Jordan form (the structure of a linear map), whereas congruence preserves symmetry, rank and inertia indices (the invariants of a quadratic form) but not eigenvalues. Mixing them up produces false invariant claims.

$SO(2)$ is abelian with $R(\theta)R(\varphi)=R(\theta+\varphi)$ and is isomorphic to the unit circle group $U(1)$ via $R(\theta)\leftrightarrow e^{i\theta}$, while $SO(3)$ is not abelian. Matrix groups thus algebraize geometric symmetry.

examples.problem: 验证 $R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}$ 属于 $SO(2)$，说明它是旋转（写出 $(1,0)$ 的像），并验证它保长度。
examples.solution:
正交性：$R(\theta)^{\mathsf T}R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&\sin\theta\\-\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta&-\cos\theta\sin\theta+\sin\theta\cos\theta\\-\sin\theta\cos\theta+\cos\theta\sin\theta&\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ ✓，故 $R(\theta)\in O(2)$；又 $\det R(\theta)=\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$ ✓，故 $R(\theta)\in SO(2)$。
旋转方向：$R(\theta)\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta\\ \sin\theta\end{pmatrix}$。当 $\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ 时像为 $(0,1)$，正是逆时针转 $90^\circ$，说明 $R(\theta)$ 是逆时针旋转 $\theta$ ✓。
保长度：对任意 $v=(x,y)$，$\|R(\theta)v\|^2=(Rv)^{\mathsf T}(Rv)=v^{\mathsf T}R^{\mathsf T}Rv=v^{\mathsf T}v=x^2+y^2=\|v\|^2$ ✓。数值例：$v=(1,1)$、$\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{4}$ 时 $R v=(\cos45^\circ-\sin45^\circ,\ \sin45^\circ+\cos45^\circ)=(0,\sqrt2)$，模方 $0+2=2=\|v\|^2$ ✓。

examples.problem: 给出 $O(2)$ 中一个行列式为 $-1$ 的例子 $S$，验证 $S^{\mathsf T}S=E$ 与 $\det S=-1$，并求它的不动点集。
examples.solution:
取 $S=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$（关于 $x$ 轴对称）。$S^{\mathsf T}=S$，且 $S^2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}=E$，故 $S^{\mathsf T}S=E$ ✓，$S\in O(2)$；$\det S=1\cdot(-1)-0\cdot0=-1$ ✓，所以 $S$ 不是旋转（$S\notin SO(2)$），而是反射。
不动点：$S(x,y)=(x,-y)=(x,y)$ 要求 $y=0$，故不动点集是 $x$ 轴 $\{(t,0):t\in\mathbb{R}\}$，正是关于 $x$ 轴的反射 ✓。
保长度验证：$\|S(x,y)\|^2=x^2+(-y)^2=x^2+y^2$ ✓；特征值为 $1$ 与 $-1$，与 $\operatorname{tr}S=0$、$\det S=-1$ 一致。另一例是 $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$（关于直线 $y=x$ 的反射），行列式同样为 $-1$。

dual-bilinear.definition:
设 $V$ 是域 $K$ 上的线性空间。从 $V$ 到 $K$ 的线性映射 $f:V\to K$ 称为**线性函数**（线性泛函），全体线性函数在逐点加法与数乘下构成线性空间 $V^*=\mathcal{L}(V,K)$，称为 $V$ 的**对偶空间**。若 $e_1,\dots,e_n$ 是 $V$ 的基，则由 $\varepsilon_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$ 唯一确定的 $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n$ 构成 $V^*$ 的基（**对偶基**），于是有限维时 $\dim V^*=\dim V$。

虽然维数相同，$V$ 与 $V^*$ 之间却**没有自然的同构**——每一个同构都依赖基的选取。相比之下，$V$ 到**双对偶** $V^{\ast\ast}$ 有一个天然嵌入 $\iota(\alpha)(f)=f(\alpha)$：它不依赖任何基，而且总是单射；当且仅当 $V$ 有限维时 $\iota$ 才是满射、从而是同构。这个「有限维」条件不能省：无限维空间里 $\iota(V)$ 只是 $V^{\ast\ast}$ 的真子集。

对子集 $S\subseteq V$ 定义**零化子** $S^\circ=\{f\in V^*: f(s)=0,\ \forall s\in S\}$，它是 $V^*$ 的子空间，有限维时满足 $\dim S+\dim S^\circ=\dim V$。零化子是用线性函数描述子空间的方式：线性方程组 $Ax=0$ 的解空间正是行向量空间（作为 $K^n$ 上的线性函数全体中的子空间）的零化子——列向量语言说「$x$ 与每一行正交」，对偶空间语言说「$x$ 落在零化子里」，两者是同一件事。

**双线性型**是双变量版本：$B:V\times V\to K$ 对每个变量分别线性。对称（$B(\alpha,\beta)=B(\beta,\alpha)$）与反对称（$B(\alpha,\beta)=-B(\beta,\alpha)$）是最重要的两类。对称双线性型与**二次型** $Q(\alpha)=B(\alpha,\alpha)$ 一一对应：在特征不等于 2 的域上，$B$ 可以由 $Q$ 经极化恒等式 $B(\alpha,\beta)=\frac12\big(Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)\big)$ 恢复。取定基后 $B(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay$，而 $B$ 对称当且仅当矩阵 $A$ 对称——这条通道把双线性型的理论与二次型标准形、惯性指数完全对接起来。
dual-bilinear.definitionEn:
Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$. A linear map $f:V\to K$ is called a **linear functional**, and the set of all of them, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication, is a vector space $V^*=\mathcal{L}(V,K)$, the **dual space** of $V$. If $e_1,\dots,e_n$ is a basis of $V$, the functionals $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n$ uniquely determined by $\varepsilon_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$ form a basis of $V^*$ (the **dual basis**), so in finite dimension $\dim V^*=\dim V$.

Although the dimensions agree, there is **no natural isomorphism** between $V$ and $V^*$: every isomorphism depends on a choice of basis. By contrast, $V$ has a canonical embedding into the **double dual** $V^{\ast\ast}$, namely $\iota(\alpha)(f)=f(\alpha)$. It uses no basis and is always injective; it is surjective, hence an isomorphism, exactly when $V$ is finite dimensional. This finiteness hypothesis cannot be dropped: in infinite dimension $\iota(V)$ is a proper subset of $V^{\ast\ast}$.

For a subset $S\subseteq V$ define the **annihilator** $S^\circ=\{f\in V^*: f(s)=0\ \text{for all } s\in S\}$, a subspace of $V^*$ that in finite dimension satisfies $\dim S+\dim S^\circ=\dim V$. The annihilator is the way to describe subspaces through functionals: the solution space of $Ax=0$ is exactly the annihilator of the row space (viewed as a subspace of the linear functionals on $K^n$). The column-vector language says 「$x$ is orthogonal to every row」; the dual language says 「$x$ lies in the annihilator」 — the same statement in two dialects.

A **bilinear form** is the two-variable counterpart: a map $B:V\times V\to K$ linear in each variable separately. Symmetric forms ($B(\alpha,\beta)=B(\beta,\alpha)$) and antisymmetric forms ($B(\alpha,\beta)=-B(\beta,\alpha)$) are the fundamental classes. A symmetric bilinear form and the **quadratic form** $Q(\alpha)=B(\alpha,\alpha)$ determine each other: over a field of characteristic not 2, $B$ is recovered from $Q$ by the polarization identity $B(\alpha,\beta)=\frac12\big(Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)\big)$. Once a basis is fixed, $B(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay$, and $B$ is symmetric if and only if $A$ is symmetric — the bridge connecting bilinear forms to the standard form of a quadratic form and to inertia indices.
derivation: 设 $V$ 是域 $K$ 上的 $n$ 维线性空间，$e_1,\dots,e_n$ 是一组基。线性函数 $f:V\to K$ 的全体构成对偶空间 $V^*=\mathcal{L}(V,K)$。定义 $\varepsilon_i\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_je_j\right)=a_i$，则 $\varepsilon_i$ 线性且 $\varepsilon_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$。对任意 $f\in V^*$，$f(\alpha)=\sum_i a_if(e_i)$，故 $f=\sum_i f(e_i)\varepsilon_i$，说明 $\{\varepsilon_i\}$ 张成 $V^*$；若 $\sum_i c_i\varepsilon_i=0$，代入 $e_j$ 得 $c_j=0$，说明它们线性无关。因此 $\{\varepsilon_i\}$ 是 $V^*$ 的基（对偶基），$\dim V^*=n$。

对偶基依赖原基的选取，不能把 $V$ 与 $V^*$ 自然等同。若新基 $e'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$（矩阵 $P=(p_{ij})$ 可逆），设对偶基 $\varepsilon'_i=\sum_k a_{ik}\varepsilon_k$，则由 $$\begin{aligned}\varepsilon'_i(e'_j)&=\sum_k a_{ik}\varepsilon_k(e'_j)\\&=\sum_k a_{ik}p_{kj}=(AP)_{ij}=\delta_{ij}.\end{aligned}$$ 得 $A=P^{-1}$，即 $\varepsilon'_i=\sum_k(P^{-1})_{ik}\varepsilon_k$。原基按 $P$ 变换，对偶基按 $P^{-1}$ 反向变换；这正是「没有自然同构」的具体含义。

双对偶与自然嵌入：定义 $\iota:V\to V^{**}$，$\iota(\alpha)(f)=f(\alpha)$。它不依赖任何基，且是线性的。若 $\iota(\alpha)=0$，则对所有 $f\in V^*$ 有 $f(\alpha)=0$；当 $\alpha\ne0$ 时，把 $\alpha$ 扩充为基，并令 $f(\alpha)=1$、其余基向量映为 $0$，得到 $f(\alpha)=1$，矛盾，故 $\alpha=0$，$\iota$ 单射。有限维时 $\dim V^{**}=\dim V^*=\dim V$，单射的线性映射在等维空间之间必为满射，故 $\iota$ 是同构；无限维时 $\iota(V)$ 只是 $V^{**}$ 的真子集（这是无限维的标准结论），「有限维」条件不能省。

零化子：对子空间 $S\le V$，定义 $$S^{\circ}=\{f\in V^*: f(s)=0,\ \forall s\in S\}.$$ 取 $S$ 的基 $e_1,\dots,e_k$ 并扩充为 $V$ 的基 $e_1,\dots,e_n$，对偶基为 $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n$。若 $f=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\varepsilon_i$，则 $f(e_j)=a_j$（$j\le k$），故 $f\in S^{\circ}\iff a_1=\cdots=a_k=0$，即 $S^{\circ}=\operatorname{span}\{\varepsilon_{k+1},\dots,\varepsilon_n\}$。因此 $$\dim S+\dim S^{\circ}=k+(n-k)=n=\dim V.$$

双线性型：$B:V\times V\to K$ 对两个变量分别线性。取基 $e_1,\dots,e_n$，令 $A=(B(e_i,e_j))$。若 $x=\sum_i x_ie_i$、$y=\sum_j y_je_j$，则由双线性 $$B(x,y)=\sum_{i,j}x_iy_jB(e_i,e_j)=x^{T}Ay.$$ 换基 $e'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$ 时坐标满足 $x=Px'$、$y=Py'$，故 $$B(x,y)=(x')^{T}(P^{T}AP)y',$$ 即矩阵按合同 $A\mapsto P^{T}AP$ 变换。$B$ 对称（$B(x,y)=B(y,x)$）当且仅当 $A^{T}=A$；合同保持秩，但不保持特征值。

对称双线性型与二次型：令 $Q(\alpha)=B(\alpha,\alpha)$。直接展开得 $$Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha).$$ 当 $B$ 对称时右边为 $2B(\alpha,\beta)$，故当域的特征不等于 $2$ 时 $$B(\alpha,\beta)=\frac12\big(Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)\big),$$ 二次型与对称双线性型互相唯一决定。特征不等于 $2$ 时，若 $B$ 反对称，则 $B(\alpha,\alpha)=0$、$Q\equiv0$，极化恒等式只恢复对称部分 $\frac12(B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha))$；特征 $2$ 时不能除以 $2$，上述对应失效。
derivationEn: Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over $K$ with basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$. The set of all linear functionals $f:V\to K$ forms the dual space $V^*=\mathcal{L}(V,K)$. Define $\varepsilon_i(\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_je_j)=a_i$; then $\varepsilon_i$ is linear and $\varepsilon_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$. For any $f\in V^*$, $f(\alpha)=\sum_i a_if(e_i)$, so $f=\sum_i f(e_i)\varepsilon_i$ and the $\varepsilon_i$ span $V^*$. If $\sum_i c_i\varepsilon_i=0$, evaluating at $e_j$ gives $c_j=0$, so they are independent. Hence $\{\varepsilon_i\}$ is a basis of $V^*$ (the dual basis), and $\dim V^*=n$.

The dual basis depends on the choice of basis, so $V$ and $V^*$ cannot be naturally identified. If a new basis is $e'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$ with $P=(p_{ij})$ invertible, and $\varepsilon'_i=\sum_k a_{ik}\varepsilon_k$, then $$\varepsilon'_i(e'_j)=\sum_k a_{ik}\varepsilon_k\left(\sum_l p_{lj}e_l\right)=\sum_k a_{ik}p_{kj}=(AP)_{ij}=\delta_{ij},$$ so $A=P^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon'_i=\sum_k(P^{-1})_{ik}\varepsilon_k$. The original basis changes by $P$, while the dual basis changes by $P^{-1}$ in the opposite direction; this is the concrete meaning of 'no natural isomorphism'.

Double dual and canonical embedding: define $\iota:V\to V^{**}$ by $\iota(\alpha)(f)=f(\alpha)$. It uses no basis and is linear. If $\iota(\alpha)=0$, then $f(\alpha)=0$ for every $f\in V^*$. If $\alpha\ne0$, extend $\alpha$ to a basis and define $f$ to be $1$ on $\alpha$ and $0$ on the other basis vectors, giving $f(\alpha)=1$, a contradiction. Hence $\alpha=0$ and $\iota$ is injective. In finite dimension $\dim V^{**}=\dim V^*=\dim V$, so an injective linear map between spaces of equal dimension is surjective, and $\iota$ is an isomorphism. In infinite dimension $\iota(V)$ is a proper subset of $V^{**}$ (a standard infinite-dimensional fact); the finite-dimensional hypothesis cannot be dropped.

Annihilator: for a subspace $S\le V$, define $$S^{\circ}=\{f\in V^*: f(s)=0\ \text{for all }s\in S\}.$$ Choose a basis $e_1,\dots,e_k$ of $S$ and extend it to a basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ of $V$, with dual basis $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n$. If $f=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\varepsilon_i$, then $f(e_j)=a_j$ for $j\le k$; hence $f\in S^{\circ}$ iff $a_1=\cdots=a_k=0$, i.e. $S^{\circ}=\operatorname{span}\{\varepsilon_{k+1},\dots,\varepsilon_n\}$. Therefore $$\dim S+\dim S^{\circ}=k+(n-k)=n=\dim V.$$

Bilinear forms: a map $B:V\times V\to K$ is bilinear if it is linear in each variable separately. Fix a basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ and let $A=(B(e_i,e_j))$. For $x=\sum_i x_ie_i$ and $y=\sum_j y_je_j$, bilinearity gives $$B(x,y)=\sum_{i,j}x_iy_jB(e_i,e_j)=x^{T}Ay.$$ Under a change of basis $e'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$ the coordinates satisfy $x=Px'$, $y=Py'$, hence $$B(x,y)=(x')^{T}(P^{T}AP)y',$$ so the matrix transforms by congruence $A\mapsto P^{T}AP$. The form $B$ is symmetric ($B(x,y)=B(y,x)$) iff $A^{T}=A$; congruence preserves rank but not eigenvalues.

Symmetric bilinear forms and quadratic forms: put $Q(\alpha)=B(\alpha,\alpha)$. Direct expansion gives $$Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha).$$ If $B$ is symmetric, the right side is $2B(\alpha,\beta)$, so over a field of characteristic not $2$, $$B(\alpha,\beta)=\frac12\big(Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)\big),$$ and the quadratic form and the symmetric bilinear form determine each other uniquely. Over a field of characteristic not $2$, an antisymmetric $B$ satisfies $B(\alpha,\alpha)=0$ and $Q\equiv0$, so polarization recovers only the symmetric part $\frac12(B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha))$; in characteristic $2$ division by $2$ is impossible and this correspondence fails.

formulas.note: 对偶空间与对偶基：$\varepsilon_i$ 由它在基上的取值 $\delta_{ij}$ 唯一确定；有限维时对偶空间的维数与原来的空间相同。
formulas.noteEn: Dual space and dual basis: each $\varepsilon_i$ is uniquely determined by its values $\delta_{ij}$ on a basis, and in finite dimension the dual has the same dimension as the original space.

formulas.latex: \iota:V\to V^{\ast\ast},\quad \iota(\alpha)(f)=f(\alpha);\qquad \iota\ \text{总是单射},\ \text{且仅当 } \dim V<\infty\ \text{时为同构}
formulas.note: 自然嵌入：不依赖任何基。单射对任意维数都成立；「满射」需要有限维这个条件，无限维时 $\iota(V)$ 只是真子集。
formulas.noteEn: The natural embedding uses no basis. Injectivity always holds; surjectivity requires finite dimension, for in infinite dimension $\iota(V)$ is a proper subset.

formulas.latex: S^{\circ}=\{f\in V^*:\ f(s)=0\ \forall s\in S\},\qquad \dim S+\dim S^{\circ}=\dim V
formulas.note: 零化子及其维数公式（有限维）：$S$ 越大零化子越小。线性方程组 $Ax=0$ 的解空间正是行向量空间的零化子（链接 homogeneous-solutions）。
formulas.noteEn: Annihilator and its dimension formula in finite dimension: the larger $S$ is, the smaller $S^\circ$. The solution space of $Ax=0$ is precisely the annihilator of the row space (see homogeneous-solutions).

formulas.note: 极化恒等式（域的特征不等于 2）：对称双线性型与二次型互相唯一决定。对一般双线性型，右边只给出对称部分 $\frac12\big(B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha)\big)$（链接 quadratic-form-standard）。
formulas.noteEn: Polarization identity (characteristic not 2): a symmetric bilinear form and its quadratic form determine each other. For a general bilinear form the right-hand side returns only the symmetric part $\frac12(B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha))$ (see quadratic-form-standard).

formulas.latex: B(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay,\qquad A=(B(e_i,e_j)),\qquad B\ \text{对称}\iff A^{\mathsf T}=A
formulas.note: 双线性型的矩阵表示：$A$ 由基上的取值唯一确定；对称性在矩阵上就是 $A$ 对称。换基 $P$ 时 $A\mapsto P^{\mathsf T}AP$（合同），故只有秩与惯性指数是内在不变量（链接 positive-definite-inertia）。
formulas.noteEn: Matrix representation of a bilinear form: $A$ is determined by the values on the basis, and symmetry of the form is symmetry of $A$. Under a change of basis $P$ one has $A\mapsto P^{\mathsf T}AP$ (congruence), so only rank and inertia indices are intrinsic (see positive-definite-inertia).

properties: 对偶基 $\varepsilon_i$ 由 $\varepsilon_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$ 唯一确定；有限维时 $V\cong V^*$，但任何同构都依赖基的选取，而 $\iota:V\to V^{\ast\ast}$ 是自然的。$\iota$ 为同构的充要条件是 $\dim V<\infty$——无限维时它只是单射，这条条件必须写明。

零化子的维数公式 $\dim S+\dim S^{\circ}=\dim V$（$S$ 为子空间）；并且恒有 $(S^{\circ})^{\circ}\supseteq\iota(S)\subseteq V^{\ast\ast}$，有限维时 $(S^{\circ})^{\circ}=\iota(\operatorname{span}S)$——当 $S$ 是子空间时这正好是 $\iota(S)$（即 $S$ 本身）。它把子空间与「约束方程」对偶起来：子空间越大，零化子越小。
线性方程组语言：$Ax=0$ 的解空间等于行空间的零化子（在自然等同 $V^{\ast\ast}\cong V$ 之下），取维数立刻得到 $\operatorname{rank}A+\dim\ker A=n$。对偶语言与「与每一行正交」的列向量语言是同一件事的两种说法。

对称双线性型与二次型一一对应（域的特征不等于 2）：$Q(\alpha)=B(\alpha,\alpha)$，极化恒等式反向恢复 $B$。对一般双线性型，极化只恢复对称部分 $\frac12\big(B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha)\big)$；反对称型满足 $B(\alpha,\alpha)=0$（特征不等于 2 时与反对称等价），此时 $Q\equiv0$，二次型完全丢失反对称部分的信息。
矩阵表示：$B(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay$ 中的 $A=(B(e_i,e_j))$ 唯一；$B$ 对称 $\iff A$ 对称；换基 $P$ 时 $A\mapsto P^{\mathsf T}AP$，因此秩与惯性指数（正负惯性指数、符号差）是 $B$ 的内在不变量——这正是二次型标准形理论的内容。
propertiesEn: The dual basis $\varepsilon_i$ is uniquely determined by $\varepsilon_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$; in finite dimension $V\cong V^*$, but every isomorphism depends on a basis, whereas $\iota:V\to V^{\ast\ast}$ is canonical. It is an isomorphism if and only if $\dim V<\infty$ — in infinite dimension it is only injective, and this hypothesis must be stated.

Annihilator dimension formula $\dim S+\dim S^{\circ}=\dim V$, and always $(S^{\circ})^{\circ}\supseteq\iota(S)\subseteq V^{\ast\ast}$, with equality $(S^{\circ})^{\circ}=\iota(S)$ (that is, $S$ itself) in finite dimension. It pairs subspaces with the constraints that cut them out: the larger the subspace, the smaller its annihilator.

Linear systems: the solution space of $Ax=0$ equals the annihilator of the row space (under the natural identification $V^{\ast\ast}\cong V$), and counting dimensions immediately gives $\operatorname{rank}A+\dim\ker A=n$. The dual phrasing and the column-vector phrasing 「orthogonal to every row」 say the same thing.

Symmetric bilinear forms correspond one-to-one with quadratic forms when the characteristic is not 2: $Q(\alpha)=B(\alpha,\alpha)$ and polarization recovers $B$. For a general bilinear form polarization recovers only the symmetric part $\frac12(B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha))$; an antisymmetric form satisfies $B(\alpha,\alpha)=0$ (equivalent to antisymmetry when the characteristic is not 2), and then $Q\equiv0$, so the quadratic form retains no information about the antisymmetric part.

Matrix representation: the matrix $A=(B(e_i,e_j))$ in $B(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay$ is unique; $B$ is symmetric $\iff$ $A$ is symmetric; under a change of basis $P$ one has $A\mapsto P^{\mathsf T}AP$, so rank and inertia indices (the numbers of positive and negative squares, and their difference) are the intrinsic invariants of $B$ — exactly the content of the standard form theory of quadratic forms.

examples.problem: 在 $\mathbb{R}^2$ 上定义 $B(x,y)=x_1y_1+2x_1y_2+3x_2y_2$（$x=(x_1,x_2)$、$y=(y_1,y_2)$）。判断 $B$ 是否对称、写出其矩阵 $A$，并用极化恒等式在 $x=(1,2)$、$y=(3,-1)$ 处回代验证。
examples.solution:
写矩阵：$A=\begin{pmatrix}B(e_1,e_1)&B(e_1,e_2)\\B(e_2,e_1)&B(e_2,e_2)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$。
判断对称性：$B(y,x)=y_1x_1+2y_1x_2+3y_2x_2=x_1y_1+2x_2y_1+3x_2y_2$。取 $x=(1,2)$、$y=(3,-1)$：$B(x,y)=1\cdot3+2\cdot1\cdot(-1)+3\cdot2\cdot(-1)=3-2-6=-5$；$B(y,x)=3\cdot1+2\cdot3\cdot2+3\cdot(-1)\cdot2=3+12-6=9$。$-5\ne9$，故 $B$ 不对称 ✓（矩阵也不对称：$A_{12}=2\ne0=A_{21}$）。
对称部分：$B_s(x,y)=\tfrac12\big(B(x,y)+B(y,x)\big)=x_1y_1+x_1y_2+x_2y_1+3x_2y_2$，矩阵 $\tfrac12(A+A^{\mathsf T})=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$ ✓。
二次型：$Q(x)=B(x,x)=x_1^2+(2+0)x_1x_2+3x_2^2=x_1^2+2x_1x_2+3x_2^2$。
极化恒等式回代：$Q(x)=1+2\cdot1\cdot2+3\cdot4=17$；$Q(y)=9+2\cdot3\cdot(-1)+3\cdot1=6$；$Q(x+y)=Q(4,1)=16+2\cdot4\cdot1+3=27$。于是 $\tfrac12\big(Q(x+y)-Q(x)-Q(y)\big)=\tfrac12(27-17-6)=2$，而 $B_s(x,y)=\tfrac12(-5+9)=2$ ✓，两者一致；注意极化给出的是对称部分 $B_s$，而不是原来的 $B$（$B(x,y)=-5\ne2$）。

examples.problem: 在 $V=\mathbb{R}^2$ 中取基 $e_1=(1,1)$、$e_2=(1,0)$，求对偶基 $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2$（写成坐标 $x,y$ 的函数），再求 $S=\operatorname{span}\{(1,1)\}$ 的零化子，并核对维数公式。
examples.solution:
设 $\varepsilon_1(x,y)=ax+by$。由 $\varepsilon_1(e_1)=a+b=1$、$\varepsilon_1(e_2)=a=0$ 得 $b=1$，故 $\varepsilon_1(x,y)=y$。
设 $\varepsilon_2(x,y)=cx+dy$。由 $\varepsilon_2(e_1)=c+d=0$、$\varepsilon_2(e_2)=c=1$ 得 $d=-1$，故 $\varepsilon_2(x,y)=x-y$。
验证：$\varepsilon_1(1,1)=1$、$\varepsilon_1(1,0)=0$、$\varepsilon_2(1,1)=0$、$\varepsilon_2(1,0)=1$，恰好是 $\delta_{ij}$ ✓。
零化子：$S=\operatorname{span}\{e_1\}=\operatorname{span}\{(1,1)\}$，对 $f=a\varepsilon_1+b\varepsilon_2$ 有 $f(e_1)=a\varepsilon_1(e_1)+b\varepsilon_2(e_1)=a$，故 $S^{\circ}=\{f:\ a=0\}=\operatorname{span}\{\varepsilon_2\}=\operatorname{span}\{x-y\}$，$\dim S^{\circ}=1$。
核对：$\dim S+\dim S^{\circ}=1+1=2=\dim V$ ✓。几何上 $\varepsilon_2=x-y$ 正是「过 $(1,1)$ 的直线」的线性方程 $x-y=0$ 所对应的线性函数。

matrix-derivative-basics.definition:
多元微积分里已经会算梯度、雅可比与全微分，但那套语言只覆盖「标量对标量、标量对向量、向量对向量」的情形。一旦自变量本身是矩阵 $X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$，第一件事不是算，而是**约定形状**——同一个函数在不同文献里可以写成形状完全不同的「导数」。本库全部矩阵微分内容统一采用**混合布局（mixed layout）**：**标量**对向量、标量对矩阵的导数按「分母布局」（谁的变元在分母上，导数的形状就跟着谁走）；**向量对向量**的导数取标准的 $m\times n$ **雅可比矩阵**（行=输出维数；这一支在文献里也称雅可比布局/分子布局）。

三种基本情形。**(i) 标量对向量**：$f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}$ 时 $\partial f/\partial x$ 与 $x$ **同型**（$n\times1$ 列向量），第 $j$ 个分量是 $\partial f/\partial x_{j}$，于是 $df=(\partial f/\partial x)^{\top}dx$。**(ii) 向量对向量**：$y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$、$x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ 时 $\partial y/\partial x$ 是 $m\times n$ 的**雅可比矩阵**，第 $(i,j)$ 元为 $\partial y_{i}/\partial x_{j}$，于是 $dy=(\partial y/\partial x)\,dx$；它的第 $i$ 行恰好是 $\nabla y_{i}$ 的转置。**(iii) 标量对矩阵**：$f:\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ 时 $\partial f/\partial X$ 与 $X$ **同型**（$m\times n$），第 $(i,j)$ 元为 $\partial f/\partial X_{ij}$，于是

$$df=\sum_{i,j}\frac{\partial f}{\partial X_{ij}}\,dX_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial X}\right)^{\!\top}dX\right).$$

最后这条恒等式是矩阵微分最常用的**识别工具**：把 $df$ 整理成 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ 的形状，则 $G$ 就是 $\partial f/\partial X$，因为 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)=\sum_{i,j}G_{ij}\,dX_{ij}$。这一个小技巧把「矩阵求导」变成「展开微分 + 凑迹」，几乎不用背公式表。

**布局警告**：不少文献（如 Wikipedia 的引言部分）默认**分子布局（numerator layout）**，把标量对向量的导数写成行向量——与本站的标量约定互为转置；向量对向量的公式则要先看清对方的雅可比是 $m\times n$ 还是 $n\times m$。另注：常用手册《Matrix Cookbook》的**标量**导数条目与本站同形，可直接照用，其向量对向量、矩阵对矩阵条目则需逐条核对取向。引用现成公式之前，先确认它用的是哪套约定，再决定要不要转置。本库的一切矩阵微分结论都按上面的**混合布局**书写。
matrix-derivative-basics.definitionEn:
Multivariable calculus already gives us gradients, Jacobians and total differentials, but that language only covers scalar and vector arguments. As soon as the variable itself is a matrix $X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the first question is not how to compute, but **how to fix shapes**: the same function is written with completely different “derivative” shapes in different references. All matrix calculus in this library uses a **mixed layout**: the derivative of a **scalar** with respect to a vector or a matrix follows the **denominator layout** (its shape follows the denominator), whereas the derivative of a vector with respect to a vector is the standard $m\times n$ **Jacobian** (rows indexed by the output; also called the Jacobian formulation, or the numerator layout in some sources).

Three basic cases. **(i) Scalar by vector**: for $f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}$, the derivative $\partial f/\partial x$ has the **same shape as x** (an $n\times1$ column vector), with $j$-th entry $\partial f/\partial x_{j}$, so $df=(\partial f/\partial x)^{\top}dx$. **(ii) Vector by vector**: for $y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$, $\partial y/\partial x$ is the $m\times n$ **Jacobian** with $(i,j)$ entry $\partial y_{i}/\partial x_{j}$, so $dy=(\partial y/\partial x)\,dx$; its $i$-th row is the transpose of $\nabla y_{i}$. **(iii) Scalar by matrix**: for $f:\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$, $\partial f/\partial X$ has the **same shape as X**, with $(i,j)$ entry $\partial f/\partial X_{ij}$, so

$$df=\sum_{i,j}\frac{\partial f}{\partial X_{ij}}\,dX_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial X}\right)^{\!\top}dX\right).$$

The last identity is the standard **recognition tool**: rearrange $df$ into the form $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ and read off $G=\partial f/\partial X$, because $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)=\sum_{i,j}G_{ij}\,dX_{ij}$. This single trick turns matrix differentiation into “expand the differential, match the trace” and makes long tables of formulas unnecessary.

**A warning on layout**: many sources (e.g. Wikipedia's introductory sections) default to the **numerator layout**, writing scalar-by-vector derivatives as row vectors — the transpose of our scalar convention; and for vector-by-vector formulas one must first check whether their Jacobian is $m\times n$ or $n\times m$. Note also that the widely used *Matrix Cookbook* matches our **scalar** derivatives directly, while its vector-by-vector and matrix-by-matrix entries should be checked case by case. Before using a published formula, check which convention it follows and transpose if necessary. Everything in this library is written in the **mixed layout** above.
derivation:
设 $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ 在 $x$ 处可微。按本批统一的分母（梯度）布局，定义 $
abla f(x)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ 为列向量，其第 $j$ 个分量为 $\partial f/\partial x_j$。由可微性的一阶展开，对任意 $dx\in\mathbb{R}^n$，$$f(x+dx)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^n rac{\partial f}{\partial x_j}\,dx_j+o(\|dx\|).$$ 右端线性项等于 $(
abla f)^{	op}dx$，故 $df=(
abla f)^{	op}dx$。结论：标量对向量的导数与 $x$ 同型，是列向量；条件是可微性，$dx$ 任意。

设 $y:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$ 在 $x$ 处可微。定义雅可比矩阵 $J=\partial y/\partial x\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$，其第 $(i,j)$ 元为 $\partial y_i/\partial x_j$。对每个分量作一阶展开并忽略 $o(\|dx\|)$，得 $dy_i=\sum_j J_{ij}dx_j$，合并为 $dy=J\,dx$；因此 $J$ 的第 $i$ 行是 $(\nabla y_i)^{\top}$。当 $m=1$ 时 $J$ 是 $1\times n$ 行向量，恰为标量梯度列向量的转置——这正是混合布局中两种情形的衔接处。结论：向量对向量取标准 $m\times n$ 雅可比（行对应输出分量）。

设 $f:\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ 在 $X$ 处可微，定义 $G\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ 的 $(i,j)$ 元为 $\partial f/\partial X_{ij}$。全微分是 $$df=\sum_{i,j}G_{ij}\,dX_{ij}.$$ 由于 $(G^{\top}dX)_{jj}=\sum_i G_{ij}dX_{ij}$，对 $j$ 求和得 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)=\sum_{i,j}G_{ij}dX_{ij}$，所以 $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$。反过来，若对某个 $H$ 有 $df=\operatorname{tr}(H^{\top}dX)$ 对一切 $dX$ 成立，取 $dX=E_{ij}$ 得 $H_{ij}=$ 该方向导数 $=G_{ij}$，故 $H=G$ 唯一。结论：标量对矩阵的导数与 $X$ 同型，且迹形式与逐元素定义等价。

沿任意方向 $B$ 取路径 $X(t)=X+tB$，由链式法则 $\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}f(X+tB)=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}B)$，等价地 $$f(X+tB)=f(X)+t\,\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}B)+o(t).$$ 向量情形同理：$f(x+td)=f(x)+t(\nabla f)^{\top}d+o(t)$。这说明导数是一个关于方向线性的泛函，而 $G$ 正是它在迹内积下的表示；也给出有限差分检验：用 $(f(X+tE_{ij})-f(X))/t$ 逼近 $G_{ij}$。条件是 $f$ 可微、$t\to0$。

例：$f(X)=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\top}X)=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}X_{ij}$。直接微分得 $df=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\top}dX)$，与 $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ 对照即 $G=A$；取 $dX=E_{ij}$ 也得到方向导数 $A_{ij}$。若写成 $f(X)=\operatorname{tr}(AX)$，则 $df=\operatorname{tr}(A\,dX)$，对照识别式得梯度 $A^{\top}$，顺序与转置不能混。结论：识别 $G$ 时只需把 $df$ 凑成迹形式，系数矩阵要连同转置一起读。

布局换算：若某文献用分子布局，把标量对向量的导数写成行向量 $r^{\top}$，则本批的列梯度是 $r$；标量对矩阵的分子布局结果 $H_{\text{num}}$ 与本批的 $G_{\text{den}}$ 互为转置，$H_{\text{num}}=G_{\text{den}}^{\top}$。向量对向量的雅可比还必须核对取向：只有当对方也满足 $dy=J\,dx$ 且 $J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ 时才与本批一致，否则先转置。结论：全篇统一「标量按分母布局、向量对向量按标准雅可比」；引用任何公式前先确认约定，且一次推导内不得混用。
derivationEn:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $x$. Under the batch-wide denominator (gradient) layout, define $
abla f(x)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ as the column vector whose $j$-th entry is $\partial f/\partial x_j$. Differentiability gives, for every $dx\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $$f(x+dx)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^n rac{\partial f}{\partial x_j}\,dx_j+o(\|dx\|).$$ The linear term equals $(
abla f)^{	op}dx$, hence $df=(
abla f)^{	op}dx$. Conclusion: the derivative of a scalar with respect to a vector has the same shape as $x$ and is a column vector; the hypothesis is differentiability and $dx$ is arbitrary.

Let $y:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$ be differentiable at $x$, and define the Jacobian $J=\partial y/\partial x\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ by $J_{ij}=\partial y_i/\partial x_j$. Expanding each component to first order and dropping $o(\|dx\|)$ gives $dy_i=\sum_j J_{ij}dx_j$, hence $dy=J\,dx$; the $i$-th row of $J$ is $(\nabla y_i)^{\top}$. For $m=1$, $J$ is a $1\times n$ row, exactly the transpose of the scalar gradient column — this is where the two cases of the mixed layout meet. Conclusion: vector-by-vector derivatives use the standard $m\times n$ Jacobian (rows indexed by outputs).

Let $f:\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $X$, and define $G\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ by $G_{ij}=\partial f/\partial X_{ij}$. The total differential is $$df=\sum_{i,j}G_{ij}\,dX_{ij}.$$ Since $(G^{\top}dX)_{jj}=\sum_i G_{ij}dX_{ij}$, summing over $j$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)=\sum_{i,j}G_{ij}dX_{ij}$, hence $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$. Conversely, if $df=\operatorname{tr}(H^{\top}dX)$ for all $dX$, testing $dX=E_{ij}$ gives $H_{ij}=$ the directional derivative $=G_{ij}$, so $H=G$ is unique. Conclusion: a scalar-by-matrix derivative has the same shape as $X$, and the trace form is equivalent to the entrywise definition.

Along any direction $B$, take $X(t)=X+tB$. The chain rule gives $\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}f(X+tB)=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}B)$, equivalently $$f(X+tB)=f(X)+t\,\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}B)+o(t).$$ The vector case is analogous: $f(x+td)=f(x)+t(\nabla f)^{\top}d+o(t)$. Thus the derivative is a linear functional of the direction, and $G$ represents it in the trace inner product; this also yields the finite-difference test $(f(X+tE_{ij})-f(X))/t\to G_{ij}$. The hypotheses are differentiability and $t\to0$.

Example: $f(X)=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\top}X)=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}X_{ij}$. Direct differentiation gives $df=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\top}dX)$, and comparison with $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ yields $G=A$; testing $dX=E_{ij}$ also gives the directional derivative $A_{ij}$. If instead $f(X)=\operatorname{tr}(AX)$, then $df=\operatorname{tr}(A\,dX)$, and the identification rule gives the gradient $A^{\top}$; order and transpose cannot be mixed up. Conclusion: to identify $G$, put $df$ into trace form and read the coefficient together with its transpose.

Layout conversion: if a source uses the numerator layout and writes the scalar-by-vector derivative as a row $r^{\top}$, then the column gradient in this batch is $r$; for scalar-by-matrix derivatives, the numerator-layout result $H_{\text{num}}$ and the denominator-layout result $G_{\text{den}}$ satisfy $H_{\text{num}}=G_{\text{den}}^{\top}$.
