Vector-by-vector Jacobians also need an orientation check: they agree with this batch only when $dy=J\,dx$ with $J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$; otherwise transpose first. Conclusion: use one convention throughout — denominator layout for scalars and the standard Jacobian for vector-by-vector — and never mix conventions within a derivation.

formulas.latex: \begin{aligned}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&\in\mathbb{R}^{n},\qquad \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right)_{j}=\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_{j}}\\[2pt]df&=\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right)^{\top}dx\end{aligned}
formulas.note: 标量对向量：梯度与 x 同型（n 维列向量），全微分就是它与 dx 的内积。
formulas.noteEn: Scalar by vector: the gradient has the same shape as x (an n-vector), and the differential is its inner product with dx.

formulas.latex: \begin{aligned}\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}&\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n},\qquad \left(\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}\right)_{ij}=\frac{\partial y_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\\[2pt]dy&=\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}\,dx\end{aligned}
formulas.note: 向量对向量：得到 m×n 的雅可比矩阵；第 i 行是 ∇yᵢ 的转置，dy 就是矩阵乘向量。
formulas.noteEn: Vector by vector: the m×n Jacobian; its i-th row is the transpose of ∇yᵢ, and dy is a matrix-vector product.

formulas.note: 标量对矩阵：与 X 同型；把 df 凑成 tr(GᵀdX) 时 G 就是 ∂f/∂X（因为 tr(GᵀdX)=Σ Gᵢⱼ dXᵢⱼ）。
formulas.noteEn: Scalar by matrix: same shape as X; once df is written as tr(Gᵀ dX), the matrix G is ∂f/∂X, because tr(Gᵀ dX) = Σ Gᵢⱼ dXᵢⱼ.

formulas.note: 一阶近似就是全微分的重写；误差是高阶小量，这也给出用有限差分检验梯度的办法。
formulas.noteEn: The first-order approximation is just the total differential rewritten; the error is of higher order, which yields the finite-difference check of a gradient.

formulas.latex: \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right)_{\text{分子布局}}=\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right)_{\text{分母布局}}^{\top}
formulas.note: 分子布局与分母布局的结果互为转置（标量对向量时前者是行向量）；套公式前先核对约定。
formulas.noteEn: The two layouts give transposes of each other (the numerator layout yields a row vector in the scalar-by-vector case); check the convention before using a formula.

properties: 形状法则：标量对向量的导数与自变量同型（列向量），向量对向量的导数是 m×n 雅可比矩阵，标量对矩阵的导数与矩阵同型；形状对不上，一定是布局搞错或漏了转置。
识别工具：把全微分整理成 tr(GᵀdX) 后，G 就是 ∂f/∂X——这一步只用到 tr(GᵀdX) = Σᵢⱼ Gᵢⱼ dXᵢⱼ。
雅可比矩阵的第 i 行是 ∇yᵢ 的转置，所以向量对向量的导数可以看成「把每个分量的梯度按行摞起来」。
一阶近似 $f(x+dx)\approx f(x)+(\nabla f)^{\top}dx$ 与全微分 $df=(\nabla f)^{\top}dx$ 是同一件事的两种写法，误差为 $o(\|dx\|)$；它同时给出用有限差分检验梯度的办法。
约定警告：本库标量导数按**分母（梯度）布局**；不少文献默认**分子布局**（标量对向量的导数为行向量），两者互为转置；向量对向量的雅可比还需另行核对取向。搬运公式前先确认约定。
propertiesEn: Shape rule: the derivative of a scalar with respect to a vector has the same shape as the vector (a column), a vector-by-vector derivative is an m×n Jacobian, and a scalar-by-matrix derivative has the same shape as the matrix; a shape mismatch always means a wrong layout or a missing transpose.
Recognition tool: once the differential is written as tr(Gᵀ dX), the matrix G is exactly ∂f/∂X, using only tr(Gᵀ dX) = Σᵢⱼ Gᵢⱼ dXᵢⱼ.
The i-th row of ∂y/∂x is the transpose of ∇yᵢ, so a vector-by-vector derivative is simply the gradients of the components stacked as rows.

The first-order approximation $f(x+dx)\approx f(x)+(\nabla f)^{\top}dx$ and the total differential $df=(\nabla f)^{\top}dx$ are two ways of writing the same statement, with error $o(\|dx\|)$; it also supplies the finite-difference test of a gradient.

Convention warning: this library uses the denominator (gradient) layout for scalar derivatives, while many sources default to the numerator layout (scalar-by-vector derivatives as row vectors) — the two are transposes of each other; Jacobians of vector-by-vector derivatives need a separate orientation check. Always verify the convention before importing a formula.

examples.problem: 设 $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)^{\top}$，$A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$。求 $\partial(x^{\top}x)/\partial x$ 与 $\partial(Ax)/\partial x$，并核对形状。
examples.solution:
**第一问**：$f(x)=x^{\top}x$，展开微分 $df=(dx)^{\top}x+x^{\top}dx=2x^{\top}dx=(2x)^{\top}dx$，故 $\partial(x^{\top}x)/\partial x=2x$，与 $x$ 同型（$n\times1$）✓。数值核对：取 $x=(1,2,3)^{\top}$，则 $f=1+4+9=14$；令 $x+te_1=(1+t,2,3)^{\top}$，得 $f=14+2t+t^2$，一次项系数 $2$ 恰等于 $(2x)_1$ ✓。

**第二问**：$g(x)=Ax$ 的第 $i$ 个分量为 $g_i=\sum_j A_{ij}x_j$，故 $\partial g_i/\partial x_j=A_{ij}$，即 $\partial(Ax)/\partial x=A$，形状 $m\times n$，与 $A$ 一致 ✓。数值核对：取 $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$、$x=(1,1)^{\top}$，则 $Ax=(3,7)^{\top}$；再令 $x+te_2=(1,1+t)^{\top}$，得 $Ax=(3,7)^{\top}+t(2,4)^{\top}$，导向量 $(2,4)^{\top}$ 正是 $A$ 的第二列 ✓。

examples.problem: 用一阶近似检验 $f(x)=x^{\top}x$ 在 $x=(1,2)^{\top}$ 附近的表现。

matrix-differential-rules.definition:
有了形状约定，还要一台**运算引擎**。矩阵微分的做法不是每次从头算偏导，而是对恒等式两边同时取**微分** $d$：把每个矩阵看成单参数族 $X(t)=X_0+tB$ 在 $t=0$ 处的方向导数，$d$ 就是「沿任意方向 $B$ 求导」的线性算子。$d$ 对加法、数乘、转置、迹都很友好，但遇到矩阵乘法时**顺序不能交换**——这是全部易错点的根源（本节法则作用于**微分 $d$** 本身，与布局约定无关；但搬运其他文献的导数/梯度公式时仍需先核对布局约定）。

基本法则：$d(X+Y)=dX+dY$、$d(kX)=k\,dX$、$d(X^{\top})=(dX)^{\top}$；乘积法则 $d(XY)=(dX)Y+X(dY)$（两个因子的左右位置固定）；逆的微分 $d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}$（负号加三个因子把 $dX$ 夹在中间，要求 $X$ 可逆）；Hadamard 乘积 $d(X\odot Y)=(dX)\odot Y+X\odot(dY)$ 逐元素成立。标量导数沿用全批统一约定（**分母/梯度布局**）：$\partial f/\partial X$ 与 $X$ 同型，$df=\operatorname{tr}((\partial f/\partial X)^{\top}dX)$。

标量函数最常用的两条：$d(\operatorname{tr}X)=\operatorname{tr}(dX)$ 与 $d(\det X)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(X)\,dX)$（一般式，$X$ 是任意方阵）；当 $X$ 可逆时 $\operatorname{adj}(X)=\det(X)X^{-1}$，于是 $d(\det X)=\det(X)\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX)$。

合成函数不必背新法则，用**先内后外**的链式流程：设 $Y=Y(X)$、$f=f(Y)$，先求内层微分 $dY$，再代入外层 $df=\operatorname{tr}\big((\partial f/\partial Y)^{\top}dY\big)$，最后把结果整理成 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$，$G$ 即 $\partial f/\partial X$。用向量化记号等价地有 $\partial f/\partial\operatorname{vec}(X)=\big(\partial\operatorname{vec}(Y)/\partial\operatorname{vec}(X)\big)^{\top}\partial f/\partial\operatorname{vec}(Y)$，两条路径给出的答案相同。
matrix-differential-rules.definitionEn:
Once shapes are settled, we need an **engine**. Matrix calculus does not recompute partial derivatives from scratch; instead it differentiates identities directly. Think of a matrix as the one-parameter family $X(t)=X_0+tB$ and of $d$ as the directional derivative at $t=0$: a linear operator that differentiates along an arbitrary direction $B$. It behaves well with addition, scalar multiplication, transposition and the trace, but with matrix products **the order can never be swapped** — that is the root of almost every mistake (the rules below act on the **differential** $d$ itself and are independent of any layout convention; when importing derivative or gradient formulas from other sources, check their layout first).

Basic rules: $d(X+Y)=dX+dY$, $d(kX)=k\,dX$ and $d(X^{\top})=(dX)^{\top}$; the product rule $d(XY)=(dX)Y+X(dY)$ (the two factors keep their positions); the inverse rule $d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}$ (a minus sign, with $dX$ sandwiched between three factors, valid for invertible $X$); and the elementwise Hadamard rule $d(X\odot Y)=(dX)\odot Y+X\odot(dY)$. Scalar derivatives keep the batch-wide convention (the **denominator/gradient layout**): $\partial f/\partial X$ has the same shape as $X$ and $df=\operatorname{tr}((\partial f/\partial X)^{\top}dX)$.

Two rules carry most of the workload for scalar functions: $d(\operatorname{tr}X)=\operatorname{tr}(dX)$ and $d(\det X)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(X)\,dX)$, which holds for every square matrix; when $X$ is invertible, $\operatorname{adj}(X)=\det(X)X^{-1}$ gives $d(\det X)=\det(X)\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX)$.

Composite functions need no new rule if you work **inner first**: for $Y=Y(X)$ and $f=f(Y)$, compute the inner differential $dY$, substitute it into the outer differential $df=\operatorname{tr}\big((\partial f/\partial Y)^{\top}dY\big)$, and rearrange the result into $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$; then $G=\partial f/\partial X$. In vectorized notation this is $\partial f/\partial\operatorname{vec}(X)=\big(\partial\operatorname{vec}(Y)/\partial\operatorname{vec}(X)\big)^{\top}\partial f/\partial\operatorname{vec}(Y)$, and both routes agree.
derivation: 把矩阵看成单参数族 $X(t)$，定义 $dF=\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}F(X(t))$（差一个 $dt$ 的标量因子）；也可直接把它理解为沿任意方向 $B$ 的方向导数。$d$ 是线性算子：$$d(X+Y)=dX+dY,\qquad d(kX)=k\,dX,\qquad d(X^{\top})=(dX)^{\top}.$$ 又因迹是线性的，$d\operatorname{tr}X=\operatorname{tr}(dX)$。条件是相关元素可微、形状相容。结论：加法、数乘、转置与迹都可以逐项穿过 $d$。

乘积法则由路径乘积求导得到：$$d(XY)=\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}\big(X(t)Y(t)\big)=(dX)Y+X\,dY.$$ 两个因子的左右位置必须保持；三因子情形为 $d(XYZ)=(dX)YZ+X(dY)Z+XY(dZ)$。Hadamard 乘积逐元素就是标量乘积，故 $d(X\odot Y)=(dX)\odot Y+X\odot dY$。条件是乘法或 Hadamard 乘积形状相容、元素可微。结论：矩阵乘法不交换，微分时不能把 $(dX)Y$ 写成 $Y(dX)$。

设 $X$ 在讨论点可逆。对恒等式 $XX^{-1}=I$ 两边取 $d$，用乘积法则得 $$(dX)X^{-1}+X\,d(X^{-1})=0,$$ 左乘 $X^{-1}$ 即得 $$d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}.$$ 这里 $dX$ 被夹在三个因子中间，顺序不能反；$-X^{-2}dX$ 或 $-(dX)X^{-2}$ 只有在 $dX$ 与 $X$ 可交换时才可能碰巧成立，一般情形是错的。可逆性在一点成立时由连续性在邻域内保持，故路径导数同样成立。结论：逆的微分公式为 $d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}dX\,X^{-1}$。

迹的微分就是 $d\operatorname{tr}X=\operatorname{tr}(dX)$；对 $f(X)=\operatorname{tr}(AX)$ 有 $df=\operatorname{tr}(A\,dX)$。若 $P\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$、$Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$，则 $$\operatorname{tr}(PQ)=\sum_{i,j}P_{ij}Q_{ji}=\operatorname{tr}(QP),$$ 多因子时只能循环移动，$\operatorname{tr}(PQR)=\operatorname{tr}(RPQ)$（形状相容时）。条件：每个迹的自变量为方阵。结论：迹的循环性是把 $dX$ 挪到末尾、从而读出梯度的关键工具，但不能任意交换因子顺序。

行列式的一般微分：固定一行 $i$ 作余子式展开 $\det X=\sum_j X_{ij}C_{ij}$，其中余子式 $C_{ij}$ 不含 $X_{ij}$，故 $\partial\det X/\partial X_{ij}=C_{ij}=(\operatorname{adj}X)_{ji}$。于是 $$\begin{aligned}d\det X&=\sum_{i,j}(\operatorname{adj}X)_{ji}dX_{ij}\\&=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(X)\,dX).\end{aligned}$$ 对任意方阵成立。当 $X$ 可逆时 $\operatorname{adj}(X)=\det(X)X^{-1}$，代入得 $$d\det X=\det(X)\,\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX).$$ 条件：第一式只要求 $X$ 为方阵，第二式额外要求 $X$ 可逆。结论：含 $X^{-1}$ 的简洁形式不能用于奇异矩阵。

复合函数用「先内后外」：设 $Y=Y(X)$、$f=f(Y)$ 均可微。先算内层 $dY$，再代入外层 $$df=\operatorname{tr}\left(\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial Y}\right)^{\top}dY\right),$$ 用循环性把 $dY$ 中的 $dX$ 归并到迹的末尾，写成 $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$，则 $G=\partial f/\partial X$。例如 $f=\operatorname{tr}(AX^{-1})$：令 $Y=X^{-1}$，则 $\partial f/\partial Y=A^{\top}$、$dY=-Y\,dX\,Y$，于是 $df=-\operatorname{tr}(A Y\,dX\,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}(Y A Y\,dX)$，读出 $G=-Y^{\top}A^{\top}Y^{\top}=-X^{-\top}A^{\top}X^{-\top}$（$X$ 可逆）。结论：链式流程不需要额外的矩阵链式法则公式，只需内层微分、回代与迹的循环。
derivationEn: View a matrix as a one-parameter family $X(t)$ and define $dF=\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}F(X(t))$ (up to the scalar factor $dt$); equivalently, read it as the directional derivative along an arbitrary direction $B$. The operator $d$ is linear: $$d(X+Y)=dX+dY,\qquad d(kX)=k\,dX,\qquad d(X^{\top})=(dX)^{\top}.$$ Since the trace is linear, $d\operatorname{tr}X=\operatorname{tr}(dX)$. The hypotheses are differentiability of the entries and compatible shapes. Conclusion: addition, scalar multiplication, transposition and the trace all pass through $d$ termwise.

The product rule comes from differentiating a path of products: $$d(XY)=\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}\big(X(t)Y(t)\big)=(dX)Y+X\,dY.$$ The left-right positions of the factors must be preserved; for three factors, $d(XYZ)=(dX)YZ+X(dY)Z+XY(dZ)$. The Hadamard product is entrywise, so $d(X\odot Y)=(dX)\odot Y+X\odot dY$. The hypotheses are compatible shapes for the product or Hadamard product and differentiability. Conclusion: matrix multiplication does not commute, so $(dX)Y$ must not be rewritten as $Y(dX)$.

Assume $X$ is invertible at the point under discussion. Applying $d$ to $XX^{-1}=I$ and using the product rule gives $$(dX)X^{-1}+X\,d(X^{-1})=0,$$ and left multiplication by $X^{-1}$ yields $$d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}.$$ Here $dX$ is sandwiched between three factors and the order is essential; $-X^{-2}dX$ or $-(dX)X^{-2}$ can hold only accidentally when $dX$ commutes with $X$, and is wrong in general. Invertibility at one point persists in a neighborhood by continuity, so the same formula holds along paths. Conclusion: $d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}dX\,X^{-1}$.

The differential of the trace is $d\operatorname{tr}X=\operatorname{tr}(dX)$; for $f(X)=\operatorname{tr}(AX)$, $df=\operatorname{tr}(A\,dX)$. If $P\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, then $$\operatorname{tr}(PQ)=\sum_{i,j}P_{ij}Q_{ji}=\operatorname{tr}(QP),$$ and with several factors only cyclic shifts are allowed: $\operatorname{tr}(PQR)=\operatorname{tr}(RPQ)$ when the shapes are compatible. The hypothesis is that every trace argument is square. Conclusion: cyclicity is the key tool for moving $dX$ to the end and reading off the gradient, but factors cannot be permuted arbitrarily.

General determinant differential: expand along a fixed row $i$, $\det X=\sum_j X_{ij}C_{ij}$, where the cofactor $C_{ij}$ does not contain $X_{ij}$; hence $\partial\det X/\partial X_{ij}=C_{ij}=(\operatorname{adj}X)_{ji}$. Therefore $$\begin{aligned}d\det X&=\sum_{i,j}(\operatorname{adj}X)_{ji}dX_{ij}\\&=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(X)\,dX).\end{aligned}$$ valid for every square matrix. If $X$ is invertible, $\operatorname{adj}(X)=\det(X)X^{-1}$, and substitution gives $$d\det X=\det(X)\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX).$$ The first identity needs only a square $X$; the second additionally needs invertibility. Conclusion: the compact form containing $X^{-1}$ cannot be used for singular matrices.

For composites, work “inner first”: let $Y=Y(X)$ and $f=f(Y)$ be differentiable. Compute the inner differential $dY$, substitute it into the outer differential $$df=\operatorname{tr}\left(\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial Y}\right)^{\top}dY\right),$$ then use cyclicity to collect $dX$ at the end of the trace and write $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$; then $G=\partial f/\partial X$. For example, for $f=\operatorname{tr}(AX^{-1})$, set $Y=X^{-1}$; then $\partial f/\partial Y=A^{\top}$ and $dY=-Y\,dX\,Y$, so $df=-\operatorname{tr}(A Y\,dX\,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}(Y A Y\,dX)$, giving $G=-Y^{\top}A^{\top}Y^{\top}=-X^{-\top}A^{\top}X^{-\top}$ for invertible $X$. Conclusion: the chain workflow needs no separate matrix chain-rule formula — only the inner differential, substitution and trace cyclicity.

formulas.note: 线性与转置：d 逐项作用在加法、数乘与转置上，是后面所有法则的基础。
formulas.noteEn: Linearity and transpose: d acts termwise on sums, scalar multiples and transposes; everything else builds on this.

formulas.note: 乘积法则：两个因子的左右顺序不能交换——矩阵乘法不满足交换律。
formulas.noteEn: Product rule: the two factors keep their left-right positions, since matrix multiplication does not commute.

formulas.note: 逆的微分：负号与三因子顺序都要记牢，由 XX⁻¹=I 两边微分得到。
formulas.noteEn: Inverse rule: remember both the minus sign and the order of the three factors; it follows by differentiating XX⁻¹=I.

formulas.note: 迹与行列式：一般式对任意方阵成立，含 X⁻¹ 的版本只对可逆矩阵成立。
formulas.noteEn: Trace and determinant: the general form holds for every square matrix, while the form containing X⁻¹ requires X to be invertible.

formulas.note: Hadamard（逐元素）乘积：逐元素看就是普通的标量乘积法则。
formulas.noteEn: Hadamard (elementwise) product: entry by entry it is just the usual scalar product rule.

properties: 顺序法则：矩阵乘法不交换，$d(XY)$ 的两项位置固定，$d(X^{-1})$ 必须是 $-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}$——写成 $-X^{-2}dX$ 或 $-(dX)X^{-2}$ 都是错的（形状虽然相同，数值/顺序不对）：必须三个因子夹着 $dX$。
线性与兼容：$d$ 与加法、数乘、转置、迹都可交换，所以任何由乘法与逆搭出的表达式都能逐层微分。
行列式：一般式 $d(\det X)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(X)\,dX)$ 对任意方阵成立；只有写成 $\det(X)\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX)$ 时才需要 $X$ 可逆。
链式法则：稳妥的用法是「先内后外」——先算内层 $dY$，再代入外层 $df$，最后凑成 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ 读出梯度；这避免了不同教材对矩阵链式法则的表述分歧。
检验习惯：任何新推出的 $dF$ 都可以用有限差分核对——比较 $(F(X+tB)-F(X))/t$ 与公式给出的方向导数，$t$ 足够小时两者应吻合。
propertiesEn: Order rule: matrix products do not commute. The two terms of $d(XY)$ keep their positions, and $d(X^{-1})$ must be written as $-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}$; forms such as $-X^{-2}dX$ are wrong (the shapes can coincide, but the order and the values are off): $dX$ has to sit between three factors.
Linearity: d commutes with addition, scalar multiplication, transposition and the trace, so every expression built from products and inverses can be differentiated layer by layer.

Determinant: the general rule $d(\det X)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(X)\,dX)$ holds for every square matrix; only the version $\det(X)\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX)$ requires $X$ to be invertible.

Chain rule: work “inner first” — compute the inner differential dY, substitute it into the outer df, then match $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ to read off the gradient; this avoids the notational disputes found across textbooks.
Testing habit: any new differential dF can be checked by finite differences — compare $(F(X+tB)-F(X))/t$ with the directional derivative predicted by the formula; for small t the two must agree.

examples.problem: 设 $X$ 为 $2\times2$ 可逆矩阵。用法则推导 $d(\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}))$，即求 $\partial\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1})/\partial X$，并在 $X=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ 处用有限差分核对。
examples.solution:
**推导**：$d(\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}))=\operatorname{tr}(d(X^{-1}))=\operatorname{tr}(-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1})=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}X^{-1}\,dX)$（用了迹的轮换），对照 $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ 得 $\partial\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1})/\partial X=-X^{-\top}X^{-\top}$。

**数值核对**：$X^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$（可验证 $XX^{-1}=I$），$X^{-1}X^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}2&-3\\-3&5\end{pmatrix}$，故 $G=\begin{pmatrix}-2&3\\3&-5\end{pmatrix}$。

**有限差分**（把 $X$ 的第 $(i,j)$ 元加 $t$ 后对 $t$ 求导）：
· 第 $(1,1)$ 元：$\operatorname{tr}(X(t)^{-1})=\dfrac{3+t}{1+t}$，在 $t=0$ 处导数为 $-2=G_{11}$ ✓
· 第 $(1,2)$ 元：$\operatorname{tr}(X(t)^{-1})=\dfrac{3}{1-t}$，导数为 $3=G_{12}$ ✓
· 第 $(2,2)$ 元：$\operatorname{tr}(X(t)^{-1})=\dfrac{3+t}{1+2t}$，导数为 $-5=G_{22}$ ✓（$G$ 对称，第 $(2,1)$ 元同为 $3$）

examples.problem: 验证逆的微分公式：取 $X=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$、方向 $B=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$，比较 $d(X^{-1})$ 与公式 $-X^{-1}B\,X^{-1}$。
examples.solution:
沿 $B$ 的矩阵族为 $X(t)=\begin{pmatrix}2&1+t\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$，其行列式 $\det X(t)=1-t$，故 $X(t)^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{1-t}\begin{pmatrix}1&-(1+t)\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$。在 $t=0$ 处逐项求导得 $\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$。

另一方面 $X^{-1}B=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$，$(X^{-1}B)X^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}$，取负得 $\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$，与直接求导完全一致 ✓。

matrix-gradient-identities.definition:
有了运算法则，真正的计算任务就是：把 $f$ 的微分整理成 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$（向量情形是 $(\nabla f)^{\top}dx$），再读出 $G$。几乎所有公式都能现推，但常用的一批值得记牢。本库统一用**分母布局**：$\partial f/\partial x$ 与 $x$ 同型、$\partial f/\partial X$ 与 $X$ 同型，恒有

$$df=(\partial f/\partial x)^{\top}dx=\operatorname{tr}\!\left((\partial f/\partial X)^{\top}dX\right).$$

**凑迹三步法**：第一步，展开 $df$（乘积法则、逆的微分、行列式与迹的法则）；第二步，用迹的轮换 $\operatorname{tr}(PQ)=\operatorname{tr}(QP)$（多因子时 $\operatorname{tr}(PQR)=\operatorname{tr}(RPQ)$）把 $dX$ 挪到迹的**末尾**；第三步，把系数写成「某个矩阵的转置」并对照 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ 读出 $G$。目标形永远是 $\operatorname{tr}(\text{系数矩阵}\cdot dX)$，读梯度时别忘了转置这一层。

两个最容易踩的坑。其一，**对称化**：$\partial(x^{\top}Ax)/\partial x=(A+A^{\top})x$ 对一般 $A$ 成立，只有当 $A=A^{\top}$ 时才等于 $2Ax$；迹二次型 $\partial\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}AX)/\partial X=(A+A^{\top})X$ 同理。其二，**可逆条件**：$\partial\det(X)/\partial X$ 与 $\partial\ln\det(X)/\partial X$ 的简洁形式都要求 $X$ 可逆，而且都是**无约束**（全矩阵空间）版本——把 $X$ 限制在对称矩阵上会改变切空间，公式不能再照搬。文献中的同类结果若按其他布局给出，需先核对约定（标量公式常与本库互为转置）。
matrix-gradient-identities.definitionEn:
With the rules in hand, the actual task is to rearrange the differential of $f$ into the form $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ — or $(\nabla f)^{\top}dx$ in the vector case — and read off $G$. Every identity can be re-derived in a line or two, but the standard list is worth memorizing. This library uses the **denominator layout** throughout: $\partial f/\partial x$ matches the shape of $x$ and $\partial f/\partial X$ matches the shape of $X$, so that

$$df=(\partial f/\partial x)^{\top}dx=\operatorname{tr}\!\left((\partial f/\partial X)^{\top}dX\right).$$

**The three-step trace method**: expand $df$ (product rule, inverse rule, determinant and trace rules); use the cyclic property $\operatorname{tr}(PQ)=\operatorname{tr}(QP)$ — and $\operatorname{tr}(PQR)=\operatorname{tr}(RPQ)$ for several factors — to move $dX$ to the **end** of the trace; then interpret the coefficient as a transpose and match $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ to read off $G$. The target form is always $\operatorname{tr}(\text{coefficient matrix}\cdot dX)$, and the transpose must not be dropped when reading the gradient.

Two classic traps. First, **symmetrization**: $\partial(x^{\top}Ax)/\partial x=(A+A^{\top})x$ for general $A$, reducing to $2Ax$ only when $A$ is symmetric; the same holds for $\partial\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}AX)/\partial X=(A+A^{\top})X$. Second, **invertibility**: the compact forms of $\partial\det(X)/\partial X$ and $\partial\ln\det(X)/\partial X$ require $X$ to be invertible, and both are **unconstrained** (full matrix space) versions — restricting $X$ to symmetric matrices changes the tangent space, so they cannot be copied over. Comparable results in the literature may use a different layout; check the convention before importing them (scalar formulas are often transposes of ours).
derivation: 目标是把 $df$ 写成 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$，然后读出 $G=\partial f/\partial X$；向量情形则写成 $(\nabla f)^{\top}dx$。操作固定为三步：① 用乘积、逆、行列式、迹的法则展开 $df$；② 用 $\operatorname{tr}(PQR)=\operatorname{tr}(RPQ)$ 把 $dX$ 移到迹的末尾；③ 把 $dX$ 前的系数整体看成 $G^{\top}$，转置得到 $G$。条件是 $f$ 在 $X$ 处可微、所有迹的形状相容；分母布局保证 $G$ 与 $X$ 同型。结论：所有条目都可以现场重推，不必死记。

线性迹型：$f=\operatorname{tr}(AX)$，则 $$df=\operatorname{tr}(A\,dX)=\operatorname{tr}\big((A^{\top})^{\top}dX\big),$$ 故 $\partial\operatorname{tr}(AX)/\partial X=A^{\top}$。这不是 $A$：转置来自识别式中的 $G^{\top}$。同理 $\operatorname{tr}(AX^{\top})$ 的微分为 $\operatorname{tr}(A(dX)^{\top})=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\top}dX)$，故其梯度为 $A$；$\operatorname{tr}X$ 的梯度为 $I$。对 $\operatorname{tr}(AX)$ 要求 $A$ 为 $m\times n$、$X$ 为 $n\times m$；对 $\operatorname{tr}(AX^{\top})$ 要求 $A,X$ 同为 $m\times n$。两者都不要求方阵，只要迹有定义。结论：迹线性型的系数矩阵在读出梯度时要转置，$A^{\top}$ 与 $A$ 的位置不能凭记忆混用。

二次型与双线性型。对 $f(x)=x^{\top}Ax$，$$\begin{aligned}df&=(dx)^{\top}Ax+x^{\top}A\,dx\\&=x^{\top}A^{\top}dx+x^{\top}A\,dx\\&=x^{\top}(A+A^{\top})dx.\end{aligned}$$ 故 $\nabla f=(A+A^{\top})x$；只有 $A=A^{\top}$ 时才简化为 $2Ax$。对 $f(X)=a^{\top}Xb$，$$\begin{aligned}df&=a^{\top}(dX)b=\operatorname{tr}(ba^{\top}dX)\\&=\operatorname{tr}\big((ab^{\top})^{\top}dX\big).\end{aligned}$$ 故 $\partial(a^{\top}Xb)/\partial X=ab^{\top}$。条件是 $A$ 为 $n\times n$ 实矩阵、$a,b$ 与 $X$ 形状相容；二次型公式不要求 $A$ 对称，但必须对称化。结论：外积 $ab^{\top}$ 与对称化后的 $(A+A^{\top})x$ 是两张基本表。

迹二次型：设 $A$ 为 $n\times n$、$X$ 为 $n\times p$，$f=\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}AX)$。则 $$\begin{aligned}df&=\operatorname{tr}\big((dX)^{\top}AX\big)+\operatorname{tr}\big(X^{\top}A\,dX\big)\\&=\operatorname{tr}\big(X^{\top}A^{\top}dX\big)+\operatorname{tr}\big(X^{\top}A\,dX\big)\\&=\operatorname{tr}\big(((A+A^{\top})X)^{\top}dX\big),\end{aligned}$$ 故梯度为 $(A+A^{\top})X$；$A$ 对称时为 $2AX$。第一步用了 $\operatorname{tr}((dX)^{\top}AX)=\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}A^{\top}dX)$（标量转置不变），最后一步用了 $(A+A^{\top})X$ 的转置。条件：形状相容、$f$ 可微。结论：无论 $X$ 是向量还是矩阵，二次型的梯度都要先对称化 $A$。

行列式与逆型（$X$ 可逆）。由 Jacobi 公式 $d\det X=\det X\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX)$，而 $\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX)=\operatorname{tr}((X^{-\top})^{\top}dX)$，故 $$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial\det X}{\partial X}&=\det(X)\,X^{-\top},\\ \frac{\partial\ln\det X}{\partial X}&=X^{-\top}.\end{aligned}$$ 对 $f=\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}A)$，用 $d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}dX\,X^{-1}$：$$df=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX\,X^{-1}A)=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}AX^{-1}dX),$$ 故 $\partial f/\partial X=-X^{-\top}A^{\top}X^{-\top}$。条件：$X$ 可逆（$\ln\det$ 还要求 $\det X>0$ 以取实对数，例如 $X$ 正定）。结论：逆型公式的两个转置都不能漏。

两个易错点。其一，上面的 $\partial\det X/\partial X$ 与 $\partial\ln\det X/\partial X$ 是**无约束**（整个矩阵空间）版本；若把 $X$ 限制在对称矩阵上，切空间只剩对称方向，内在梯度应取对称部分 $\operatorname{sym}(G)=(G+G^{\top})/2$，因为 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ 只看见 $dX$ 的对称部分。对对称可逆 $X$，$\det X\,X^{-\top}=\det X\,X^{-1}$ 已经对称，故该条不变；但 $\operatorname{tr}(AX)$ 在对称子空间上的内在梯度是 $(A+A^{\top})/2$，不是 $A^{\top}$。其二，任何结果都可用有限差分核对：任取 $B$，比较 $(f(X+tB)-f(X))/t$ 与 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}B)$。条件：约束流形上的内积与切空间必须固定。结论：先确认是否无约束，再套公式。
derivationEn: The goal is to write $df$ as $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ and then read off $G=\partial f/\partial X$; in the vector case, write $df=(\nabla f)^{\top}dx$. The procedure has three steps: (i) expand $df$ using the product, inverse, determinant and trace rules; (ii) use $\operatorname{tr}(PQR)=\operatorname{tr}(RPQ)$ to move $dX$ to the end of the trace; (iii) regard the coefficient of $dX$ as $G^{\top}$ and transpose it to obtain $G$. The hypotheses are differentiability of $f$ at $X$ and compatible trace shapes; the denominator layout guarantees that $G$ has the shape of $X$. Conclusion: every entry can be re-derived on the spot, with no need for memorization.

Linear trace forms: for $f=\operatorname{tr}(AX)$, $$df=\operatorname{tr}(A\,dX)=\operatorname{tr}\big((A^{\top})^{\top}dX\big),$$ so $\partial\operatorname{tr}(AX)/\partial X=A^{\top}$. It is not $A$: the transpose comes from $G^{\top}$ in the identification formula. Likewise, $\operatorname{tr}(AX^{\top})$ has differential $\operatorname{tr}(A(dX)^{\top})=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\top}dX)$, so its gradient is $A$; the gradient of $\operatorname{tr}X$ is $I$. For $\operatorname{tr}(AX)$ one needs $A$ of size $m\times n$ and $X$ of size $n\times m$; for $\operatorname{tr}(AX^{\top})$ one needs $A,X$ both of size $m\times n$. Neither requires square matrices, only a defined trace. Conclusion: the coefficient matrix of a linear trace form is transposed when the gradient is read off; $A^{\top}$ and $A$ must not be confused.

Quadratic and bilinear forms. For $f(x)=x^{\top}Ax$, $$\begin{aligned}df&=(dx)^{\top}Ax+x^{\top}A\,dx\\&=x^{\top}A^{\top}dx+x^{\top}A\,dx\\&=x^{\top}(A+A^{\top})dx.\end{aligned}$$ so $\nabla f=(A+A^{\top})x$; it reduces to $2Ax$ only when $A=A^{\top}$. For $f(X)=a^{\top}Xb$, $$\begin{aligned}df&=a^{\top}(dX)b=\operatorname{tr}(ba^{\top}dX)\\&=\operatorname{tr}\big((ab^{\top})^{\top}dX\big).\end{aligned}$$ so $\partial(a^{\top}Xb)/\partial X=ab^{\top}$. The hypotheses are that $A$ is a real $n\times n$ matrix and $a,b$ have compatible shapes with $X$; the quadratic formula does not require symmetry of $A$, but symmetrization is mandatory. Conclusion: the outer product $ab^{\top}$ and the symmetrized $(A+A^{\top})x$ are two basic entries.

Trace-quadratic form: let $A$ be $n\times n$ and $X$ be $n\times p$, with $f=\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}AX)$. Then $$\begin{aligned}df&=\operatorname{tr}\big((dX)^{\top}AX\big)+\operatorname{tr}\big(X^{\top}A\,dX\big)\\&=\operatorname{tr}\big(X^{\top}A^{\top}dX\big)+\operatorname{tr}\big(X^{\top}A\,dX\big)\\&=\operatorname{tr}\big(((A+A^{\top})X)^{\top}dX\big),\end{aligned}$$ so the gradient is $(A+A^{\top})X$, which becomes $2AX$ when $A$ is symmetric. The first step uses $\operatorname{tr}((dX)^{\top}AX)=\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}A^{\top}dX)$ (a scalar equals its transpose), and the last uses the transpose of $(A+A^{\top})X$. The hypotheses are compatible shapes and differentiability. Conclusion: whether $X$ is a vector or a matrix, a quadratic form must be symmetrized in $A$ before reading the gradient.

Determinant and inverse forms ($X$ invertible). Jacobi's formula gives $d\det X=\det X\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX)$, and $\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX)=\operatorname{tr}((X^{-\top})^{\top}dX)$, hence $$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial\det X}{\partial X}&=\det(X)\,X^{-\top},\\ \frac{\partial\ln\det X}{\partial X}&=X^{-\top}.\end{aligned}$$ For $f=\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}A)$, use $d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}dX\,X^{-1}$: $$df=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX\,X^{-1}A)=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}AX^{-1}dX),$$ so $\partial f/\partial X=-X^{-\top}A^{\top}X^{-\top}$. The hypotheses are invertibility of $X$ (and $\det X>0$ for the real logarithm, e.g. positive definite $X$). Conclusion: neither transpose in the inverse formula may be dropped.

Two pitfalls. First, the formulas for $\partial\det X/\partial X$ and $\partial\ln\det X/\partial X$ above are **unconstrained** (full matrix space) versions; if $X$ is restricted to symmetric matrices, the tangent space contains only symmetric directions, and the intrinsic gradient is the symmetric part $\operatorname{sym}(G)=(G+G^{\top})/2$, because $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ sees only the symmetric part of $dX$. For symmetric invertible $X$, $\det X\,X^{-\top}=\det X\,X^{-1}$ is already symmetric, so that entry is unchanged; but the intrinsic gradient of $\operatorname{tr}(AX)$ on the symmetric subspace is $(A+A^{\top})/2$, not $A^{\top}$. Second, every result can be checked by finite differences: for any $B$, compare $(f(X+tB)-f(X))/t$ with $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}B)$. The hypothesis is that the inner product and tangent space on the constrained manifold are fixed. Conclusion: decide first whether the problem is constrained, then apply a formula.

formulas.note: 线性型与范数：aᵀx 的梯度是 a，线性映射 Ax 的雅可比是 A，‖x‖² 的梯度是 2x（a 与 2x 都与 x 同型；A 是 m×n 的雅可比矩阵，一般与 x 不同型）。
formulas.noteEn: Linear forms and norms: the gradient of aᵀx is a, the Jacobian of Ax is A, and the gradient of ‖x‖² is 2x (a and 2x share the shape of x; A is an m×n Jacobian and generally has a different shape).

formulas.note: 二次型：一般 A 必须先对称化；只有 A 对称时才简写成 2Ax——这是最常见的出错点。
formulas.noteEn: Quadratic form: for general A the answer must be symmetrized; only symmetric A allows the shorthand 2Ax — the most common source of errors.

formulas.note: 迹的线性型：系数矩阵要转置；tr(X) 的梯度是单位阵（有些文献记作 E）。
formulas.noteEn: Linear trace forms: the coefficient matrix gets transposed; the gradient of tr(X) is the identity matrix (some texts write E for it).

formulas.note: 迹二次型与双线性型：前者得到对称化后的 (A+Aᵀ)X；后者是列乘行的外积 abᵀ。
formulas.noteEn: Trace-quadratic and bilinear forms: the first gives the symmetrized (A+Aᵀ)X, the second gives the outer product abᵀ.

formulas.note: 行列式与逆（X 可逆）：前两条是无约束情形的公式；最后一条由逆的微分法则直接得到。
formulas.noteEn: Determinant and inverse (X invertible): the first two are the unconstrained versions, and the last one follows directly from the inverse rule.

properties: 上表全部分式在分母布局下成立，且都能用 $df=(\partial f/\partial x)^{\top}dx$ 或 $df=\operatorname{tr}((\partial f/\partial X)^{\top}dX)$ 在一两步内验证。
对称化是二次型公式的灵魂：一般写法是 $(A+A^{\top})x$ 与 $(A+A^{\top})X$，只有 $A$ 对称时才退化为 $2Ax$、$2AX$。
迹的轮换 $\operatorname{tr}(PQR)=\operatorname{tr}(RPQ)$ 是推导主力：它把 $dX$ 挪到迹的末尾，从而直接读出梯度。
$\partial\det(X)/\partial X=\det(X)X^{-\top}$ 与 $\partial\ln\det(X)/\partial X=X^{-\top}$ 要求 $X$ 可逆，且是无约束版本；把 $X$ 限制在对称矩阵上时切空间改变，不能照搬。
数值检验：任取 $X$ 与方向 $B$，比较 $(f(X+tB)-f(X))/t$ 与 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}B)$，$t$ 足够小时两者吻合。
propertiesEn: Every identity above holds in the denominator layout, and each can be verified in one or two lines from $df=(\partial f/\partial x)^{\top}dx$ or $df=\operatorname{tr}((\partial f/\partial X)^{\top}dX)$.
Symmetrization is the heart of the quadratic-form formulas: the general answers are $(A+A^{\top})x$ and $(A+A^{\top})X$, collapsing to $2Ax$ and $2AX$ only for symmetric A.
The cyclic property $\operatorname{tr}(PQR)=\operatorname{tr}(RPQ)$ is the workhorse: it moves dX to the end of the trace so the gradient can be read off directly.

The formulas $\partial\det(X)/\partial X=\det(X)X^{-\top}$ and $\partial\ln\det(X)/\partial X=X^{-\top}$ require X to be invertible and are unconstrained versions; restricting X to symmetric matrices changes the tangent space, so they cannot be copied over.
Numerical check: for any X and direction B, compare $(f(X+tB)-f(X))/t$ with $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}B)$; for small t the two agree.

examples.problem: 推导 $\partial\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}AX)/\partial X$，并用有限差分在 $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$、$X=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ 处核对。
examples.solution:
**推导**：$d\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}AX)=\operatorname{tr}((dX)^{\top}AX)+\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}A\,dX)=\operatorname{tr}((AX)^{\top}dX)+\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}A\,dX)=\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}(A^{\top}+A)dX)=\operatorname{tr}\big(((A+A^{\top})X)^{\top}dX\big)$，故梯度 $G=(A+A^{\top})X$（这里用到了 $\operatorname{tr}((dX)^{\top}AX)=\operatorname{tr}((AX)^{\top}dX)$）。

**数值**：$A+A^{\top}=\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&6\end{pmatrix}$，$G=(A+A^{\top})X=\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\2&8\end{pmatrix}$，且 $\operatorname{tr}(X^{\top}AX)=7$。

**有限差分**（把 $X$ 的第 $(i,j)$ 元加 $t$，读一次项系数）：$(1,1)$ 元得 $7+2t+t^2$，$(1,2)$ 元得 $7+4t+t^2$，$(2,1)$ 元得 $7+2t+3t^2$，$(2,2)$ 元得 $7+8t+3t^2$，对应 $2,4,2,8$，与 $G$ 完全一致 ✓。

examples.problem: 用凑迹法推导 $\partial(a^{\top}Xb)/\partial X$ 与 $\partial\operatorname{tr}(AX)/\partial X$，并对前者取 $a=(1,2)^{\top}$、$b=(3,1)^{\top}$、$X=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ 做有限差分核对。
examples.solution:
**外积公式**：$d(a^{\top}Xb)=a^{\top}(dX)b=\operatorname{tr}(a^{\top}(dX)b)=\operatorname{tr}(ba^{\top}dX)=\operatorname{tr}\big((ab^{\top})^{\top}dX\big)$，故 $\partial(a^{\top}Xb)/\partial X=ab^{\top}$。

**迹公式**：$d\operatorname{tr}(AX)=\operatorname{tr}(A\,dX)$，对照 $\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dX)$ 得 $G=A^{\top}$。

**数值核对**：$ab^{\top}=\begin{pmatrix}3&1\\6&2\end{pmatrix}$，$f(X)=a^{\top}Xb=6$；分别把四个元素加 $t$，得 $f=6+3t$、$6+t$、$6+6t$、$6+2t$，一次项系数 $3,1,6,2$ 正是 $ab^{\top}$ 的四个元素 ✓。

matrix-calculus-optimization.definition:
矩阵微分的第一个大应用是最优化：写出 $\nabla f=0$ 求驻点，再看二阶条件。与多元微积分相比，「增量」在求导技术上：以前逐个算偏导，现在用 $d$ 与迹整块地算梯度与 Hessian。标量导数沿用全批统一约定（**分母/梯度布局**）：$\nabla f=\partial f/\partial x$ 与 $x$ 同型（文献中常按分子布局写成行向量，与本库互为转置，套公式前先核对约定）。

**一阶条件**：$f$ 可微时，局部极值点 $x^{*}$ 必须满足 $\nabla f(x^{*})=0$。**二阶条件**：Hessian $H(x)=\partial^{2}f/\partial x\,\partial x^{\top}$ 的第 $(i,j)$ 元是 $\partial^{2}f/\partial x_i\partial x_j$，在二阶偏导连续时**对称**。于是：$H(x^{*})$ 正定 $\Rightarrow$ $x^{*}$ 是严格局部极小点；$H(x^{*})$ 负定 $\Rightarrow$ 严格局部极大点；$H(x^{*})$ 不定（特征值有正有负）$\Rightarrow$ 鞍点。注意正定给出的是**充分不必要**条件：$H$ 半正定甚至 $H=0$ 时也可能是严格极小，例如 $f(x)=x^4$ 在 $x=0$ 处 $H=0$，但 $0$ 依然是严格极小点——这种情形要靠更高阶项判定。

最常用的两个模型。**无约束二次型**：$f(x)=x^{\top}Ax-b^{\top}x$（取 $A=A^{\top}$）满足 $\nabla f=2Ax-b$、$H=2A$；当 $A$ 正定时有唯一极小点 $x^{*}=\frac{1}{2}A^{-1}b$。**最小二乘**：$f(x)=\|Ax-b\|^{2}$ 有 $\nabla f=2A^{\top}(Ax-b)$，令梯度为零即得**正规方程** $A^{\top}Ax=A^{\top}b$；$A$ 列满秩时 $x^{*}=(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}b$，秩亏时解不唯一，用广义逆取最小范数解 $A^{+}b$。

两个方向的一句话延拓：数值上用**梯度下降** $x\leftarrow x-\eta\nabla f(x)$ 迭代；带约束时用**拉格朗日乘数法**把约束的梯度并入一阶条件。
matrix-calculus-optimization.definitionEn:
The first big application of matrix calculus is optimization: solve $\nabla f=0$ for stationary points and then apply second-order conditions. Compared with multivariable calculus the upgrade is technical — instead of computing partial derivatives one by one, the differential and the trace deliver the gradient and the Hessian in one block. Scalar derivatives keep the batch-wide **denominator (gradient) layout**, so $\nabla f=\partial f/\partial x$ has the shape of $x$ (much of the literature writes the gradient as a row vector, the transpose of ours; check the convention before plugging in a formula).

**First-order condition**: if $f$ is differentiable, a local extremum $x^{*}$ must satisfy $\nabla f(x^{*})=0$. **Second-order conditions**: the Hessian $H(x)=\partial^{2}f/\partial x\,\partial x^{\top}$ has $(i,j)$ entry $\partial^{2}f/\partial x_i\partial x_j$ and is **symmetric** whenever the second partials are continuous. Hence: $H(x^{*})$ positive definite $\Rightarrow$ strict local minimum; $H(x^{*})$ negative definite $\Rightarrow$ strict local maximum; $H(x^{*})$ indefinite (eigenvalues of both signs) $\Rightarrow$ saddle point. Positive definiteness is **sufficient, not necessary**: a positive semidefinite Hessian — even $H=0$ — may still give a strict minimum, as $f(x)=x^4$ does at $x=0$, where the decision needs higher-order terms.

Two workhorse models. **Unconstrained quadratic form**: $f(x)=x^{\top}Ax-b^{\top}x$ with $A=A^{\top}$ has $\nabla f=2Ax-b$ and $H=2A$; if $A$ is positive definite the unique minimizer is $x^{*}=\frac{1}{2}A^{-1}b$. **Least squares**: $f(x)=\|Ax-b\|^{2}$ has $\nabla f=2A^{\top}(Ax-b)$, and setting it to zero gives the **normal equations** $A^{\top}Ax=A^{\top}b$; when $A$ has full column rank, $x^{*}=(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}b$, while in the rank-deficient case the solutions form a set and the pseudoinverse selects the least-norm one, $A^{+}b$.

Two one-line extensions: numerically, **gradient descent** iterates $x\leftarrow x-\eta\nabla f(x)$; with constraints, the **method of Lagrange multipliers** folds the constraint gradients into the first-order condition.
derivation:
设 $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ 在 $x^{*}$ 处可微，且 $x^{*}$ 是定义域的内点、局部极小点。对任意方向 $d$，一元函数 $\varphi(t)=f(x^{*}+td)$ 在 $t=0$ 取局部极小，故 $$0=\varphi'(0)=
abla f(x^{*})^{	op}d.$$ 该式对所有 $d$ 成立，取 $d=
abla f(x^{*})$ 得 $\|
abla f(x^{*})\|^{2}=0$，即 $
abla f(x^{*})=0$。条件是内点与可微性；边界点的一阶条件要换成可行方向或 KKT 条件。结论：驻点是局部极值的必要条件，但非充分条件（鞍点也满足）。

设 $f$ 在 $x^{*}$ 的邻域内 $C^{2}$，Hessian $H(x)=\partial^{2}f/\partial x\,\partial x^{\top}$ 连续，故对称。若 $\nabla f(x^{*})=0$，Taylor 展开为 $$f(x^{*}+td)=f(x^{*})+\frac{t^{2}}{2}d^{\top}H(x^{*})d+o(t^{2}).$$ 若 $H(x^{*})\succ0$，则 $d^{\top}Hd\ge\lambda_{\min}\|d\|^{2}>0$，对小 $t\ne0$ 有 $f(x^{*}+td)>f(x^{*})$，故为严格局部极小；$H\prec0$ 时为严格局部极大。若 $H$ 不定，取 $d_{+},d_{-}$ 使其二次型分别为正、负，则沿两方向的函数值一增一减，$x^{*}$ 是鞍点。条件是 $C^{2}$ 与 $H$ 的定号性；$H$ 半正定（含 $H=0$）时此判据失效。结论：正定、负定、不定分别给出严格极小、严格极大、鞍点，但正定只是充分条件。

无约束二次型：取 $A=A^{	op}\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes n}$、$b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$，$$f(x)=x^{	op}Ax-b^{	op}x.$$ 由 $
abla(x^{	op}Ax)=(A+A^{	op})x=2Ax$、$
abla(b^{	op}x)=b$，得 $$
abla f=2Ax-b,\qquad H=2A.$$ 令梯度为零得 $Ax=b/2$；当 $A\succ0$ 时 $A$ 可逆且 $H\succ0$，唯一全局极小点为 $$x^{*}= rac12A^{-1}b,\qquad f(x^{*})=- rac14b^{	op}A^{-1}b.$$ 条件是 $A$ 对称；正定性保证唯一极小，$A$ 不定时驻点是鞍点，$A$ 半正定奇异时需另行分析。结论：二次型的梯度、Hessian 与极小点都是整块公式。

最小二乘：$A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$、$b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$，$$f(x)=\|Ax-b\|^{2}=x^{\top}A^{\top}Ax-2b^{\top}Ax+b^{\top}b.$$ 由二次型公式（$A^{\top}A$ 对称）得 $$\nabla f=2A^{\top}Ax-2A^{\top}b=2A^{\top}(Ax-b),\qquad H=2A^{\top}A\succeq0.$$ 令梯度为零得正规方程 $$A^{\top}Ax=A^{\top}b.$$ 它总有解，因为 $A^{\top}b\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\top})=\operatorname{range}(A^{\top}A)$。若 $A$ 列满秩，$A^{\top}A\succ0$，解唯一：$$x^{*}=(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}b;$$ 若秩亏，解集是仿射子空间，广义逆给出最小范数解 $A^{+}b$。条件：$A$ 实矩阵、$b$ 同维；列满秩才保证唯一。结论：正规方程是最小二乘的一阶条件，Hessian 半正定保证凸性。

用正交性证明最优：设 $x$ 满足正规方程，令 $r=b-Ax$，则 $A^{\top}r=0$。对任意 $z$，$$\begin{aligned}f(x+z)&=\|r-Az\|^{2}\\&=\|r\|^{2}-2r^{\top}Az+\|Az\|^{2}\\&=f(x)+\|Az\|^{2}\ge f(x),\end{aligned}$$ 其中交叉项 $r^{\top}Az=(A^{\top}r)^{\top}z=0$。故 $x$ 是全局极小点；等号成立当且仅当 $Az=0$。几何上 $r\perp\operatorname{col}(A)$，$Ax$ 是 $b$ 在列空间上的正交投影。条件：$x$ 满足正规方程；列满秩时 $Az\ne0$（$z\ne0$），极小点唯一。结论：正规方程不仅是一阶必要条件，也直接给出全局最优性。

半正定的细微差别与二阶条件的方向。若 $f$ 在 $x^{*}$ 局部极小且 $C^{2}$，则必有 $H(x^{*})\succeq0$（否则沿负曲率方向 $d^{\top}Hd<0$，$f$ 会下降），这是二阶必要条件；但 $H\succ0$ 只是严格极小的充分条件，不是必要条件。反例 $f(x)=x^{4}$ 在 $x=0$：$f'=4x^{3}$、$f''=12x^{2}$，故 $H(0)=0$ 半正定，而 $0$ 仍是严格极小点，需看更高阶项。反过来，$f(x)=x^{3}$ 在 $0$ 处同样 $H(0)=0$，但 $0$ 不是极小点，所以半正定本身也不充分。数值上一阶方法用 $x_{k+1}=x_{k}-\eta\nabla f(x_{k})$，牛顿法在 $H\succ0$ 时用方向 $-H^{-1}\nabla f$。条件是 $C^{2}$ 保证 $H$ 对称。结论：在驻点处，$H$ 正定 $\Rightarrow$ 严格极小；局部极小 $\Rightarrow$ $H$ 半正定；反向蕴含均不成立。
derivationEn:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $x^{*}$, an interior point of its domain and a local minimum. For every direction $d$, the one-variable function $\varphi(t)=f(x^{*}+td)$ has a local minimum at $t=0$, so $$0=\varphi'(0)=
abla f(x^{*})^{	op}d.$$ This holds for all $d$; taking $d=
abla f(x^{*})$ gives $\|
abla f(x^{*})\|^{2}=0$, hence $
abla f(x^{*})=0$. The hypotheses are an interior point and differentiability; at a boundary point the first-order condition is replaced by feasible directions or KKT conditions. Conclusion: a stationary point is necessary for a local extremum, but not sufficient (saddles also satisfy it).

Assume $f$ is $C^{2}$ near $x^{*}$, with continuous Hessian $H(x)=\partial^{2}f/\partial x\,\partial x^{\top}$, which is therefore symmetric. If $\nabla f(x^{*})=0$, Taylor's expansion gives $$f(x^{*}+td)=f(x^{*})+\frac{t^{2}}{2}d^{\top}H(x^{*})d+o(t^{2}).$$ If $H(x^{*})\succ0$, then $d^{\top}Hd\ge\lambda_{\min}\|d\|^{2}>0$, so $f(x^{*}+td)>f(x^{*})$ for small $t\ne0$: a strict local minimum. If $H\prec0$, it is a strict local maximum. If $H$ is indefinite, choose $d_{+},d_{-}$ making the quadratic form positive and negative; along these directions $f$ increases and decreases, so $x^{*}$ is a saddle. The hypotheses are $C^{2}$ and a definite sign of $H$; when $H$ is only positive semidefinite (including $H=0$), this test is inconclusive. Conclusion: positive definite, negative definite and indefinite give a strict minimum, a strict maximum and a saddle respectively, but positive definiteness is only sufficient.

Unconstrained quadratic form: take $A=A^{	op}\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes n}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$, $$f(x)=x^{	op}Ax-b^{	op}x.$$ Since $
abla(x^{	op}Ax)=(A+A^{	op})x=2Ax$ and $
abla(b^{	op}x)=b$, $$
abla f=2Ax-b,\qquad H=2A.$$ Setting the gradient to zero gives $Ax=b/2$; when $A\succ0$, $A$ is invertible and $H\succ0$, so the unique global minimizer is $$x^{*}= rac12A^{-1}b,\qquad f(x^{*})=- rac14b^{	op}A^{-1}b.$$ The hypothesis is symmetry of $A$; positive definiteness guarantees a unique minimum, an indefinite $A$ makes the stationary point a saddle, and a singular positive semidefinite $A$ needs separate analysis. Conclusion: the gradient, Hessian and minimizer of a quadratic form are all block formulas.

Least squares: $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$, $$f(x)=\|Ax-b\|^{2}=x^{\top}A^{\top}Ax-2b^{\top}Ax+b^{\top}b.$$ The quadratic formula (with $A^{\top}A$ symmetric) gives $$\nabla f=2A^{\top}Ax-2A^{\top}b=2A^{\top}(Ax-b),\qquad H=2A^{\top}A\succeq0.$$ Setting the gradient to zero yields the normal equations $$A^{\top}Ax=A^{\top}b.$$ They are always consistent, because $A^{\top}b\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\top})=\operatorname{range}(A^{\top}A)$. If $A$ has full column rank, $A^{\top}A\succ0$ and the solution is unique: $$x^{*}=(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}b;$$ if $A$ is rank deficient, the solution set is an affine subspace and the pseudoinverse selects the least-norm solution $A^{+}b$. The hypotheses are a real $A$ and a compatible $b$; uniqueness requires full column rank. Conclusion: the normal equations are the first-order condition for least squares, and the positive semidefinite Hessian guarantees convexity.

Optimality via orthogonality: let $x$ satisfy the normal equations and set $r=b-Ax$, so $A^{\top}r=0$. For any $z$, $$\begin{aligned}f(x+z)&=\|r-Az\|^{2}\\&=\|r\|^{2}-2r^{\top}Az+\|Az\|^{2}\\&=f(x)+\|Az\|^{2}\ge f(x),\end{aligned}$$ because the cross term $r^{\top}Az=(A^{\top}r)^{\top}z=0$. Hence $x$ is a global minimizer, with equality iff $Az=0$. Geometrically, $r\perp\operatorname{col}(A)$ and $Ax$ is the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space. The hypothesis is that $x$ satisfies the normal equations; with full column rank, $Az\ne0$ for $z\ne0$ and the minimizer is unique. Conclusion: the normal equations are not only necessary but directly imply global optimality.

The positive-semidefinite subtlety and the direction of the second-order conditions. If $f$ has a local minimum at $x^{*}$ and is $C^{2}$, then necessarily $H(x^{*})\succeq0$ (otherwise $f$ decreases along a direction with $d^{\top}Hd<0$); this is the second-order necessary condition. But $H\succ0$ is only sufficient for a strict minimum, not necessary. Counterexample: $f(x)=x^{4}$ at $x=0$ has $f'=4x^{3}$ and $f''=12x^{2}$, so $H(0)=0$ is positive semidefinite, yet $0$ is still a strict minimum; higher-order terms decide. Conversely, $f(x)=x^{3}$ at $0$ also has $H(0)=0$, but $0$ is not a minimum, so positive semidefiniteness alone is not sufficient either. Numerically, first-order methods iterate $x_{k+1}=x_{k}-\eta\nabla f(x_{k})$, while Newton's method uses the direction $-H^{-1}\nabla f$ when $H\succ0$. The hypothesis $C^{2}$ makes $H$ symmetric. Conclusion: at a stationary point, $H$ positive definite $\Rightarrow$ strict minimum, and a local minimum $\Rightarrow$ $H$ positive semidefinite; neither converse holds.

formulas.note: 一阶必要条件与 Hessian 的定义；分母布局下 H 的第 (i,j) 元是 ∂²f/∂xᵢ∂xⱼ。
formulas.noteEn: The first-order necessary condition and the definition of the Hessian; in the denominator layout its (i,j) entry is ∂²f/∂xᵢ∂xⱼ.

formulas.latex: H(x^{*})\succ0\Rightarrow\text{严格极小},\qquad H(x^{*})\prec0\Rightarrow\text{严格极大},\qquad H\ \text{不定}\Rightarrow\text{鞍点}
formulas.note: 正定只是严格极小的充分条件，不是必要条件；H 半正定也可能给出严格极小（如 x⁴）。
formulas.noteEn: Positive definiteness is only sufficient for a strict minimum, never necessary; a positive semidefinite Hessian may also give a strict minimum (e.g. x⁴).

formulas.note: 二次型的完整解：梯度、Hessian 与正定时的唯一极小点都是整块公式。
formulas.noteEn: The complete quadratic-form solution: gradient, Hessian and, for positive definite A, the unique minimizer — all in closed form.

formulas.note: 最小二乘：梯度里的 2 与 Aᵀ 位置都不能错；令梯度为零即得正规方程。
formulas.noteEn: Least squares: neither the factor 2 nor the position of Aᵀ in the gradient may be misplaced; setting it to zero yields the normal equations.

formulas.note: 梯度下降：沿负梯度方向走一步，步长 η 需要适当选取。
formulas.noteEn: Gradient descent: one step along the negative gradient, with the step size η chosen appropriately.

properties: Hessian 对称（二阶偏导连续时混合偏导可交换），所以二阶条件只看 $H$ 的特征值符号；沿单位特征向量 $v$ 的方向，$f$ 的局部曲率恰为 $v^{\top}Hv=\lambda$。
正定 $\Rightarrow$ 严格极小是**充分不必要**；$H$ 半正定也可能给出严格极小（$f(x)=x^4$ 在 $0$ 处 $H=0$），需要更高阶项才能判定。
二次型求导前先对称化：$\nabla(x^{\top}Ax)=(A+A^{\top})x$；本节的二次型公式默认 $A=A^{\top}$，此时才写成 $2Ax$。
最小二乘的几何：最优残差 $r=b-Ax^{*}$ 与 $A$ 的列空间正交（$A^{\top}r=0$），$Ax^{*}$ 就是 $b$ 在列空间上的正交投影；$A$ 列满秩时解唯一，秩亏时用广义逆取最小范数解。
迭代法（梯度下降）只用到一阶信息：步长过大会发散，收敛慢时可用牛顿法方向 $-H^{-1}\nabla f$ 加速（代价是计算并求逆 $H$）。
propertiesEn: The Hessian is symmetric (mixed partials commute when the second derivatives are continuous), so the second-order test depends only on the signs of its eigenvalues; along a unit eigenvector v the local curvature of f equals $v^{\top}Hv=\lambda$.

Positive definiteness is sufficient but not necessary for a strict minimum; a positive semidefinite Hessian may also give a strict minimum ($f(x)=x^4$ at 0, where H = 0), and higher-order terms are then needed.
Symmetrize before differentiating a quadratic form: $\nabla(x^{\top}Ax)=(A+A^{\top})x$; the formulas here assume $A=A^{\top}$, in which case $2Ax$ is correct.

Least squares has a geometric meaning: the optimal residual $r=b-Ax^{*}$ is orthogonal to the column space of A ($A^{\top}r=0$), so $Ax^{*}$ is the orthogonal projection of b; the solution is unique for full column rank, and the pseudoinverse selects the least-norm solution in the rank-deficient case.

Gradient descent uses only first-order information: too large a step diverges, and slow convergence can be accelerated by the Newton direction $-H^{-1}\nabla f$, at the cost of forming and inverting H.

examples.problem: 取 $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$、$b=(3,1,5)^{\top}$，最小化 $f(x)=\|Ax-b\|^{2}$：写出 $\nabla f$ 与正规方程，解出 $x^{*}$ 并验证它确实最优。
examples.solution:
**梯度**：展开得 $f(x)=x^{\top}A^{\top}Ax-2b^{\top}Ax+b^{\top}b$，由二次型公式 $\nabla f=2A^{\top}Ax-2A^{\top}b=2A^{\top}(Ax-b)$。

**正规方程**：$A^{\top}A=\begin{pmatrix}3&6\\6&14\end{pmatrix}$，$A^{\top}b=(9,20)^{\top}$，即 $\begin{cases}3x_1+6x_2=9\\6x_1+14x_2=20\end{cases}$；$\det(A^{\top}A)=6$，解得 $x^{*}=(1,1)^{\top}$（代回两个方程都成立 ✓）。

**验证最优性**：$Ax^{*}=(2,3,4)^{\top}$，残差 $r=b-Ax^{*}=(1,-2,1)^{\top}$，而 $A^{\top}r=(0,0)^{\top}$，即残差与 $A$ 的两列都正交，于是 $\nabla f(x^{*})=0$ ✓。此时 $f(x^{*})=1+4+1=6$；对比 $x=(0,0)^{\top}$ 时 $f=35$、$x=(2,1)^{\top}$ 时 $f=0+9+0=9$，都更大 ✓。

examples.problem: 设 $f(x)=x^{\top}Ax-b^{\top}x$，其中 $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$、$b=(6,6)^{\top}$。求驻点并判断类型。
examples.solution: $\nabla f=2Ax-b=(4x_1+2x_2-6,\;2x_1+4x_2-6)^{\top}$，令 $\nabla f=0$ 得 $x^{*}=(1,1)^{\top}$。Hessian $H=2A=\begin{pmatrix}4&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$ 的顺序主子式为 $4>0$ 与 $16-4=12>0$，故 $A$ 正定（$H$ 的特征值为 $2,6$），$x^{*}$ 是严格极小点。函数值 $f(x^{*})=x^{*\top}Ax^{*}-b^{\top}x^{*}=6-12=-6$。

matrix-spectral-derivatives.definition:
本节点沿用全批统一约定（标量导数按**分母/梯度布局**）——$\partial f/\partial A$ 与 $A$ 同型，恒有 $df=\mathrm{tr}\big((\partial f/\partial A)^{\top}dA\big)$。文献里其他布局的公式需先对齐约定（标量公式常与本批互为转置）。

特征值 $\lambda_i(A)$、奇异值 $\sigma_i(A)$ 作为矩阵元素的函数如何求导？在**单重**（simple，代数重数 1）特征值处，一阶变化只沿对应特征向量「采样」扰动矩阵：实对称（更一般地 Hermitian，把转置换成共轭转置）情形有 $d\lambda_i=v_i^{\top}(dA)\,v_i$，其中 $v_i$ 是单位特征向量，$(dA)$ 被夹在 $v_i^{\top}$ 与 $v_i$ 中间；一般非对称矩阵需要左特征向量 $w_i$（$w_i^{\top}A=\lambda_i w_i^{\top}$）修正为 $d\lambda_i=\dfrac{w_i^{\top}(dA)v_i}{w_i^{\top}v_i}$。推导思路（对称情形）：对 $A(t)v(t)=\lambda(t)v(t)$ 两边求导得 $\dot Av+A\dot v=\dot\lambda v+\lambda\dot v$，左乘 $v^{\top}$，利用 $v^{\top}A=\lambda v^{\top}$ 与规范化条件 $v^{\top}\dot v=0$，即得 $\dot\lambda=v^{\top}\dot Av$。

奇异值照样简洁：对**单重正奇异值** $\sigma_i$ 与单位左右奇异向量 $u_i,v_i$，有 $d\sigma_i=u_i^{\top}(dA)\,v_i$（**不带绝对值**——$\sigma_i>0$ 处函数光滑）。整体特例是把矩阵平方：$d\|A\|_F^2=2\,\mathrm{tr}(A^{\top}dA)$，完全不需要奇异值分解。使用时务必核对前提：重特征值、重奇异值处一阶公式可能失效甚至分叉——$A(t)=\mathrm{diag}(t,-t)$ 的最大特征值是 $|t|$，在 $t=0$ 处有折点；含 Jordan 块时特征值按 $t^{1/m}$ 的分数幂展开（$m$ 为块阶数）。奇异值恒非负，$\sigma_i=0$ 且扰动使秩提升时 $\sigma_i(t)$ 形如 $|ct|$，公式只给出单侧方向导数。
matrix-spectral-derivatives.definitionEn:
This node follows the batch-wide convention: **denominator (gradient) layout for scalar derivatives** — $\partial f/\partial A$ has the same shape as $A$, and always $df=\mathrm{tr}\big((\partial f/\partial A)^{\top}dA\big)$. Sources that use a different layout state the same results transposed (scalar formulas especially), so align conventions before plugging in anything.

How does one differentiate eigenvalues $\lambda_i(A)$ and singular values $\sigma_i(A)$ with respect to the entries of $A$? At a **simple** eigenvalue (algebraic multiplicity one) the first-order change merely samples the perturbation along the corresponding eigenvector: for a real symmetric (more generally Hermitian) matrix, $d\lambda_i=v_i^{\top}(dA)\,v_i$, where $v_i$ is a unit eigenvector and $(dA)$ is sandwiched between $v_i^{\top}$ and $v_i$; a general non-symmetric matrix needs the left eigenvector $w_i$ ($w_i^{\top}A=\lambda_i w_i^{\top}$) and the correction $d\lambda_i=\frac{w_i^{\top}(dA)v_i}{w_i^{\top}v_i}$. Derivation (symmetric case): differentiate $A(t)v(t)=\lambda(t)v(t)$, multiply on the left by $v^{\top}$, use $v^{\top}A=\lambda v^{\top}$ and the normalization $v^{\top}\dot v=0$.

Singular values are just as simple: for a **simple positive singular value** $\sigma_i$ with unit singular vectors $u_i,v_i$, $d\sigma_i=u_i^{\top}(dA)\,v_i$ (**no absolute value** — the function is smooth where $\sigma_i>0$). A useful global special case is the squared Frobenius norm, $d\|A\|_F^2=2\,\mathrm{tr}(A^{\top}dA)$, which needs no SVD at all. Always check the hypotheses: at repeated eigenvalues or singular values the first-order formula may fail or branch — the largest eigenvalue of $A(t)=\mathrm{diag}(t,-t)$ is $|t|$, with a kink at $t=0$, and perturbations of a Jordan block expand eigenvalues in fractional powers $t^{1/m}$ ($m$ the block size). Singular values are always nonnegative, so when $\sigma_i=0$ and the perturbation raises the rank, $\sigma_i(t)$ behaves like $|ct|$ and the formula returns only a one-sided directional derivative.
derivation: 设 $A(t)$ 可微，$\lambda(t)$ 是 $A(t)$ 的一个**单重**特征值（代数重数 1），$v(t)$ 是对应的单位特征向量：$A(t)v(t)=\lambda(t)v(t)$、$v(t)^{\top}v(t)=1$。单重性保证特征值分支与特征向量可选取为可微（Kato 扰动定理）。对恒等式求导：$$\dot A v+A\dot v=\dot\lambda v+\lambda\dot v.$$ 左乘 $v^{\top}$，得 $$v^{\top}\dot A v+v^{\top}A\dot v=\dot\lambda\,v^{\top}v+\lambda\,v^{\top}\dot v.$$ 对称情形 $A=A^{\top}$ 且扰动 $dA=dA^{\top}$ 有 $v^{\top}A=\lambda v^{\top}$，且 $v^{\top}v=1$，故 $\lambda v^{\top}\dot v$ 两项相消，$\dot\lambda=v^{\top}\dot A v$。结论：在对称矩阵空间内 $d\lambda=v^{\top}(dA)v$，其中 $dA$ 对称。

把方向导数写成迹形式：$$\begin{aligned}d\lambda&=v^{\top}(dA)v=\operatorname{tr}(v^{\top}(dA)v)\\&=\operatorname{tr}(vv^{\top}dA)=\operatorname{tr}\big((vv^{\top})^{\top}dA\big).\end{aligned}$$ 与 $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dA)$ 对照，得 $$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial A}=vv^{\top}.$$ 该梯度对称、半正定、秩一、迹为 1，正是向 $v$ 的正交投影；$v\to-v$ 时 $vv^{\top}$ 不变，符合特征值不依赖特征向量符号。条件是实对称、扰动 $dA$ 对称（Hermitian 情形把转置换成共轭转置、用 $v^{*}$）且 $\lambda$ 单重。结论：对称情形特征值梯度是秩一投影。

非对称矩阵需要左右特征向量：右特征向量 $Av=\lambda v$，左特征向量 $w^{\top}A=\lambda w^{\top}$，并取 $\lambda$ 单重。对 $Av=\lambda v$ 求导并左乘 $w^{\top}$：$$w^{\top}\dot A v+w^{\top}A\dot v=\dot\lambda\,w^{\top}v+\lambda\,w^{\top}\dot v.$$ 由 $w^{\top}A=\lambda w^{\top}$，第二项相消，故 $$\dot\lambda=\frac{w^{\top}\dot A v}{w^{\top}v}.$$ 单重性保证 $w^{\top}v\ne0$；公式对 $v$、$w$ 各自的非零伸缩不变。写成微分与梯度：$$\begin{aligned}d\lambda&=\frac{w^{\top}(dA)v}{w^{\top}v},\\ \frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial A}&=\frac{wv^{\top}}{w^{\top}v}.\end{aligned}$$ 条件：$\lambda$ 单重；对称情形 $w=v$ 退化为 $vv^{\top}$。结论：一般矩阵的特征值梯度是秩一但非对称的矩阵。

奇异值：设 $\sigma>0$ 是 $A$ 的单重奇异值，$u,v$ 为单位左、右奇异向量：$$Av=\sigma u,\qquad A^{\top}u=\sigma v,\qquad \|u\|=\|v\|=1.$$ 对第一式求导并左乘 $u^{\top}$：$$u^{\top}\dot A v+u^{\top}A\dot v=\dot\sigma\,u^{\top}u+\sigma\,u^{\top}\dot u.$$ 由 $A^{\top}u=\sigma v$ 得 $u^{\top}A=\sigma v^{\top}$，故 $u^{\top}A\dot v=\sigma v^{\top}\dot v=0$；又 $u^{\top}\dot u=0$（单位向量），所以 $$\dot\sigma=u^{\top}\dot A v,\qquad d\sigma=u^{\top}(dA)v.$$ 与 $d\sigma=\operatorname{tr}((uv^{\top})^{\top}dA)$ 对照得 $\partial\sigma/\partial A=uv^{\top}$。条件是 $\sigma>0$ 且单重（保证 $u,v$ 可微且符号可固定）；$\sigma=0$ 处公式不成立。结论：正奇异值的梯度是 $uv^{\top}$，式中没有绝对值；$uv^{\top}$ 在同时变号 $(u,v)\to(-u,-v)$ 下不变。单独翻转一个奇异向量会改变 $uv^{\top}$ 的符号并破坏奇异向量方程，因此配对奇异向量只有公共符号自由。

条件失效的反例。特征值：$A(t)=\operatorname{diag}(t,-t)$ 的特征值为 $t,-t$，最大特征值 $\lambda_{\max}(t)=|t|$ 在 $t=0$ 有折点，不可微；此时 $t=0$ 处特征值 $0$ 是二重的，单重前提不成立。若 $A(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\t&0\end{pmatrix}$，特征多项式为 $\lambda^{2}-t=0$，特征值 $\pm\sqrt t$（$t\ge0$）在 $0$ 处出现 $t^{1/2}$ 行为，正对应 $t=0$ 处 Jordan 块大小为 2 的分数幂展开。奇异值：$A(t)=\operatorname{diag}(t,0)$ 的奇异值为 $|t|,0$，在 $t=0$ 处 $\sigma_1=\sigma_2=0$ 既为零又二重；$|t|$ 只有单侧导数 $\pm1$，而 $u^{\top}\dot A v=1$ 只对应 $t>0$ 的一侧。结论：重特征值、重奇异值或 $\sigma=0$ 处一阶公式一般不能套用，至少要逐例检查；此时最多谈方向导数或分叉。

谱函数组合：设 $A=A^{\top}$ 的特征值 $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ 单重，$V=[v_1\ \cdots\ v_n]$ 正交，$f(A)=g(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$，$g$ 对称且可微。由 $d\lambda_i=v_i^{\top}dA\,v_i$，$$\begin{aligned}df&=\sum_i\frac{\partial g}{\partial\lambda_i}v_i^{\top}dA\,v_i\\&=\operatorname{tr}\left(\left(\sum_i\frac{\partial g}{\partial\lambda_i}v_iv_i^{\top}\right)^{\top}dA\right),\end{aligned}$$ 故 $$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial f}{\partial A}&=\sum_i\frac{\partial g}{\partial\lambda_i}v_iv_i^{\top}\\&=V\operatorname{diag}(\nabla_\lambda g)V^{\top}.\end{aligned}$$ 例：$g=\sum_i\lambda_i^{2}$ 给出 $2A$；$g=\sum_i\ln\lambda_i$（$A\succ0$）给出 $A^{-1}$。另 $d\|A\|_F^{2}=2\operatorname{tr}(A^{\top}dA)$，梯度 $2A$，完全不需要 SVD。条件是对称扰动下谱单重时逐特征值推导；若特征值重合但 $g$ 对称，谱函数仍可能光滑，需用 Daleckii–Krein 或矩阵函数理论，不能硬套单个 $\lambda_i$ 的导数。结论：谱函数梯度按特征投影加权；单个特征值公式在单重时保证可用，重根处一般失效，不能硬套。
derivationEn: Let $A(t)$ be differentiable and let $\lambda(t)$ be a **simple** eigenvalue (algebraic multiplicity one) with unit eigenvector $v(t)$: $A(t)v(t)=\lambda(t)v(t)$ and $v(t)^{\top}v(t)=1$. Simplicity guarantees that the eigenvalue branch and the eigenvector can be chosen differentiable (Kato perturbation theory). Differentiating the identity gives $$\dot A v+A\dot v=\dot\lambda v+\lambda\dot v.$$ Multiplying on the left by $v^{\top}$, $$v^{\top}\dot A v+v^{\top}A\dot v=\dot\lambda\,v^{\top}v+\lambda\,v^{\top}\dot v.$$ In the symmetric case $A=A^{\top}$ with a symmetric perturbation $dA=dA^{\top}$, $v^{\top}A=\lambda v^{\top}$, and $v^{\top}v=1$, so the two $\lambda v^{\top}\dot v$ terms cancel and $\dot\lambda=v^{\top}\dot A v$. Conclusion: within the symmetric-matrix space, $d\lambda=v^{\top}(dA)v$ with $dA$ symmetric.

Write the directional derivative in trace form: $$\begin{aligned}d\lambda&=v^{\top}(dA)v=\operatorname{tr}(v^{\top}(dA)v)\\&=\operatorname{tr}(vv^{\top}dA)=\operatorname{tr}\big((vv^{\top})^{\top}dA\big).\end{aligned}$$ Comparison with $df=\operatorname{tr}(G^{\top}dA)$ gives $$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial A}=vv^{\top}.$$ This gradient is symmetric, positive semidefinite, rank one and has trace one — the orthogonal projector onto $v$. It is unchanged by $v\to-v$, consistent with the eigenvalue being independent of the eigenvector's sign. The hypotheses are real symmetry, a symmetric perturbation $dA$, and simplicity of $\lambda$ (in the Hermitian case replace transposes by conjugate transposes and use $v^{*}$). Conclusion: for a symmetric matrix the eigenvalue gradient is a rank-one projector.

A non-symmetric matrix requires left and right eigenvectors: $Av=\lambda v$ and $w^{\top}A=\lambda w^{\top}$, with $\lambda$ simple. Differentiate $Av=\lambda v$ and multiply on the left by $w^{\top}$: $$w^{\top}\dot A v+w^{\top}A\dot v=\dot\lambda\,w^{\top}v+\lambda\,w^{\top}\dot v.$$ Since $w^{\top}A=\lambda w^{\top}$, the second terms cancel, hence $$\dot\lambda=\frac{w^{\top}\dot A v}{w^{\top}v}.$$ Simplicity guarantees $w^{\top}v\ne0$, and the formula is invariant under separate nonzero rescalings of $v$ and $w$. In differential and gradient form, $$\begin{aligned}d\lambda&=\frac{w^{\top}(dA)v}{w^{\top}v},\\ \frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial A}&=\frac{wv^{\top}}{w^{\top}v}.\end{aligned}$$ The hypothesis is simplicity of $\lambda$; in the symmetric case $w=v$ and this reduces to $vv^{\top}$. Conclusion: for a general matrix the eigenvalue gradient is rank one but non-symmetric.

Singular values: let $\sigma>0$ be a simple singular value of $A$, with unit left and right singular vectors $u,v$: $$Av=\sigma u,\qquad A^{\top}u=\sigma v,\qquad \|u\|=\|v\|=1.$$ Differentiate the first equation and multiply on the left by $u^{\top}$: $$u^{\top}\dot A v+u^{\top}A\dot v=\dot\sigma\,u^{\top}u+\sigma\,u^{\top}\dot u.$$ From $A^{\top}u=\sigma v$ we get $u^{\top}A=\sigma v^{\top}$, so $u^{\top}A\dot v=\sigma v^{\top}\dot v=0$; also $u^{\top}\dot u=0$ because $u$ is a unit vector. Hence $$\dot\sigma=u^{\top}\dot A v,\qquad d\sigma=u^{\top}(dA)v.$$ Comparison with $d\sigma=\operatorname{tr}((uv^{\top})^{\top}dA)$ gives $\partial\sigma/\partial A=uv^{\top}$. The hypotheses are $\sigma>0$ and simplicity (which makes $u,v$ differentiable with fixed signs); the formula fails at $\sigma=0$. Conclusion: the gradient of a positive singular value is $uv^{\top}$, with no absolute value in the formula; $uv^{\top}$ is unchanged under the simultaneous sign flip $(u,v)\to(-u,-v)$. Flipping only one singular vector changes the sign of $uv^{\top}$ and breaks the singular-vector equations, so a paired singular-vector pair has only common sign freedom.

Counterexamples when the hypotheses fail. Eigenvalues: $A(t)=\operatorname{diag}(t,-t)$ has eigenvalues $t,-t$, and its largest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\max}(t)=|t|$ has a kink at $t=0$, so it is not differentiable; at $t=0$ the eigenvalue $0$ is repeated, violating simplicity. For $A(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\t&0\end{pmatrix}$ the characteristic polynomial is $\lambda^{2}-t=0$, so the eigenvalues are $\pm\sqrt t$ for $t\ge0$ and exhibit $t^{1/2}$ behavior at $0$, matching the fractional-power expansion for a Jordan block of size 2 at $t=0$. Singular values: $A(t)=\operatorname{diag}(t,0)$ has singular values $|t|,0$; at $t=0$, $\sigma_1=\sigma_2=0$ is both zero and repeated, $|t|$ has only the one-sided derivatives $\pm1$, and $u^{\top}\dot A v=1$ corresponds only to the side $t>0$. Conclusion: at repeated eigenvalues, repeated singular values or $\sigma=0$, first-order formulas generally cannot be applied without a case-by-case check; at most one speaks of directional derivatives or branching.

Spectral composition: let $A=A^{\top}$ have simple eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$, let $V=[v_1\ \cdots\ v_n]$ be orthogonal, and let $f(A)=g(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ with $g$ symmetric and differentiable. From $d\lambda_i=v_i^{\top}dA\,v_i$, $$\begin{aligned}df&=\sum_i\frac{\partial g}{\partial\lambda_i}v_i^{\top}dA\,v_i\\&=\operatorname{tr}\left(\left(\sum_i\frac{\partial g}{\partial\lambda_i}v_iv_i^{\top}\right)^{\top}dA\right),\end{aligned}$$ hence $$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial f}{\partial A}&=\sum_i\frac{\partial g}{\partial\lambda_i}v_iv_i^{\top}\\&=V\operatorname{diag}(\nabla_\lambda g)V^{\top}.\end{aligned}$$ For example, $g=\sum_i\lambda_i^{2}$ gives $2A$, and $g=\sum_i\ln\lambda_i$ for $A\succ0$ gives $A^{-1}$. Separately, $d\|A\|_F^{2}=2\operatorname{tr}(A^{\top}dA)$ has gradient $2A$ and requires no SVD. The hypothesis is a simple spectrum under symmetric perturbations for the eigenvalue-by-eigenvalue derivation; if eigenvalues coincide but $g$ is symmetric, the spectral function may still be smooth and one needs Daleckii–Krein or matrix-function theory rather than the derivative of an individual $\lambda_i$. Conclusion: spectral gradients weight eigenprojectors; the single-eigenvalue formula is guaranteed under simplicity and generally fails at repeated eigenvalues, so it must not be applied blindly.

formulas.note: 实对称单重特征值（Hermitian 把转置换成共轭转置）：$v_i$ 为单位特征向量，$(dA)$ 夹在中间。梯度是秩一对称矩阵，对 $v_i\to -v_i$ 不变。分母布局自检：$\mathrm{tr}\big((v_i v_i^{\top})^{\top}dA\big)=v_i^{\top}(dA)v_i=d\lambda_i$。
formulas.noteEn: Simple eigenvalue of a real symmetric matrix (Hermitian: replace transposes by conjugate transposes): $v_i$ is a unit eigenvector and $(dA)$ sits in the middle. The gradient is rank one and symmetric, and flipping $v_i\to -v_i$ changes nothing. Denominator-layout check: $\mathrm{tr}\big((v_i v_i^{\top})^{\top}dA\big)=v_i^{\top}(dA)v_i=d\lambda_i$.

formulas.note: 一般（非对称）矩阵：$v_i$ 是右特征向量（$Av_i=\lambda_i v_i$），$w_i$ 是左特征向量（$w_i^{\top}A=\lambda_i w_i^{\top}$）。单重性自动保证 $w_i^{\top}v_i\neq 0$，且公式对 $v_i$、$w_i$ 各自的伸缩不变。对称情形 $w_i=v_i$，退化为上一条公式。
formulas.noteEn: General (non-symmetric) matrix: $v_i$ is a right eigenvector ($Av_i=\lambda_i v_i$) and $w_i$ a left eigenvector ($w_i^{\top}A=\lambda_i w_i^{\top}$). Simplicity guarantees $w_i^{\top}v_i\neq 0$, and the formula is invariant under separate rescalings of $v_i$ and $w_i$. In the symmetric case $w_i=v_i$ and it reduces to the previous formula.

formulas.note: 单重正奇异值：$u_i$、$v_i$ 为单位左右奇异向量（$Av_i=\sigma_i u_i$）。**式子里没有绝对值**，$\sigma_i>0$ 处函数光滑。梯度秩一但一般非对称；由 $\sigma_i(A)=\sigma_i(A^{\top})$ 可知转置后左右奇异向量互换。
formulas.noteEn: For a simple positive singular value, $u_i$ and $v_i$ are unit left and right singular vectors ($Av_i=\sigma_i u_i$). **There is no absolute value in the formula** — the function is smooth where $\sigma_i>0$. The gradient is rank one but generally non-symmetric; the identity $\sigma_i(A)=\sigma_i(A^{\top})$ interchanges left and right singular vectors under transposition.

formulas.note: F 范数平方：直接展开 $d\,\mathrm{tr}(A^{\top}A)$ 即可，完全不需要奇异值或奇异向量（它同时等于 $\sum_i\sigma_i^2$）。
formulas.noteEn: The squared Frobenius norm: expand $d\,\mathrm{tr}(A^{\top}A)$ directly; no singular values or vectors are involved (it also equals $\sum_i\sigma_i^2$).

formulas.note: 对称矩阵的谱函数组合规则（$V$ 的列为 $v_i$，是正交矩阵）：把每个 $\lambda_i$ 的秩一梯度按 $\partial g/\partial\lambda_i$ 加权。例：$g=\sum_i\lambda_i^2$ 给出 $2A$（与上一条一致）；$g=\sum_i\ln\lambda_i$（$A$ 正定）给出 $A^{-1}$。适用于 $g$ 关于特征值对称、或谱在考虑范围内不交叉的情形。
formulas.noteEn: Composition rule for spectral functions of a symmetric matrix (the columns of $V$ are the $v_i$; $V$ is orthogonal): weight the rank-one gradient of each $\lambda_i$ by $\partial g/\partial\lambda_i$. For example $g=\sum_i\lambda_i^2$ gives $2A$ (matching the previous formula), and $g=\sum_i\ln\lambda_i$ for positive definite $A$ gives $A^{-1}$. It applies when $g$ is a symmetric function of the eigenvalues, or when the spectrum stays ordered without crossings.

properties: 前提是「单重 + 扰动可微」：重特征值处 $\lambda_i(A)$ 一般不可微甚至分叉（$A(t)=\mathrm{diag}(t,-t)$ 的最大特征值为 $|t|$；Jordan 块的扰动展开含 $t^{1/m}$）；奇异值恒非负，$\sigma_i=0$ 且秩提升时 $\sigma_i(t)$ 形如 $|ct|$，公式只能给单侧方向导数。
公式本质是方向导数：$\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{t=0}\lambda_i(A+tB)=v_i^{\top}Bv_i$（对称情形），对 $dA$ 线性；逐元素取 $dA=E_{jk}$ 就能组装出 $\partial\lambda_i/\partial A$ 的每个分量。
对称情形的梯度 $v_i v_i^{\top}$ 对称、半正定、秩一、迹为 1（即向 $v_i$ 的正交投影矩阵）；奇异值梯度 $u_i v_i^{\top}$ 一般非对称。配对奇异向量只有公共符号自由：$(u_i,v_i)\to(-u_i,-v_i)$ 时 $u_i v_i^{\top}$ 不变；单独翻转一个会改变符号并破坏奇异向量方程。
单个 $\lambda_i$ 不可微并不代表一切失效：关于特征值的对称函数（$\det$、$\mathrm{tr}$、$\|A\|_F^2$ 等）仍可对 $A$ 光滑求导，此时应使用谱函数组合规则，而不是硬套单个特征值的公式。
propertiesEn: The hypotheses are simple eigenvalue plus differentiable perturbation: at repeated eigenvalues $\lambda_i(A)$ is generally non-differentiable or branches (the largest eigenvalue of $A(t)=\mathrm{diag}(t,-t)$ is $|t|$; perturbations of a Jordan block expand in powers $t^{1/m}$). Singular values are always nonnegative, so when $\sigma_i=0$ and the perturbation raises the rank, $\sigma_i(t)$ behaves like $|ct|$ and the formula only gives a one-sided directional derivative.

The formulas are directional derivatives in disguise: $\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{t=0}\lambda_i(A+tB)=v_i^{\top}Bv_i$ in the symmetric case, linear in $dA$; testing $dA=E_{jk}$ entry by entry assembles every component of $\partial\lambda_i/\partial A$.

In the symmetric case the gradient $v_i v_i^{\top}$ is symmetric, positive semidefinite, rank one, with trace 1 (the orthogonal projector onto $v_i$); the singular-value gradient $u_i v_i^{\top}$ is generally non-symmetric. A paired singular-vector pair has only common sign freedom: $(u_i,v_i)\to(-u_i,-v_i)$ leaves $u_i v_i^{\top}$ unchanged, while flipping only one vector changes its sign and breaks the singular-vector equations.

Nondifferentiability of an individual $\lambda_i$ does not break everything: symmetric functions of the eigenvalues ($\det$, $\mathrm{tr}$, $\|A\|_F^2$, and so on) may still be smooth in $A$, and then one should use the spectral composition rule instead of the single-eigenvalue formula.

examples.problem: 设 $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$、$B=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&-1\end{pmatrix}$，考虑 $A(t)=A+tB$。用公式求 $t=0$ 处的 $\frac{d\lambda_1}{dt}$、$\frac{d\lambda_2}{dt}$，并用有限差分（$t=10^{-3}$）验证。
examples.solution: $A$ 的特征值为 $\lambda_1=3$、$\lambda_2=1$，均为单重，对应单位特征向量 $v_1=(1,1)^{\top}/\sqrt2$、$v_2=(1,-1)^{\top}/\sqrt2$。由 $d\lambda_i=v_i^{\top}Bv_i$：$Bv_1=(3,1)^{\top}/\sqrt2$，得 $v_1^{\top}Bv_1=\frac{1+3}{2}=2$；$Bv_2=(-1,3)^{\top}/\sqrt2$，得 $v_2^{\top}Bv_2=\frac{-1-3}{2}=-2$。直接验算：$A(t)=\begin{pmatrix}2+t&1+2t\\1+2t&2-t\end{pmatrix}$，特征方程化为 $(2-\lambda)^2=1+4t+5t^2$，即 $\lambda=2\pm\sqrt{1+4t+5t^2}$，故 $\frac{d\lambda_1}{dt}\big|_0=2$、$\frac{d\lambda_2}{dt}\big|_0=-2$，与公式一致。有限差分（$t=10^{-3}$，$\sqrt{1.004005}\approx1.0020005$）：$\frac{\lambda_1(t)-3}{t}\approx2.0005$，$\frac{\lambda_2(t)-1}{t}\approx-2.0005$，误差 $O(t)$ 随 $t$ 减小而消失。

examples.problem: 设 $A=\mathrm{diag}(3,1)$、$B=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$，$A(t)=A+tB$。用奇异值公式求 $t=0$ 处的 $\frac{d\sigma_1}{dt}$、$\frac{d\sigma_2}{dt}$，并用有限差分（$t=10^{-3}$）验证。
examples.solution: $t=0$ 时 $A$ 的奇异值为 $\sigma_1=3$、$\sigma_2=1$，都单重且为正，左右奇异向量可取 $u_i=v_i=e_i$。由 $d\sigma_i=u_i^{\top}Bv_i$：$\frac{d\sigma_1}{dt}=B_{11}=2$，$\frac{d\sigma_2}{dt}=B_{22}=3$。直接验算：$M(t)=(A+tB)^{\top}(A+tB)=\begin{pmatrix}9+12t+5t^2&4t+5t^2\\4t+5t^2&1+6t+10t^2\end{pmatrix}$，由 $\mathrm{tr}\,M=10+18t+15t^2$ 与 $\det M=9+66t+151t^2$ 逐阶定出特征值 $\lambda_1=9+12t+7t^2+O(t^3)$、$\lambda_2=1+6t+8t^2+O(t^3)$，开方得 $\sigma_1=3+2t+O(t^2)$、$\sigma_2=1+3t+O(t^2)$，与公式吻合。有限差分：$t=10^{-3}$ 时 $\frac{\sigma_1(t)-3}{t}\approx2.0005$、$\frac{\sigma_2(t)-1}{t}\approx2.9995$。

matrix-function-derivatives.definition:
本节点沿用全批统一约定（标量导数按**分母/梯度布局**），$\partial f/\partial X$ 与 $X$ 同型，恒有 $df=\mathrm{tr}\big((\partial f/\partial X)^{\top}dX\big)$；其他布局文献的公式需先对齐约定（标量公式常与本批互为转置）。

矩阵函数 $f(X)$ 的求导比标量情形复杂，根源只有一条：$X$ 与 $\dot X$（或扰动 $E$）一般**不交换**。对指数函数，最有用的一般公式是 $\frac{d}{dt}e^{X(t)}=\int_0^1 e^{sX}\,\dot X\,e^{(1-s)X}\,ds$——它对任意可微的 $X(t)$ 都成立，不需要任何交换性；只有当 $X$ 与 $\dot X$ 可交换时，被积函数才与 $s$ 无关，积分退化为 $\dot Xe^{X}=e^{X}\dot X$。常见的误写 $de^{X}=e^{X}dX$ 只属于这一特例。这个积分同时也是 $e^{X}$ 的 Fréchet 导数 $L_{\exp}(X,E)$：它关于 $E$ 线性，是 $e^{X+E}$ 对 $E$ 的最佳线性逼近，方向导数即 $\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}e^{X+tE}=L_{\exp}(X,E)$。

逆矩阵沿可逆路径的导数由 $XX^{-1}=I$ 两端求导直接得到：$\frac{d}{dt}X^{-1}=-X^{-1}\dot XX^{-1}$，与标量 $(1/x)'=-x'/x^2$ 及一般微分法则一致。对 logm 与 sqrtm，一般情形的 Fréchet 导数仍由 Daleckii-Krein 型积分给出，例如 $d\log X=\int_0^1(sX+(1-s)I)^{-1}(dX)(sX+(1-s)I)^{-1}ds$（要求谱落在定义域内）；只有当 $X$ 与 $dX$ 可交换时，才会简化为熟悉的 $d\log X=X^{-1}dX$ 与 $d\sqrt X=\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}dX$。判断任何简化能否成立的唯一标准永远是「$X$ 与 $dX$（或 $\dot X$）是否交换」。
matrix-function-derivatives.definitionEn:
This node follows the batch-wide convention: **denominator (gradient) layout for scalar derivatives**, so $\partial f/\partial X$ has the same shape as $X$ and always $df=\mathrm{tr}\big((\partial f/\partial X)^{\top}dX\big)$; formulas from sources using a different layout are stated transposed (scalar formulas especially), so align the convention first.

Differentiating a matrix function $f(X)$ is harder than the scalar case for exactly one reason: $X$ and $\dot X$ (or a perturbation $E$) generally do **not commute**. For the exponential the general formula is $\frac{d}{dt}e^{X(t)}=\int_0^1 e^{sX}\,\dot X\,e^{(1-s)X}\,ds$, valid for every differentiable $X(t)$ with no commutativity assumption; only when $X$ commutes with $\dot X$ does the integrand become independent of $s$ and the integral collapse to $\dot Xe^{X}=e^{X}\dot X$. The familiar shorthand $de^{X}=e^{X}dX$ is valid only in that special case. The same integral is the Frechet derivative $L_{\exp}(X,E)$ of the exponential: it is linear in $E$ and is the best linear approximation to $e^{X+E}$, with directional derivative $\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}e^{X+tE}=L_{\exp}(X,E)$.

The derivative of the inverse along an invertible path follows from differentiating $XX^{-1}=I$: $\frac{d}{dt}X^{-1}=-X^{-1}\dot XX^{-1}$, consistent with the scalar rule $(1/x)'=-x'/x^2$ and with the general differential rules. For logm and sqrtm, the general Frechet derivative is again given by a Daleckii-Krein type integral, for example $d\log X=\int_0^1(sX+(1-s)I)^{-1}(dX)(sX+(1-s)I)^{-1}ds$ (spectrum inside the domain); it simplifies to the familiar $d\log X=X^{-1}dX$ and $d\sqrt X=\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}dX$ only when $X$ and $dX$ commute. The only test for whether any simplification is legitimate is always: do $X$ and $dX$ (or $\dot X$) commute?
derivation: 先看幂：对可微的 $X(t)$，由乘积法则归纳得 $$d(X^{k})=\sum_{a=0}^{k-1}X^{a}(dX)X^{k-1-a}\qquad(k\ge1).$$ 例如 $d(X^{2})=(dX)X+X(dX)$，一般不等于 $2X\,dX$。当 $X\,dX=dX\,X$ 时，各项相同，公式化为 $d(X^{k})=kX^{k-1}dX$；不交换时不能这样化简。条件是 $X(t)$ 可微、幂有定义；不需要 $X$ 可逆。结论：非交换性是矩阵函数求导与标量求导的根本差异，任何简化前先检查 $X$ 与 $dX$ 是否交换。

矩阵指数由幂级数定义：$e^{X}=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}X^{k}/k!$，在紧集上一致收敛，可逐项微分。于是 $$d e^{X}=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k!}\sum_{a+b=k-1}X^{a}(dX)X^{b}.$$ 将其与积分 $$L_{\exp}(X,dX)=\int_0^1 e^{sX}(dX)e^{(1-s)X}\,ds$$ 比较：展开两个指数后，$X^{a}(dX)X^{b}$ 的系数是 $$\frac{1}{a!b!}\int_0^1s^{a}(1-s)^{b}ds=\frac{1}{(a+b+1)!},$$ 正好等于幂级数求导中的系数。故对任意可微 $X(t)$，$$d e^{X}=\int_0^1e^{sX}(dX)e^{(1-s)X}\,ds,$$ 无需交换性。结论：这是 $e^{X}$ 的 Fréchet 导数 $L_{\exp}(X,\cdot)$，对扰动线性。

可交换特例：若 $X\,dX=dX\,X$，则 $e^{sX}$、$e^{(1-s)X}$ 都与 $dX$ 交换，且乘积为 $e^{X}$，被积函数与 $s$ 无关，积分化为 $$d e^{X}=e^{X}dX=dX\,e^{X}.$$ 特别地取 $X=tA$、$dX=A\,dt$，因 $A$ 与 $e^{tA}$ 恒交换，得 $$\frac{d}{dt}e^{tA}=A\,e^{tA}=e^{tA}A,\qquad \frac{d^{k}}{dt^{k}}e^{tA}=A^{k}e^{tA}.$$ 这也说明 $e^{tA}$ 是线性 ODE $Y'=AY$、$Y(0)=I$ 的解，$A$ 是生成元。条件：$X$ 与 $dX$ 交换；$X=tA$ 自动满足。结论：常见的 $de^{X}=e^{X}dX$ 是可交换特例下的化简，不能当作通式。

逆矩阵：设 $X(t)$ 在讨论点可逆。对 $XX^{-1}=I$ 求导，$$\dot X X^{-1}+X\frac{d}{dt}X^{-1}=0,$$ 故 $$\frac{d}{dt}X^{-1}=-X^{-1}\dot X X^{-1},\qquad d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}.$$ 可逆性在一点成立时由连续性在邻域保持，所以路径导数有意义；公式对每个可逆点逐点成立。它与标量 $(1/x)'=-x'/x^{2}$ 相容，但矩阵情形必须保留两侧的 $X^{-1}$，不能写成 $-X^{-2}dX$。结论：求逆的 Fréchet 导数由这个三因子夹心公式给出，顺序不可换。

对数与平方根。对谱在 $\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]$ 内的 $X$，$\log X$ 的 Fréchet 导数为 $$d\log X=\int_0^1(sX+(1-s)I)^{-1}(dX)(sX+(1-s)I)^{-1}\,ds.$$ 对平方根，$d\sqrt X$ 是 Sylvester 方程 $$(d\sqrt X)\sqrt X+\sqrt X(d\sqrt X)=dX$$ 的唯一解；当 $\sqrt X$ 与 $-\sqrt X$ 的谱不相交（实对称正定时自动成立）时解唯一。若 $X$ 与 $dX$ 交换，这两式分别简化为 $$d\log X=X^{-1}dX,\qquad d\sqrt X=\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}dX.$$ 条件是谱落在函数定义域内、导数存在；实对称正定时 $\log$ 与 $\sqrt{}$ 都可微。结论：一般情形必须用积分或 Sylvester 方程；在可交换情形下可化简为普通的左乘 $X^{-1}$ 或 $\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}$。

迹与行列式的例外。对任意可微的 $X(t)$，由积分公式和迹的循环性，$$\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dt}\operatorname{tr}e^{X}&=\operatorname{tr}\left(\int_0^1e^{sX}\dot Xe^{(1-s)X}ds\right)\\&=\operatorname{tr}(e^{X}\dot X),\end{aligned}$$ 即 $d\operatorname{tr}e^{X}=\operatorname{tr}(e^{X}dX)$；按分母布局，梯度为 $(e^{X})^{\top}$。对可逆 $X$，Jacobi 公式给出 $$d\det X=\det(X)\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX),$$ 与矩阵函数是否可交换无关，只要求 $X$ 可逆。条件是 $X$ 可微；行列式公式额外要求可逆。结论：非交换性使 $de^{X}$ 变复杂，但迹与行列式仍保持简洁，可作为检验一般公式的基准。
derivationEn: Start with powers: for differentiable $X(t)$, induction on the product rule gives $$d(X^{k})=\sum_{a=0}^{k-1}X^{a}(dX)X^{k-1-a}\qquad(k\ge1).$$ For example, $d(X^{2})=(dX)X+X(dX)$, which is not $2X\,dX$ in general. When $X\,dX=dX\,X$, all terms coincide and the formula collapses to $d(X^{k})=kX^{k-1}dX$; without commutativity this simplification is invalid. The hypotheses are differentiability of $X(t)$ and defined powers; invertibility of $X$ is not required. Conclusion: noncommutativity is the fundamental difference from scalar calculus, and every simplification must be preceded by a check whether $X$ and $dX$ commute.

The matrix exponential is defined by the power series $e^{X}=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}X^{k}/k!$, which converges uniformly on compact sets and may be differentiated termwise. Hence $$d e^{X}=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k!}\sum_{a+b=k-1}X^{a}(dX)X^{b}.$$ Compare this with the integral $$L_{\exp}(X,dX)=\int_0^1 e^{sX}(dX)e^{(1-s)X}\,ds.$$ Expanding the two exponentials, the coefficient of $X^{a}(dX)X^{b}$ is $$\frac{1}{a!b!}\int_0^1s^{a}(1-s)^{b}ds=\frac{1}{(a+b+1)!},$$ exactly the coefficient in the differentiated series. Therefore, for every differentiable $X(t)$, $$d e^{X}=\int_0^1e^{sX}(dX)e^{(1-s)X}\,ds,$$ with no commutativity assumption. Conclusion: this is the Fréchet derivative $L_{\exp}(X,\cdot)$ of $e^{X}$, linear in the perturbation.

Commuting special case: if $X\,dX=dX\,X$, then $e^{sX}$ and $e^{(1-s)X}$ commute with $dX$, their product is $e^{X}$, and the integrand is independent of $s$; the integral becomes $$d e^{X}=e^{X}dX=dX\,e^{X}.$$ In particular, take $X=tA$ and $dX=A\,dt$; since $A$ always commutes with $e^{tA}$, $$\frac{d}{dt}e^{tA}=A\,e^{tA}=e^{tA}A,\qquad \frac{d^{k}}{dt^{k}}e^{tA}=A^{k}e^{tA}.$$ This also shows that $e^{tA}$ solves the linear ODE $Y'=AY$, $Y(0)=I$, with generator $A$. The hypothesis is that $X$ and $dX$ commute; $X=tA$ satisfies it automatically. Conclusion: the familiar $de^{X}=e^{X}dX$ is a simplification available in the commuting special case, not a general formula.

Inverse: let $X(t)$ be invertible at the point under discussion. Differentiating $XX^{-1}=I$ gives $$\dot X X^{-1}+X\frac{d}{dt}X^{-1}=0,$$ hence $$\frac{d}{dt}X^{-1}=-X^{-1}\dot X X^{-1},\qquad d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}.$$ Invertibility at one point persists in a neighborhood by continuity, so the path derivative is meaningful; the formula holds pointwise at every invertible point. It is consistent with the scalar rule $(1/x)'=-x'/x^{2}$, but in the matrix case both factors $X^{-1}$ must be kept and the result cannot be written as $-X^{-2}dX$. Conclusion: the Fréchet derivative of the inverse is given by this three-factor sandwich, and the order cannot be changed.

Logarithm and square root. For $X$ with spectrum in $\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]$, the Fréchet derivative of $\log X$ is $$d\log X=\int_0^1(sX+(1-s)I)^{-1}(dX)(sX+(1-s)I)^{-1}\,ds.$$ For the square root, $d\sqrt X$ is the unique solution of the Sylvester equation $$(d\sqrt X)\sqrt X+\sqrt X(d\sqrt X)=dX,$$ with uniqueness guaranteed when the spectra of $\sqrt X$ and $-\sqrt X$ are disjoint (automatic for real symmetric positive definite $X$). If $X$ and $dX$ commute, these formulas simplify to $$d\log X=X^{-1}dX,\qquad d\sqrt X=\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}dX.$$ The hypotheses are that the spectrum lies in the domain of the function and the derivative exists; for real symmetric positive definite $X$, both $\log$ and $\sqrt{}$ are differentiable. Conclusion: the general case requires the integral or the Sylvester equation; in the commuting case the formulas reduce to left multiplication by $X^{-1}$ or $\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}$.

The trace and determinant are exceptional. For every differentiable $X(t)$, the integral formula and cyclicity of the trace give $$\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dt}\operatorname{tr}e^{X}&=\operatorname{tr}\left(\int_0^1e^{sX}\dot Xe^{(1-s)X}ds\right)\\&=\operatorname{tr}(e^{X}\dot X),\end{aligned}$$ that is, $d\operatorname{tr}e^{X}=\operatorname{tr}(e^{X}dX)$; in the denominator layout the gradient is $(e^{X})^{\top}$. For invertible $X$, Jacobi's formula gives $$d\det X=\det(X)\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}dX),$$ independently of commutativity, requiring only invertibility. The hypothesis is differentiability of $X$; the determinant formula additionally requires invertibility. Conclusion: noncommutativity complicates $de^{X}$, but the trace and determinant remain simple and serve as benchmarks for general formulas.

formulas.note: 单参数线性情形：$tA$ 与 $A$ 永远交换，两式同时成立；$e^{tA}$ 是线性 ODE $Y'=AY$、$Y(0)=I$ 的解，所以这也说明：生成元 $A$ 恰是解在 $t=0$ 处的导数。高阶导数只需把 $A$ 的幂乘在最左（或最右）。
formulas.noteEn: Single-parameter linear case: $tA$ always commutes with $A$, so both orderings hold; $e^{tA}$ solves the linear ODE $Y'=AY$, $Y(0)=I$, so the generator $A$ is exactly the derivative of the solution at $t=0$. Higher derivatives just multiply more copies of $A$ on the left (or right).

formulas.note: 一般公式：对任意可微矩阵 $X(t)$ 成立，**无需交换性**；被积函数在代换 $s\to1-s$ 下形式不变（$\int_0^1e^{sX}\dot Xe^{(1-s)X}ds=\int_0^1e^{(1-s)X}\dot Xe^{sX}ds$）。$X$ 与 $\dot X$ 可交换时化简为 $\dot Xe^{X}$；不能用 $e^{X}\dot X$ 顶替一般情形。
formulas.noteEn: The general formula, valid for every differentiable matrix $X(t)$ with **no commutativity assumption**; the integrand is preserved in form by the substitution $s\to1-s$ ($\int_0^1e^{sX}\dot Xe^{(1-s)X}ds=\int_0^1e^{(1-s)X}\dot Xe^{sX}ds$). It collapses to $\dot Xe^{X}$ when $X$ and $\dot X$ commute; one must not replace it by $e^{X}\dot X$ in general.

formulas.note: Fréchet 导数：$L_{\exp}(X,E)$ 关于 $E$ 线性连续，是 $e^{X}$ 在 $X$ 处的最佳线性逼近，方向导数为 $\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}e^{X+tE}=L_{\exp}(X,E)$。可交换时 $L_{\exp}(X,E)=e^{X}E=Ee^{X}$。
formulas.noteEn: Frechet derivative: $L_{\exp}(X,E)$ is linear and continuous in $E$ and is the best linear approximation to $e^{X}$ at $X$, with directional derivative $\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{0}e^{X+tE}=L_{\exp}(X,E)$. When $X$ and $E$ commute, $L_{\exp}(X,E)=e^{X}E=Ee^{X}$.

formulas.latex: X\dot X=\dot X X\ \Longrightarrow\ \frac{d}{dt}e^{X(t)}=\dot Xe^{X}=e^{X}\dot X
formulas.note: 可交换特例：涵盖 $X(t)=tA$ 与 $X(t)=f(t)Y$（$f$ 为标量、$Y$ 固定）等常见路径，此时矩阵指数像标量公式一样工作。不满足交换时一律回到积分公式。
formulas.noteEn: The commuting special case: it covers paths such as $X(t)=tA$ or $X(t)=f(t)Y$ with scalar $f$ and fixed $Y$, where the matrix exponential behaves like the scalar formula. Outside this case, always fall back to the integral formula.

formulas.note: 可逆路径的求逆导数（逐点恒等式，与微分形式 $d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}$ 一致）；配合乘积法则可对整数幂归纳出 $d(X^k)=\sum_{a+b=k-1}X^a(dX)X^b$。可交换情形另有 $d\log X=X^{-1}dX$、$d\sqrt X=\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}dX$。
formulas.noteEn: Derivative of the inverse along an invertible path (a pointwise identity, matching the differential form $d(X^{-1})=-X^{-1}(dX)X^{-1}$); together with the product rule it gives $d(X^k)=\sum_{a+b=k-1}X^a(dX)X^b$ for integer powers by induction. In the commuting case one also has $d\log X=X^{-1}dX$ and $d\sqrt X=\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}dX$.

properties: $e^{tA}$ 满足线性 ODE $Y'=AY$、$Y(0)=I$；$A$ 与 $e^{tA}$ 恒交换（$e^{tA}$ 是 $A$ 的幂级数），因此左右两种写法一致，高阶导数只需累乘 $A$ 的幂。
交换性是唯一的「隐藏开关」：$X\dot X=\dot X X$ 时一切像标量微积分一样工作；否则积分公式中 $e^{sX}$ 与 $e^{(1-s)X}$ 的位置不能动。非交换时 $\dot Xe^{X}$、$e^{X}\dot X$ 都与真导数无关（见例题）。
迹与行列式例外地简单：对任意可微的 $X(t)$ 都有 $\frac{d}{dt}\mathrm{tr}\,e^{X}=\mathrm{tr}(e^{X}\dot X)$（迹的循环性让积分坍缩）；与之配套的 Jacobi 公式在 $X$ 可逆时给出 $d\det X=\det(X)\,\mathrm{tr}(X^{-1}dX)$。

logm 与 sqrtm 的可微性依赖谱条件：log 要求谱在 $\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]$ 内（实对称情形即正定），平方根要求谱避开负实轴 $( -\infty,0]$；可交换时 $d\log X=X^{-1}dX$、$d\sqrt X=\frac12(\sqrt X)^{-1}dX$，一般情形由 Daleckii-Krein 型积分（谱上的分差或围道积分）给出。
propertiesEn: $e^{tA}$ satisfies the linear ODE $Y'=AY$, $Y(0)=I$; $A$ commutes with $e^{tA}$ always (it is a power series in $A$), so both orderings agree and higher derivatives just accumulate powers of $A$.

Commutativity is the only hidden switch: when $X\dot X=\dot X X$ everything works like scalar calculus; otherwise the positions of $e^{sX}$ and $e^{(1-s)X}$ in the integral are immovable. When the matrices do not commute, both $\dot Xe^{X}$ and $e^{X}\dot X$ are unrelated to the true derivative (see the example).

The trace and the determinant are exceptional: for every differentiable $X(t)$, $\frac{d}{dt}\mathrm{tr}\,e^{X}=\mathrm{tr}(e^{X}\dot X)$, because cyclicity of the trace collapses the integral; the companion Jacobi formula gives $d\det X=\det(X)\,\mathrm{tr}(X^{-1}dX)$ whenever $X$ is invertible.
